# Modified HasteBoots proof implementation

The target is complete protocol 12, schedule 5, non-hiding Brakedown, Goldilocks
first and BabyBear second. Preserve native degree 1024, LWE dimension 728,
public evaluation keys and output keys. The final target is application
soundness/knowledge and 128-bit expected work per false acceptance in an
explicit classical ideal-oracle model. Encryption privacy and zero knowledge
are separate claims.

The current arithmetic target is `CanonicalPBS` with `CanonicalKeySwitch`.
The earlier frozen `NativePBS`/`NativeKeySwitch` references use subtraction of
positive-mask digit products. Native code instead decomposes the canonical
negative mask and adds the products; these operations differ for general key
rows. Earlier claims that those old evaluators already matched native key
switching are superseded by the correction documented at the end of this file.
The old modules remain retained-source artifacts, not the corrected target.

## Source wrapper reborrow, call and normal-return cleanup

The getter profile now validates the fixture wrapper's complete statement tree,
including the shared reborrow's pointee/metadata, local scopes, moved argument,
callee/region/destination, unwind continuation, normal cleanup and return.
The generated wrapper executes typed initialization, prefix locals, an actual
checked storage reborrow, the argument move, the previously proved source getter
and its result write/return. No existing library/interpreter operation is changed.

Thirty-eight additional source theorems cover wrapper execution and its explicit
normal-return scope cleanup. Snapshot execution supplies both read permission and
the complete live 16-byte extent. These derive reborrow success and getter success;
the complete snapshot/wrapper theorem assumes neither as a separate premise.
Cleanup ends exactly the fresh child loan and restores the incoming lease list.
It retains the executed reads, advanced tag counter, reference-register history
and birth record. Operational projection, reachability, well-formedness and heap
preservation hold through the wrapper, including rejected/partial executions.

Twenty additional examples exercise overflow padding, allocation errors, copied
results, child revocation, parent usability, tag/birth history, invalid inputs and
failed getter reads retaining their prefix. The source gate passes 632 dependency
audits, 55 rejecting controls and 30 examples in total. Related gates pass:
constructor 945 audits/165 controls, Vec destruction 1044/87, allocator caller
388/31 and empty constructor 395/17. Shared library/root-test/
toolchain/dependency/full-check inputs remain unchanged; the preceding successful
11101-job full project check is reused.

Normal-return cleanup is explicit model composition for this non-unit result;
it is not a new native lifetime theorem or a change to generic unit settlement.
The getter's reference-materialization boundary remains explicit. The original
constructor error handler, native ABI/stack/type/compiler/lifetime correspondence,
physical reclamation, resident destruction, physical work and final security
remain open.

## Transparent source getter agrees after reference materialization

The new `interop/aeneas/reservation-error-kind` profile includes
`alloc::collections` and retains the transparent original getter, its safe
fixture wrapper and five relevant types. The reifier resolves declarations by
identity and validates the complete getter body: shared dereferences, variant
match/fallthrough, Layout copy, temporary moves, retags, aggregate construction,
cleanup and returns. Source type IDs are local to this extraction and are not
silently identified with the constructor profile's IDs.

The emitted getter body executes in the existing aggregate interpreter after an
explicit checked reference-materialization step. Eleven source theorems cover
all valid alignment discriminants, both original branches, their common result,
heap-derived kind validity, equality with the checked getter operation, heap
framing, operational projection, snapshot composition and reachability. No final
getter-result premise is assumed. Ten examples include overflow padding, ordinary
and boundary layouts, actual snapshot/getter runs and rejected operands.

The new source gate passes 577 dependency audits and 39 rejecting controls. Related
gates pass: constructor 945 audits/165 controls, Vec destruction 1044/87,
allocator caller 388/31 and empty constructor 395/17. The
shared library, root tests, toolchain/dependencies and full-check scripts are
unchanged, so the preceding successful 11101-job full check remains applicable.

Equivalence is established at the explicit materialized-reference boundary.
The fixture wrapper's reborrow/call sequence is retained but not executed, and
the original constructor error handler is not yet connected. Native reference
ABI, stack placement, lifetime/compiler correspondence, reclamation, resident
destruction, physical work and final security remain open.

## Snapshot reads and checked kind getter are complete

`NativeReservationErrorRead` separates byte residency from alias permission.
Its `Readable` descriptor includes the selected shared lease, physical extent,
complete base pointer in the register file, raw read permission and stored error
fields. The descriptor is derived from the actual root storage-loan grant after
the snapshot's allocation and byte write; it is not an external certificate.

Fifteen core theorems prove permission for bounded subranges, actual aligned word
access, preservation of readability across the first word read, and complete
error decoding. Overflow reads only the initialized first word; allocation
errors read alignment and size. Every successful typed-local snapshot now has a
successful decoder result without an assumed read-success premise.

The checked `getKind` operation validates a shared two-word operand, resolves its
stable tag through the current reference register file and performs those reads.
It returns the original encoded kind, preserves the heap, and projects to actual
machine steps. A later loan may shift register positions without changing which
error object is read. Seventeen examples cover both variants, tag shifts between
distinct objects, revocation, invalid operands and a failed second read retaining
the first read's effects. Twenty-eight dependency guards cover the new module.
Two source-agreement theorems and two concrete source examples connect constructor
error payloads to this modeled getter after actual snapshot execution. All three
new-module warning-as-error checks pass, and a fresh full `scripts/check`
passes with 11101 build jobs. The constructor gate passes 945 dependency audits,
165 rejecting controls, 130 source examples and 151 model examples. Related
gates pass: Vec destruction 1044 audits/87 controls, allocator caller 388/31
and empty constructor 395/17.

This closes read completeness for successful snapshots, not read completeness
from byte residency alone. It does not establish equivalence to the extracted
Rust getter body, install the operation in the source error handler, or refine
marshaling to native stack placement/borrowing. Source getter/caller execution,
native ABI/type/compiler/lifetime correspondence, storage reclamation, resident
destruction, physical work and final security remain open.

## Typed reservation-error locals marshal into resident storage

`NativeReservationErrorLocal` reads a complete typed LLBC local, decodes its
nominal wrapper/kind/Layout/alignment tags, checks allocation-layout validity,
and marshals the value into modeled 16-byte storage. The actual operations are
allocation, one byte write, and a checked shared storage loan. Overflow writes
only the first eight bytes; allocation errors write alignment then size. The
result is a checked two-word reference operand. Failed operations retain every
machine step already executed.

Twenty-three core theorems prove codec inversion/validity, execution traces,
reachability and well-formedness, recovery of fields from actual byte writes,
and a residency relation tying the returned loan to that same written pointer.
A successful typed-local snapshot establishes that the original complete local
equals the encoded kind and that the selected resident lease contains its fields.
The generic subword proof derives the two aligned word loads from the full byte
write; field equality is not supplied as an assumption.

The reifier emits the descriptor using already validated source identities.
Four source theorems connect both original constructor error payloads to the
codec, including allocation failures for every capacity below `2^63`. Three
source examples exercise overflow, ordinary allocation error and the upper
accepted capacity. Twenty-two model examples cover local round trips, padding,
type/tag/initialization rejection and a genuine executed-prefix failure at the
modeled address boundary. Forty-two dependency guards cover the new module.
All three new-module warning-as-error checks pass. A fresh full `scripts/check`
passes with 11098 build jobs. The constructor gate passes 915 dependency audits,
165 rejecting controls, 128 source examples and 134 model examples. Related
gates pass too: Vec destruction 1044 audits/87 controls, allocator caller
388/31 and empty constructor 395/17.

This marshaling is a representation bridge, not execution of the original
Rust borrow. The new local operation is not yet installed in the source error
handler, and getter execution, read-completeness from residency, native stack
placement/lifetime and storage reclamation remain open. Outer error/unwind
propagation, native ABI/compiler correspondence, resident destruction, physical
work and final security also remain open.

## Storage loans admit uninitialized padding

`NativeByteBorrowStorage.borrow` checks the existing parent/raw permission rules
and `checkRange`, then issues a fresh lease without reading any bytes. A positive
range must lie in a live allocation with the exact stored origin. Alignment,
extent, parent containment and mode restrictions remain checked. The original
initialized-byte borrow operation is unchanged; its successful results refine
the new storage operation exactly.

`NativeStorageBorrowMachine` embeds every original reference-machine operation
unchanged and adds storage borrowing through checked pointer/reference registers.
Its grant executes the new primitive and records the actual fresh tag, parent,
lease and birth. Twenty-nine theorems across both modules prove complete and
successful grants, live allocation coverage, exclusive separation, compatibility
with original grants, well-formedness, heap/incoming-authority preservation,
pointer projection, and borrowing followed by error-field reads. Original runs
embed into extension runs. Reachability in the extension is stated separately;
it is not asserted to be reachability in the original initialized-byte machine.

Twenty-two examples now mint the padded reservation-error loan through actual
operations and read `CapacityOverflow` through it. They prove the resulting
state well formed and the decoder result reachable in the extension. Other
examples reject uninitialized field reads, origin forgery, misalignment, extent
escape, permission upgrades, conflicting root loans, freeing borrowed storage
and ending a parent before its child. Forty-one dependency guards cover the
new declarations and constructors. All four new-module warning-as-error checks
pass, and a fresh full `scripts/check` passes with 11095 build jobs. The
constructor source gate passes 868 dependency audits, 165 rejecting controls,
125 source examples and 112 model examples. Related gates
also pass: Vec destruction 1044 audits/87 controls, allocator caller 388/31
and empty constructor 395/17.

This removes the decoder test's need to assume a resident padded loan. It does
not yet connect an LLBC local to this heap-backed storage, interpret the source
getter through that local, or establish Rust typed-reference validity. Source
local placement/lifetime, native ABI/compiler correspondence, outer error and
unwind propagation, resident storage/destruction, physical work and final
security remain open.

## Reservation-error field decoder and padding boundary

`NativeReservationErrorFields` reads the retained 16-byte reservation-error
representation through checked reference-machine accesses. It reads the word at
offset zero as layout alignment. Zero returns `capacityOverflow` immediately;
only a nonzero alignment causes the size word at offset eight to be read. An
allocation error is returned only when the recovered layout satisfies the
existing 64-bit `Layout.Valid` predicate. Failed reads and invalid layouts retain
the machine steps already executed.

Seventeen theorems establish complete and successful-read characterizations,
observations of the original heap, the overflow branch's lack of a tail read,
heap and incoming-authority preservation, operational projection, reachability
and well-formedness. Twenty-three dependency guards cover the type, constructors,
operations and theorems. Sixteen model examples include both variants, malformed
alignment, excessive size, wrong reference/mutability, alias conflict and an
uninitialized overflow tail. The source reifier now validates the complete
wrapper/niche layouts against the extracted target; eight mutations test those
checks. The source gate passes 827 dependency audits and 165 rejecting
controls, alongside 125 source examples and 90 model examples. A fresh full
`scripts/check` passed with 11091 build jobs. This validates the representation
used by the model, not native ABI or compiler correspondence. Related gates also
pass: Vec destruction 1044 audits/87 controls, allocator caller 388/31 and empty
constructor 395/17.

The padded-tail example explicitly supplies an existing resident loan and makes
no claim to have issued it. A paired test proves that the current full-byte
borrow primitive refuses to issue the 16-byte loan when the tail is uninitialized.
At that stage, the missing step was a checked storage-borrow operation whose
permission and extent checks do not read padding; the extension above now
supplies it. Typed field validity and local storage construction remain open. The transparent source getter and outer error path
still need to be connected to this decoder. Native stack/lifetime correspondence,
resident storage/destruction, physical work and final security remain open.

Constructor errors are interpreted before the outer caller reaches its explicit

variant reconstruction, and supply the nonzero-sized resident local borrow.
This exploratory extraction has no new correctness theorem. Outer unwind
handling, resident storage/destruction, native correspondence, physical work and

The source gate passes 783 dependency audits, 157 rejecting controls and 118

## Register-bound references now use the provenance-aware heap

`NativeReferenceMachine` binds reference operations to reference registers.
Operands select registers rather than supplying ledger tags or reference
records. Checked root borrows and reborrows mint the reference values and record
their birth leases. The ledger is a view of the existing pointer-machine heap,
so byte memory is shared rather than duplicated. Raw pointer reads, writes,
copies and frees check ledger permissions; allocation and pointer-value
construction retain their existing checked semantics.

Tagged accesses select a resident lease, check its mode and bounds, derive the
access pointer with the lease's allocation origin, and check the ledger's
through-access permissions. Byte reads/writes and pointer loads/stores use the
concrete heap and origin metadata. Pointer stores retain data origins; numerical
writes erase them. Scratch-register recovery selects an existing complete
pointer value, never a provenance reconstructed from address bits. Every
resident lease retains its original pointer in the registers, and recovery is
proved available for that pointer.

Forty-one theorems cover exact reference/lease/pointer binding, projection into
the closed pointer machine, heap/ledger well-formedness, causal checked-borrow
birth witnesses, unique minted tags, monotone counters, raw-free conflict
exclusion and permanent revocation. After a reference ends, every later access
selecting that old tag is rejected, even after new borrows. The strongest birth
result starts from a successful program run on the concrete empty state and
exposes the earlier actual checked borrow and an execution suffix reaching the
current state. The pointer-machine projection preserves allocation-origin
authenticity through reference operations.

operation constructors and execution/effect constructors. Thirty-six executable

## Closed pointer programs now have causal allocation-origin authenticity

`NativePointerMachine` restricts pointer construction to nine data-only

layouts and register indices, with no pointer records or allocation identities.
Numerical construction supplies no origin; address replacement preserves the
selected register's origin. The machine has no operation for importing a
caller-supplied origin. Allocation records its checked base/layout and the
allocator's actual generation.

Thirty-five theorems establish heap well-formedness, register/stored-value
origin authenticity and generation bounds through every operation and arbitrary
finite executions. Every history entry has an actual successful allocator step
and an execution suffix reaching the current state. The strongest program
results start from the concrete empty state and expose the underlying successful
byte-heap allocator result for each register or stored pointer origin, with that
causal suffix. These do not assume the authenticity invariant as input.
Allocation generations in reachable histories are pairwise distinct, and the
next allocation generation has not already been issued. Historical origins
remain authentic after free; storage checks still reject stale dereferences.

## Thin pointer bytes and allocation origins now compose

`NativePointerByteMemory` couples the concrete byte heap to finite per-byte
allocation-origin metadata. Thin pointers occupy eight initialized little-endian
bytes with alignment eight; the stored address comes from those bytes and the
origin comes from a uniform metadata span. Null and dangling pointer values can
be stored without dereferencing their targets. Mixed-origin spans are rejected
by this explicit model policy. This is not a general Rust typed-layout or alias
semantics theorem.

Thirty-one theorems establish pointer store/load and copy/load round trips,
checked store availability, heap well-formedness, exact metadata changes on
allocation/free, and stale storage load/store rejection. Copies snapshot both
bytes and metadata before writing, including overlap. Numerical word writes
clear origins even when the stored address bits remain unchanged. Freeing an
allocation removes metadata owned by its storage while retaining dangling
pointer values in other allocations. Load origins must come from existing
metadata cells; copies and numerical writes cannot introduce new origins, and
pointer stores can introduce only the supplied value's origin.

All 44 declarations have persistent dependency audits. Nineteen executable
regressions cover uninitialized storage, actual address bytes, numeric origin
erasure, partial fragments, alignment, overlapping relocation, uninitialized
copies, null values, dangling values, address reuse and storage cleanup. The
model and tests are included in the root aggregates. Full `scripts/check` passes
(10,957 build jobs plus all subsequent audit/smoke commands; log:
`/tmp/hasteboots-pointer-byte-memory-full-check.log`). Production Rust and the
compiler/backend are unchanged.

The subsequent closed machine above proves allocation-origin authenticity
for its register and stored pointer values. The low-level storage API still
accepts supplied pointer values and does not itself authenticate them. Connecting these operations to original native
pointer accesses and lifecycle bodies, borrow identity, compiler/caller/NTT/
SIMD/scheduler coverage, causal lifetime oracle-owner history, BabyBear and the
final expected physical attacker-work inequality all remain open. This is not a
native constructor acceptance or an end-to-end security result.

## Untyped byte copies and finite allocation-origin metadata now check

`NativeRawByteRange` snapshots and replaces actual heap cells, including
uninitialized cells. Positive copies snapshot before writing, so overlapping
copies retain the original source cells. A separate nonoverlapping operation
rejects overlapping spans. Empty copies check alignment without dereferencing
storage. Thirty-one theorems establish exact read-back, initialization-state
preservation, agreement with initialized byte writes, outside-byte framing,
well-formedness and derived availability from checked spans. These are model
operations; native pointer-copy source correspondence and physical costs remain
open. Rust's [copy_nonoverlapping documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/core/ptr/fn.copy_nonoverlapping.html)
specifies untyped copying that preserves initialization state, motivating the
cell representation rather than an initialized-values-only copy.

`NativePointerShadow` provides finite per-byte allocation-origin metadata keyed
by the containing allocation's identity and byte address. Replacement and
snapshot operations support relocation. Integer-byte writes can clear metadata
even when address bits stay unchanged. Eleven theorems establish selected-cell
membership, exact inside replacement, outside framing, snapshot length and
uniform-span behavior. Mixed fragments are rejected by this model's policy;

stored/native registry vectors. Earlier unused aliases remain included when
proving first-original ownership, even if a later batch stops.

`StoredSourceSnapshotBudget` proves a polynomial operation bound for complete

`StoredParentMetadataBudget` derives polynomial replay time from the existing

`GoldBatchQueriesCost` now measures the outer original batch-query vector,

`StoredSourceMentionsCost` now composes **all original direct source formats**:

reading costs at most `113*(N+1)+15`; serialization costs at most `156*T+372`.
The exact logical length, table and repetitions are preserved, with no separate

`StoredCanonicalBindingCost` now reads the complete original canonical binding:

serialization and byte comparison; it equals the original exact binding codec

binding. Its bound is `302*N+1764*(N/128+1)+1100`. Alternate nested count/word/degree
spellings and trailing bytes reject. No functional helper/context/root or serializer

`StoredBindingFramesCost` charges exact binding kind/label checks, complete message

The helper projection equals `ExecutableParentInputView.frameHelper`; under the

Collection from `N` raw bytes costs at most `(4971+6*K)*N+5`, for fixed binding

`StoredSourceVectorReadCost` now measures native context/root source-vector

contexts sharing a root remain distinct; original duplicate pairs remain present.

Byte comparison is executable over stored lists, with proved equality and cost

A successful matching head costs exactly 389, and appending any entries after a

reindexing proof establish equality of the full prepared and function-interface

includes domain generation, decoding, padding removal and rectangular assembly;

extraction and complete-history analysis equalities remain proved. This is an

security theorem. Public-log processing, source reconstruction/materialization,
physical/backend refinement and application security remain required.

The default polynomial division API now uses `DensePolynomialDivision` for its

`DensePolynomialStepCost` now implements measured shifted subtraction and a

Seven runtime regressions cover consecutive division steps, complete cancellation,

`CompactSourceHistory` transports snapshot construction through the changed
request ordering. Checkpoint entries are permuted, while each step still records

extractor and its native expected-work event now run through this compact path.
The reference implementations remain as proof targets.

Stored source/helper metadata entries are bounded by
`H * (4*B^2 + 2*B)`, where H is the number of observations and B their total
input-byte count. `CompactParentWorkStorage` and `CompactSourceHistory` derive
`W * (4*W^2 + 2*W)` from actual closed-interpreter work; work is not defined by
log length. Each stored parent has duplicate-free source/helper lists, and at
most H parent records are retained. These are entry-count bounds, not total
physical memory or running-time bounds.

`SolverOperationCost` now executes deterministic elimination with explicit

and zero dimensions. The rectangular matrix interface now uses this runner via
`solveWithCost`; its charge adds one return step and its result is proved equal
to the previous interface, preserving soundness and completeness.

This is an abstract field/access count, not a complete RAM instruction or
physical-time bound. Evaluating input matrix/rhs functions, constructing their
materialized equations, backend arithmetic costs and later result reads are
excluded. The elimination bound therefore does not price arbitrary callbacks or

Native batch-model accepted-false-analysis-claim coverage now uses the closed

`ClosedByteMachineNativeSoundness` transports arbitrary accepted batch witnesses

The earlier theorem uses the common-source analysis extractor; the executable

The global source/collision event now has an unbounded first-moment work
bound for the closed byte interpreter. `NativeRootFamilyHashStep` combines the
existing posterior checkpoint and cached-hash collision laws under the complete
mixed history. Prior bad states are retained explicitly. Starts and SHAKE reads
preserve the bad-state predicate, and cached hash calls have zero fresh charge.
`ClosedByteMachineRootFailure` derives the conditional and averaged first-new-
failure laws and locates every actual global bad prefix at an earlier actual
hash instruction. No one-observation/one-instruction clock assumption is used.

`ClosedByteMachineRootWork` uses the derived per-hash envelope and an
analysis-only work split. Low-work charges sum against actual instruction
prices; Markov pays the entire large-work branch. With analysis threshold

allowed, and no finite second moment or success floor is assumed.

`ClosedByteMachineGoldAllRisk` unites that global event with the existing
field/column/receipt events on the SAME interpreter execution and proves
measurability and the unconditioned bound
`(2^-159 + 17/2^141 + 2^-255) * expectedWork`. Its coefficient is at most
`18/2^141`. The numerical allowance satisfies
`2^128 * (64 * 4 * coefficient) ≤ 9/16`. This last inequality is arithmetic;
it does not prove how the application consumes a shape/role union, and the
finite factors are not attacker trial or lifetime caps.

Validation: `scripts/check` passed all 10,608 build jobs and its strict

cost separation, randomized initialization, original registry/context ownership,

The actual root/source registry now has a derived per-hash work envelope.

`NativeParentLedgerPools` proves every frozen source belongs to the Cartesian

Early receipt events now have a first-moment work bound on the same closed

`ClosedByteMachineReceiptWork` splits the analysis at an arbitrary positive

by `expectedWork / T`. The native execution has no threshold or lifetime cap,

The combined field/column/receipt lifetime event has coefficient
`17/2^141 + 2^-255`, under the earlier Goldilocks role/constructor premises.
This is an event/work theorem in the declared interpreter units, without a

A closed byte instruction interpreter now supplies explicit local execution
steps. Its finite instruction syntax contains no evaluator or oracle
continuation supplied by an adversary. Register/stack operations, branches,

Reads may obtain their offset and length from earlier response bytes. Halt,
reject, empty-pop failure and out-of-code abort pay for the executed instruction
and then stutter without further work. Initialization charges finite owned code,
private tapes and zeroed registers; immutable public setup is excluded and is
charged when copied. This is a specified byte-work schedule, still requiring a
physical implementation/refinement argument.

`ClosedByteMachine` proves exact per-instruction accounting and its finite
sum, prefix resumption, monotone work, terminal stuttering and replay.
`ClosedByteMachineHistory` locates first exposure by the actual instruction

classifier agrees with each actual interpreter operation and derives the
existing first-read selector at that instruction boundary. The classifier's
`done next` for a local instruction is a single-instruction view, not termination
of the interpreter.

`ClosedByteMachineWork` proves measurability and equality between expected
lifetime work and the supremum of prefix means, retaining incomplete and
infinite tails. `ClosedByteMachineRootLifetime` transports the global
root/source hazard bound to these instruction prefixes with the full causal

`ClosedByteMachineGoldRisk` proves that compatible Goldilocks roles with
`Q ≥ 544` have lifetime field/column exposure-event probability at most
`(17 / 2^141) * expectedWork` for this closed interpreter. The proof sums actual
instruction costs, makes stopped exposure charges zero, and uses the earlier

runtime cap, observation-count cost proxy, completion conditioning or success
floor.

`RectangularPCSParameters` uses proximity `(δ/p)^w` and the maximum of the

Accepted native false claims in a complete causal machine prefix now derive

Physical expected-work coupling, 128-bit calibration, BabyBear instantiation

height lookup from the batch availability path. Each newly resolved complete

Accepted Goldilocks batches now derive their actual context hash, computed raw
requests and positive random-test exposure from the native program. Complete
history reconstruction proves that all 64 heights share one retained log per
frozen key. Under global no-disagreement, every accepted column equals that
immutable raw source and satisfies all response groups. No supplied checkpoint,

boundary. Arbitrary causal prequeries and epilogue calls share the same caches

The availability bound now covers any witnessed accepted native batch in a
complete mixed history, including all such batches in any finite prefix of a
possibly nonterminating causal machine. The global source predicate requires the verifier's actual context-hash result,
rather than an arbitrary tag sharing the root. The context computation is a
recorded native subtrace. Acceptance and context witnesses replay under the
same observations, making both finite and lifetime failure events measurable.
Truthful reconstruction is audited; hash-cache collisions and source-failure
flags persist under later observations. One global lifetime bound uses the
supremum of nondecreasing actual prefix charges, including the causal prelude.
It adds no factor for batches, columns, response groups or prefix count, and
prefix suspension retains the real residual machine state, ledger and caches.
The native framing/message-size domain remains in each acceptance witness.
This is raw-source availability; the supremum has not yet been related to
physical attacker work or the final 128-bit application-security theorem.

The actual deferred dispatcher now supplies receipt acceptance and observation
subtraces to the availability proof, including receipts retained before a later
stopped/rejected batch. Receipt calls retain first-original registry ownership,
original grouped raw queries/values, root and width. The whole registered lookup
connects those owners to its computed original metadata, including earlier
unused aliases. Its frozen-source witness is tagged by that complete original
context/root key; equal digests are not used to infer parameter-object equality.
Whole-lookup source failures now reduce to the shared any-batch event over
finite histories and unbounded causal lifetimes, with measurable events and

receipt. Codeword/application soundness, full exposure lineage, physical work
and implementation refinement are still required.

Deferred receipt framing is now derived by the real transitions instead of
supplied per receipt. Structural transcript framing survives prime collection,
rejection/suspension/resumption, field receipts, checked atomic index sampling,
batch binding/responses, deferred sealing, source-claim insertion and alias
rejection. The dispatcher induction retains framing for earlier accepted
receipts when a later call stops. Its domain bounds the original ordered
group/packet pairs; no future oracle answer chooses a framing certificate.
Source collection carries framing from the helper's actual last-accepted parent
into the deferred handoff. Availability corollaries use that parent and static
encoded claim/binding/response size bounds. Single-opening PCS and the ordered
helper loop now preserve framed ancestry as well, using actual accepted sampler
and PCS transitions. Registered lookup preparation carries that result into
the availability corollary, which can start from the earlier lookup-body parent.
The caller-parent corollary now derives lookup-body framing through original
request preflight, full registry serialization, multiplicity binding, retained
child initialization and successful child finishing. It assumes only the
original caller parent is framed and static native message allocation bounds;
no intermediate future transcript framing certificate is supplied. Strict Rust
decoding/refinement and the remaining security obligations are not discharged
by this invariant.

Caller-domain whole-lookup source failures now have finite-history and unbounded
lifetime bounds with intermediate receipt framing derived from execution. The
failure witnesses carry original caller framing and explicit message allocation
domains, rather than per-receipt framing. Replay retains the same prepared
lookup, source progress, receipt and actual context hash, so the events are
measurable. All witnessed lookups in one shared history reduce to the same
any-batch charge; the lifetime bound adds no lookup, receipt or prefix factor.
Message allocation/refinement, full lineage and attacker-work transfer remain
separate obligations.

Batch response semantics now derive polynomial-code membership for every
computed test lane and every actual response group from successful preparation,
the retained code constructor and its primitive root. The native stride, block
width and Merkle height match that code. Accepted raw-source equations transport
to vector linear checks on one complete frozen context/root word for all lanes
and groups. These deterministic results retain independent test and symbol
widths. They do not supply Fiat–Shamir freshness or the final PCS soundness
probability composition; root-generation and implementation refinement remain
explicit backend obligations.

The native batch now supplies the original typed ordered draw vector to these
checks, with exact quota, order and repetitions. Every draw occurrence has a
computed raw request even though workers transport sorted distinct columns.
Nonempty response groups follow from the actual binding gate. Finite group/lane
indices expose coded responses and shared frozen-word agreement in the form
used by rectangular opening soundness. No freshness, probability bound or
independence between response families is inferred from this transport.

Rectangular finishing/extraction algebra now separates packing width from code
symbol width and truncates decoded padding to the original message length.
The fixed-word interactive kernel allows probabilistic adaptive response state
between the uniform test matrix and shared ordered columns. One query-independent
analysis table supports an any-false-original-query batch bound, without query,
group or lane count factors. Its proximity term is `(distance / field size)^testWidth`.
This is not yet the production Fiat–Shamir theorem: full native probability
composition, freshness/lineage, efficient public extraction and work/refinement
transfer remain required.

Native accepted suffix claims now equal the rectangular finishing of their
actual computed encoded response group. Lane chunks are exactly the original
messages with zero padding, and native query/message counts supply the index
transport. Every original right query is retained even when responses share a
left-prefix group. The right-fold/encoding equation is closed. Native grouped
left weights now also have the ordered tensor semantics, and a single checked
geometry bijection reindexes the native source rows as left cell/source lane.
Every original query's computed structured combination uses those rectangular
weights on that common source, including field-representative aliases. Composing
these deterministic equations with the production transcript probability law
remains open. The native finishing gate is now composed with the interactive
any-false-original-query bound under a uniform matrix and fresh shared draws.

The actual native shared-candidate-budget collector now has a conditional
scaled-uniform field-vector/matrix law on an unread SHAKE tail after any
replayable mixed history. Exact typed-value and full-log projections connect
that law to the native Goldilocks batch's `work.random` array and common row
bijection. The first positive read of the exact challenge input, at any offset,
derives fresh-tail eligibility from the actual history, excluding prior partial
reads. The increasing union of all candidate prefixes is dominated by the
joint uniform law, without a retry cap or division by completion probability.
Global coverage/lineage and the response-bound column challenge law still need
composition with the interactive batch soundness theorem.

Still open: complete first-exposure lineage for orphan/pending/receipt cases,
application soundness and independent public extraction, BabyBear integration,
physical attacker-work accounting and the final 128-bit numerical theorem,
and strict decoder plus Rust/Charon/Aeneas/NTT/SIMD/Div64/scheduler refinement.

Current native integration executes raw Goldilocks lookup retries with an
exact projection to the abstract sampler, then equality preparation, scalar
verification, strict terminal guards, terminal-value binding and child
finishing. The lookup-body entry point is checked against native fixture bytes
in the kernel. Its bound result feeds the PCS continuation. Concrete raw column
authentication and PCS payload codecs are linked to the existing cached
verifier. The completed run now also derives every ordered helper PCS call with no
truncation or extra oracle observation. The ordered helper loop now executes
the checked PCS prefix, raw column workers and computed claim check in one
causal oracle program. The typed Goldilocks continuation now collects source
claims and dispatches sealed native batches. Application/PCS soundness
composition remains open. Base-field challenges, response framing and atomic
index draws now have executable adapters and a joint finite-byte sampling law. The retained
block-code constructor and its complete serialization now supply the same
code object to parameter binding and computed scalar response encoding. See
[the current implementation layer](#shared-native-batch-pcs-execution).
The joint ideal-oracle model also has a proved accumulated SHA-512 collision
bound for causal mixed SHAKE/hash programs, including repeated calls and
inherited bad events. The full application security theorem remains unproved:
full native protocol/PCS composition, work coupling, numerical certification,
strict decoding and checked Rust/scheduler refinement are still required.

ArkLib is a pinned path dependency. Root dependency resolution must retain
`vendor/VCVio`, not materialize a second incompatible oracle framework.
`HasteBootsSmoke` checks unequal matrix splits, a noncommuting matrix example,
zero-round folding and a concrete block-distance specialization.

## Completion ledger

1. Dependency foundation and initial deterministic algebra: implemented and
   compiled. Native field instantiation and encoder/Rust representation refinement
   remain open.
2. Independent NAND/PBS trace relation and native evaluator: public preprocessing
   and binary blind rotation are now modeled independently. Blind-rotation trace
   generation, arithmetic validity, unique output, and zero-round identity are
   proved. One-block key switching, extraction and complete reference trace
   composition are now implemented. `NativePBS.exists_trace_iff` and the public
   extractor's exact failure-measure identity are checked. Native NTT/key-format
   representation linkage and proof-system stage enforcement remain open.
3. Common-source PCS security: deterministic unique common decoding, total fallback

   near/far column losses. Native semantic response assembly and matrix-query

7. Implementation refinement: open. Prove typed Rust acceptance refines the Lean
   model, then specify byte decoding separately. Extraction tools and primitives

Intermediate theorems may expose explicit premises. No final security claim may
silently assume its unresolved PCS, Fiat-Shamir or expected-work conclusion.
The permitted kernel foundations are `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and
`Quot.sound`; headline dependencies must not contain `sorryAx`, custom axioms,
or native-compiler trust.

## Ideal reciprocal rejection loop: operational limiting law and candidate work

`RejectionSampling.runPrefix` implements fresh candidate draws and the real
accept/retry branch over a finite accepted domain. The result retains the
entire ordered candidate list, including rejected candidates. `none` denotes
suspension at the next draw, with all prior work retained; it is not a verifier
rejection or an imposed native retry budget. Every natural prefix length is
an analysis approximation to the same unbounded loop.

For rejected fraction rho, the suspended mass after n attempts is exactly
rho^n. Successful event mass is the sum of rho^i times the first-draw hit
probability for i<n. The successful-event probabilities are monotone in the
prefix length and converge to uniform selection on the accepted domain.
`eventProbability_eq_uniform` identifies their supremum with the existing
optional accepted-domain sampler, including the empty-domain failure case.
`success_tends_to_uniform` proves convergence of the actual operational event
laws. Nonempty accepted domains have rho<1 and vanishing suspended mass.
No pathwise retry bound or empirical maximum is assumed.

`expectedAttempts` integrates the actual retained trace length, counting every
attempt on success and suspension alike. Its recurrence is 1 plus rho times
the suffix expectation. Its exact value on a prefix is the finite geometric
sum, and its monotone unbounded limit is card(A)/accepted.card. Empty domains
have infinite expected attempts, rather than silently returning a dummy value
or zero work. Nonempty domains have finite unbounded expected attempts.

`ReciprocalRejection` specializes the loop to exactly the zero/public-table
pole predicate in `HasteBoots/snarks/src/packed_extension_lookup.rs::challenges`.
Its marginal output law agrees with `ReciprocalDetection.sample`, the ideal
law used by `StagedPrivateLookup`. The exact expected field-candidate count
uses the actual number of distinct allowed values. The derived public upper
bound is q/(q-size-1), using the proved distinct-exclusion bound; repeated
public hashes do not inflate the exact cost. Every operational prefix embeds
as private shared work with the incoming hash/cache/checkpoint state unchanged.

not a full native work refinement. The staged lookup theorem still runs its
accepted-domain sampler. A trace-aware joint refinement of retries, helper
construction and child/parent transcript state is required before replacing
that whole operational execution. Equality of the marginal accepted values
does not equate transcript states or discard rejected-draw work. Canonical
byte-to-field rejection in `helper/src/classical_transcript.rs::field_build`,

remain open. Honest cryptographic opening/scheduler completion, deferred/global
PBS, application/knowledge and full PBS composition, and the final concrete
unbudgeted 128-bit expected-work theorem also remain open. The full objective
stays active.

## Canonical raw-byte sampler: direct native guard, limiting law and byte cost

`CanonicalByteMask` models increasing byte addresses by increasing powers of
256 and proves the little-endian decoding sum. Its explicit high/low-bit
bijection retains all discarded high bits and proves that masking fresh
uniform bytes gives a uniform value below 2^bits. The mask is the native
bitwise AND with 2^bits-1; it is not reduction modulo the characteristic.
Zero-padding an unread scratch suffix preserves the decoded word, and the
16-byte scratch word stays within the u128 range.

`CanonicalByteSampler` sets bits to the bit length of p-1 and byteCount to
(bits+7)/8, matching `helper/src/transcript.rs::CanonicalSampler`. Its actual
`runPrefix` draws raw byte chunks, decodes and masks them, directly compares
the result with p, and retries on failure. It retains all raw chunks,
including those rejected after masking, in their original order. It does not
implement the comparison by enumerating a finite accepted set. `runPrefix_eq`
proves exact oracle-program equality with the generic rejection analysis,
without extra draws, filtering or postselection. Generic `returned_mem` and
specialized `returned_canonical` prove that each actually returned value
satisfies the below-modulus guard, independently of probability claims.

For p>1, the derived bit range contains p and is strictly smaller than 2p.
When p fits a u128, the byte width fits the native 16-byte scratch array. The
explicit full-width mask branch avoids shifting by 128. `nativeCandidate_eq`
proves that decoding the zero-initialized full scratch array and taking that
branch gives exactly the candidate used by the operational comparison.
These are bounded natural/byte reference semantics; full Rust integer/array
refinement is still a separate obligation.

The limiting successful-value law is uniform on canonical `Fin p` values,
and `uniform_zmod` transports it to the residue ring by the proved canonical
representative map. Primality is needed for its field structure, not for this
sampling law. Successful operational event laws converge to that uniform
law; suspended prefixes contribute no successful value. The all-zero raw
chunk establishes nonemptiness, so the suspension probability vanishes with
no retry cap. The proof derives these laws from raw-byte masking and the
actual retry programs, without a caller-supplied uniformity certificate.

`consumedBytes` counts byteCount times the length of the actual retained raw
trace. `expectedBytes_eq` integrates that observation and identifies it with
the corresponding candidate expectation. The monotone unbounded limit is
byteCount * 2^bits/p, strictly below 2*byteCount for a valid characteristic.
The proof includes every attempted read on success and suspension; it uses
all operational prefixes, rather than an observed maximum or a protocol
budget. The new generic normalization theorem derives hit-event ratios from
those operational prefixes.

Regressions exercise real byte-query paths. With p=17, raw bytes 255 and 49
mask to rejected values 31 and 17, then 144 masks to accepted value 16. Their
raw trace is retained and the subsequent byte remains unused. Modulo-p
reduction would incorrectly accept the first raw byte. A shorter prefix
suspends with both rejected chunks retained. A two-byte p=257 path decodes
bytes [1,2] as 513, masks the unused high bits to obtain accepted value one,
charges two consumed bytes and preserves the next byte. Additional checks
cover zero-padding, the full 128-bit mask branch and the power-of-two p=2
edge case. Concrete profile checks give Goldilocks bits=64/bytes=8 and
BabyBear bits=31/bytes=4, retaining their exact expected byte formulas.

sampling. It does not identify the complete native field-challenge stream.
Production XOF blocks and readers, variable-length consumed-byte receipts,
labels/descriptors and child/parent transcript binding remain open. Joint

assembly, reciprocal retries and adaptive helper construction remains open;

completion, deferred/global PBS, application/knowledge and full PBS
composition, and the final concrete unbudgeted 128-bit expected-work theorem

## Byte-backed reciprocal retries: nested law, partial work and unbounded cost

`OptionalUniformSequence.bind_probability` extends the scaled optional value

sampling or security certificate from the caller.

`OptionalRejectionLoop` retains a complete list of trial observations. A
completed rejected candidate starts the next trial; an unfinished inner field
sample suspends with its observation retained and starts no further trial.
The value projection preserves the exact oracle program. Returned-value
support proves actual acceptance by the supplied direct predicate. Finite
successful laws retain both the field completion factor and the reciprocal
rejection factor, and are dominated by the full accepted-domain law without
normalizing away suspension.

`OptionalRejectionWork` sums the actual work of every retained trial. The head
is always charged, including a partially completed last field sample. For

head cost C, an outer prefix of length m costs
C * sum_{i<m}(beta*rho)^i. Its successful event mass is
sum_{i<m}(beta*rho)^i * beta * h_event, where h_event is the full uniform
field draw's accepted-event probability. These recurrences require no
cost/value independence assumption: all head work is included before its
value/completion test, while only a completed rejection starts the fresh
suffix.

`ByteReciprocalSampler` instantiates this control flow with the actual
canonical-byte extension program. Each trial retains its optional assembled

enumerate the field at runtime. A support theorem proves that every returned

bounded by the ideal accepted-domain event law, with no protocol retry cap.

The private shared-state theorem retains the incoming hash/cache/checkpoints
and all nested trial observations. An arbitrary later continuation can inspect
those full observations, including the partially sampled last trial. All of
its actual shared queries remain in the complete execution, and cannot
increase a fixed earlier accepted-offset event. This is not an erasure of
observable retry metadata or an equality of native transcript states.

`ByteReciprocalLimit` takes all inner coefficient and outer reciprocal
approximations. Successful event probabilities are monotone in both depths.
For each fixed outer prefix the inner limit recovers the full uniform-field
rejection prefix. The outer limit therefore has exactly the accepted-domain
law already used by the staged lookup theorem. Nonempty trusted domains have

the same limiting construction, giving the exact unbounded cost

extension-draw byte cost. The public bound is
C_field * card(K)/(card(K)-tableSize-1). Duplicate poles affect the exact
allowed cardinality, rather than being charged repeatedly as distinct poles.
No empirical maximum or pathwise sampling budget is assumed.

probabilities. Supported successful pairs retain the sampled first challenge
and pass the reciprocal exclusions for that exact hashed table.

The finite pair law is the first draw's completion mass times a uniform
average of the **challenge-dependent** reciprocal prefix probabilities.
There is no assertion that the coordinates are independent or that finite
pair completion has one challenge-independent normalization factor. Every
finite approximation is bounded by the existing joint ideal pair law and
inherits both original single-pair lookup losses. Arbitrary later shared
work may inspect both raw observations; its actual execution remains while
a fixed earlier pair event remains bounded by the same ideal pair event.

fieldCost + average_y [fieldCost * card(K) / card(allowed(hashes(table, y)))]

## Repeated raw-byte pairs with retained work

`ObservedOptionalVector` is a fresh-call vector program for an arbitrary
optional observed sampler. It assumes no scaled uniform kernel. Each call
retains its full observation; suspension stops later calls and retains the
completed value list and the final partial observation. Its optional view is
an exact erasure of the query program, including the suspension gate. The
successful all-coordinate event probability is the actual single-call event
mass raised to the requested count. Supported completed vectors inherit any
property proved for every supported successful single call.

Its work observation sums the real costs of all started calls. The exact
recurrence is `mean(count+1) = singleMean + completion * mean(count)`, including
the current call's cost even on suspension. The resulting finite mean is the
single-call mean times the geometric prefix sum of actual successful
completion mass. No cost/value independence or conditioning on success is
used in these statements.

`ByteLookupPairDiagonal` proves that increasing one common analysis depth is
cofinal in all three raw-byte pair-prefix depths. It proves monotonicity and
convergence of successful event probabilities and unconditional byte means.
A common depth is an analysis approximation, not a native retry budget.

`ByteLookupPairVector` instantiates the observed-vector program with the
actual raw-byte pair program. Every repetition draws a fresh hash challenge
and samples its offset against that challenge's hashed public table. The
finite all-pass law is the actual successful single-pair pass mass to the
true repetition count; no independence between the two coordinates of one
pair is inserted. Both original lookup losses therefore amplify to
`TupleLookupPair.error(...) ^ repetitions`. Completing all operational
approximations recovers the existing repeated lookup **all-pass event** law.
The theorem is explicitly an all-coordinate-event law, not an asserted
arbitrary-vector/transcript distribution equivalence.

A sufficiently large field gives eventual completion mass one. Exact
unbounded bytes are the single pair's true domain-dependent average byte
mean times the repetition count. The public upper bound is consequently

```
fieldCost * (1 + card(K)/(card(K)-size-1)) * repetitions
```

The zero-repetition case is handled separately, without assuming finiteness
to justify a product limit at zero. All completed offsets are proved nonzero
from the support of the actual byte programs. An arbitrary later shared
continuation may inspect all retained observations and make its real hash
queries; the fixed earlier all-pass event is still bounded by the same
repeated lookup error.

## Original staged native lookup bound with an expected availability account

`StagedByteFactor.factor` proves equality of query programs between the
original `StagedCommitmentPrefix.program` byte/helper/native execution and
the prefix-plus-completed-continuation program used by the charge proof.
The original source commitment and its root annotations run before bytes;
the actual helper builder and chosen helper roots follow completed sampling.
The typed sample and every raw observation remain stored in the helper
emission. Projection only repackages returned values and inserts no query,
fallback typed vector, root or native result on suspension.

Its two structural premises state that suspended samples record no helper
roots and run no native continuation. The concrete native theorem derives
both facts from `ByteLookupPairMiddle.completed` and
`OptionalStagedLookup.continuation`; they are not supplied security or work
certificates. `StagedByteFactor.charge` then identifies the original staged
program's charge with the factored program's charge for any state-dependent
loss, using that pure result projection adds no queries.

`StagedByteChargedLimit` projects the proven completed account construction
back to the original staged result shape: original source, typed raw-byte/
optional helper emission, optional native result, and actual final state/
account. The measure is normalized under the existing sampler/domain
conditions. Its mean account equals the supremum of the original whole
staged query program's finite charges, retaining earlier source work and
both real root-recording stages exactly once.

`StagedByteExpectedSecurity.false_acceptance_bound` now replaces the charge
supremum in the previously proved unbounded native lookup bound by this
actual mean availability account. The false-acceptance event remains in the
original frozen-source witness law; it is not changed to helper-time or
final-state source decoding. The lookup repetition, scalar algebra and
grouped PCS losses are retained. The mean account includes all source,
sampling/helper and native work charged by the actual availability metric,
including computed native rejection branches. No oracle/retry cap or
assumed PCS/FS/work certificate is introduced.

The native regressions instantiate exact query-program factorization with
an earlier source hash, original source-root recording, three genuine byte
pairs, helper/root construction and the actual algebra/PCS continuation.
They also verify normalization in the original staged return shape and the
mean identity against that original program's whole charge supremum.

## Canonical byte work in the completed raw-trace measure

`CompletedCostTransfer` partitions each unconditional prefix cost into its
completed and incomplete contributions. Monotonicity of the completed
observation measures gives convergence of the first contribution to the
actual completed mean. A proved zero limit for the second contribution
then transfers the unconditional limit exactly. This theorem does not
require finite means or replace the work-tail proof with completion
probability tending to one.

`RejectionTraceWork` derives the operational trace-length bound at each
analysis depth and proves that a suspended trace has length exactly that
depth. The incomplete expected work is therefore exactly `n * rho^n`,
where `rho` is the sampler's rejection probability. Its geometric decay
for a nonempty accepted domain proves the actual completed raw-trace
mean is the full-domain cardinality divided by the accepted cardinality.
The completed trace measure is normalized under the same condition.
An empty accepted domain instead has zero completed mass while the
unconditional retry mean is infinite; a regression checks this distinction.
These are derived bounds for finite approximations, not native retry caps.

`CanonicalTraceWork` constructs the completed measure of the actual
masked-below-modulus byte sampler, retaining every rejected raw chunk.
Its incomplete expected byte work is the configured byte width times
`n * rho^n`, which tends to zero for `1 < p`. Its completed expected bytes
thus equal the previously proved unconditional byte-work limit, exactly
`byteCount(p) * 2^bits(p) / p`. Regressions check a small modulus, positive
incomplete work at finite depth, and the native Goldilocks and BabyBear
formulas. Their raw chunk widths are eight and four bytes respectively;
these widths are separate from protocol packing parameters.

This closes the base canonical sampler's computational byte-work transfer.
Nested sequential coefficient/extension and reciprocal/pair/vector byte-work
transfers remain open, as do physical SHA/XOF/hash-work accounting, production
transcript/FS and Rust refinement, honest opening/scheduler completeness,
deferred/global PBS, application/knowledge/full-PBS composition and the final
concrete unbudgeted 128-bit expected-work theorem. The full formal-security
objective remains active.

## Completed sequential coefficient and extension byte means

`CoefficientTraceWork` derives support and suspension bounds from the actual
sequential coefficient query program. At analysis depth `n`, a request for
`c` coefficients retains at most `c * n` raw chunks, including earlier accepted
coefficients and the suspended last coefficient. Its suspension probability
is at most `c * rho^n`, where `rho` is the actual base sampler rejection
probability. The proof starts the suffix only after a completed head; it
requires no supplied independence certificate.

These bounds give an incomplete expected byte cost of at most
`byteCount(p) * c * c * (n * rho^n)`. For `1 < p`, the geometric work tail
vanishes, so `CompletedCostTransfer` identifies the completed raw-trace
mean with the previously derived unconditional limit, exactly
`c * CanonicalByteSampler.totalExpectedBytes p`. The same completed measure
is normalized without rescaling finite successful mass. The per-depth
support bounds are analysis facts, not protocol retry or byte limits.

`ExtensionTraceWork` retains the actual pure basis assembly together with
the whole coefficient observation. Its incomplete work equals that of the
`count * degree` sequential coefficients; completion is precisely coefficient
completion. Consequently its completed measure is normalized and its exact
byte mean is `count * degree` times the base sampler mean. The theorem
does not assume a concrete native field constructor or count pure assembly
as physical hash work.

Regressions check normalization, zero coefficient requests, two completed
coefficients, and the real suspended execution that accepts the first
coefficient and retains both raw chunks. A two-coordinate basis with two
requested elements checks the four-coefficient completed mean. Native
Goldilocks degree three and BabyBear degree six regressions check their
completed raw byte means; lookup degrees remain separate from PCS packing.

This closes the sequential coefficient and pure extension byte-work
transfers. Reciprocal/pair/vector byte-work transfers, physical SHA/XOF/hash
work, production transcript/FS and Rust refinement, honest opening/scheduler
completeness, deferred/global PBS, application/knowledge/full-PBS composition
and the final concrete unbudgeted 128-bit expected-work theorem remain open.
The full formal-security objective remains active.

## Completed reciprocal raw-trial byte-work mean

`OptionalRejectionTail` proves finite support cost bounds and an exact
suspension recurrence for the actual optional rejection loop. An inner
suspension stops immediately and retains that trial; only a completed
rejected candidate starts another trial. If the inner suspension probability
is `a` and completed rejection probability is `r`, outer depth `O` has
suspension probability at most `O * a + r^O`. Every supported trial's
work contributes to the prefix bound, including a partial last trial.

`ReciprocalTraceWork` derives the field-trial suspension bound from the
sequential coefficient program and the completed pole-rejection rate from
the actual candidate law. Let `w` be raw byte width, `d` the basis degree,
`I` inner depth, `O` outer depth, `kappa` the canonical byte rejection
probability and `theta` the rejection probability of the actual reciprocal
allowed domain. The full prefix consumes at most `w * d * I * O` bytes
and suspends with probability at most `O * d * kappa^I + theta^O`.
Consequently its unfinished expected work is bounded by their product.
All these are derived analysis-prefix bounds, not native retry or byte caps.

At common depth `n`, this product is
`w * d^2 * n^3 * kappa^n + w * d * n^2 * theta^n`. Polynomial/geometric
decay proves both terms tend to zero under `1 < p` and the existing
accepted-domain size condition. This accounts separately for unfinished
inner fields and completed but rejected field trials; it does not infer
work convergence merely from successful mass tending to one.

The completed raw-trial measure is normalized and cofinal in all independent
inner/outer depths, for arbitrary events on the full retained observation.
Its exact expected consumed bytes equal the existing unconditional
reciprocal work supremum and formula: one actual field draw's canonical
byte mean times `card(K) / card(allowed(table))`. The real allowed-domain
cardinality preserves duplicate-pole behavior. No cost/value independence
certificate or finite successful-mass normalization is supplied.

Regressions check immediate stopping on inner suspension, normalized
completed traces, the exact completed mean `32/15` for the small-field
one-pole fixture, support bounds including partial work, and cofinality
for a raw-byte-cost event. The concrete tape regression retains two
completed rejected fields and an incomplete third field with four issued
bytes, leaving the later tape unused.

This closes the reciprocal byte-work transfer. Pair/vector byte-work
transfers, physical SHA/XOF/hash work, production transcript/FS and Rust
refinement, honest opening/scheduler completeness, deferred/global PBS,
application/knowledge/full-PBS composition and the final concrete unbudgeted
128-bit expected-work theorem remain open. The full objective remains active.

## Completed pair and repeated typed lookup byte-work means

`PairTraceWork` derives support and suspension bounds from the actual
byte-backed pair program. The first completed field challenge chooses its
public-table hashes and reciprocal domain; unfinished first draws start no
reciprocal trial. With byte width `w`, basis degree `d` and depths `H,I,O`,
full retained work is at most `w * d * (H + I * O)`. Suspension is bounded by
`d * kappa^H + O * d * kappa^I + sum_y theta(y)^O`, where `kappa` is the
base canonical rejection probability and `theta(y)` belongs to the actual
reciprocal domain for first challenge `y`.

The unweighted finite sum over challenges is only an auxiliary work-tail
bound. It does not replace the exact conditional-domain average in the
final mean or add a security loss. Every fixed polynomial multiple of this
suspension probability tends to zero along common depth, because each
actual domain is nonempty under the existing size condition. The completed
pair measure is normalized and its byte mean equals the existing exact
unconditional pair-work formula, retaining collisions and duplicate poles.
No independence between the pair coordinates is assumed.

`ObservedVectorTail` derives support and suspension bounds for the actual
sequential observed-vector program. A failed head stops the suffix; every
started observation remains in the work sum. For `r` requested repetitions,
the raw vector support bound is `r * w * d * (n + n^2)` and its suspension
probability is at most `r` times that of the real single-pair program.
`VectorTraceWork` combines these bounds with the pair's polynomial tail
decay to prove that unfinished vector byte work vanishes. Earlier successful
pairs and the suspended last pair are all counted. These are derived bounds
on finite analysis approximations, not native retry or byte caps.

The typing adapter uses the already proved exact raw-program erasure and
completion equivalence. It transfers the result directly to the existing
`ByteLookupUnbounded.measure` used by the staged native security proof.
The actual completed typed mean equals the unconditional repeated-byte
supremum, hence the exact conditional-domain pair byte mean times the true
repetition count. A public size-based upper bound is also proved for that
same completed measure. Repetition count, extension degree and PCS packing
remain separate parameters.

Regressions check pair normalization and mean, support bounds with partial
work, zero and three repetitions in the original typed measure, and its
public size-based cost bound. The actual typed trace regression preserves
one completed pair and six total bytes when the second pair suspends
inside an offset field draw, leaving the third repetition and later tape
unstarted. Existing fixtures retain different domain cardinalities at
different first challenges.

This closes the canonical/coefficient/extension/reciprocal/pair/vector
byte-work transfers to completed sampler measures, including the existing
unbounded typed lookup law. Converting these byte means and the separate
availability account to physical SHA/XOF/hash work remains open, as do
production transcript/FS and Rust refinement, honest opening/scheduler
completeness, deferred/global PBS, application/knowledge/full-PBS composition
and the final concrete unbudgeted 128-bit expected-work theorem. The full
formal-security objective remains active.

## Revised roadmap M0: experiment contract and extraction probe

The revised plan prioritizes the custom transcript/compiler and unrestricted
expected-work gaps. Final completion requires both primitive and abstract
64-bit computation accounting, checked correspondence with the pinned Rust
typed verifier, and a separate byte-decoding corollary. The original protocol
12/schedule-5 Brakedown target, dimensions, keys, and Goldilocks-before-BabyBear
order are unchanged.

`SecurityExperiment` defines the target interface independently of any
claimed security bound. Chronological events distinguish attacker, verifier
and setup work. Primitive SHA-512 blocks, SHAKE absorb/squeeze blocks,
constructed bytes, memory operations and machine steps have separate fields;
no conversion between them is assumed. Submissions do not magically create
a paid-work event: native execution and cost refinement must justify that
charge. Earlier accepted false submissions persist after later rejection.

The final target ranges over an explicit adversary type and its implemented
experiment. A history is a potentially infinite sequence of optional events,
with the countable product sigma algebra. Total attacker steps are the
supremum of actual finite prefix counts. This admits unbounded retries and
infinite work without using a discrete sigma algebra on an uncountable
whole-history space. `RiskBound` retains an explicit initial-risk term;
`ExpectedWorkSecurity` states the desired ratio and does not prove it.
The current module is a contract, not the joint native execution or a
security certificate.

Remaining revised milestones, in order: implement joint SHAKE/SHA-512
transcript semantics; prove one actual linked lookup child under prequeries
and stream reuse; prove the stopping/work conversion; compose all PBS stages
and application extraction; compile the whole transcript and prove checked
Rust correspondence; then certify concrete parameters and the byte corollary.
No further sampler foundations are planned without a named dependency of
these end-to-end obligations.

## Revised roadmap M0: actual sampler extraction probe

`scripts/extract-hasteboots-sampler` copies the complete `CanonicalSampler`
fragment verbatim from the pinned Rust `helper/src/transcript.rs`, lines
544–573. It checks both the complete source SHA-256 and the fragment SHA-256.
A separate diagnostic wrapper supplies a fixed repeated block to the reader;
that wrapper is not an oracle model and is not used as a replacement sampler.
No original Rust source is modified.

The frontend is the official Aeneas release
[nightly-2026.07.11-15b9684](https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas/releases/tag/nightly-2026.07.11-15b9684),
with bundled Charon 0.1.223 (recorded Charon revision
`ef3748c1a92c6acc402f978770193d34adc0fe6e`). The Linux archive SHA-256 is
`a3ebfd35c9c77873bcc6e22fa0f1d9965539b6364c6b706a5af8aeca41d`.
The harness additionally verifies the three executable hashes and the bundled
Rust toolchain file. It requires Rust nightly-2026-06-01 with `rustc-dev`,
`rust-src`, `llvm-tools-preview`, and `miri` installed. Miri's sysroot is
necessary to expose the Rust standard-library MIR for `div_ceil`. This
experiment uses the verified official binaries, not a local frontend build.

Given the unpacked release directory and the prepared isolated backend:

```sh
scripts/probe-hasteboots-aeneas /tmp/hasteboots-aeneas-m0
scripts/extract-hasteboots-sampler --tools /tmp/hasteboots-aeneas-tools \
  --backend /tmp/hasteboots-aeneas-m0
scripts/extract-hasteboots-sampler --tools /tmp/hasteboots-aeneas-tools \
  --backend /tmp/hasteboots-aeneas-m0 --mode sampler
```

The default constructor-only extraction passes Lean 4.35 typechecking and
its target dependency audit is exactly `[propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound]`. `u32::div_ceil` is extracted transparently by the inclusion
pattern `core::num::_::div_ceil`; treating it as an opaque axiom is refused.
Only the generated import changes, from the umbrella `Aeneas` to `Aeneas.Std`
and `Aeneas.Tactic.RustAttributes`. Every generated declaration and term is
preserved. This establishes an import/extraction subgate, not constructor
functional correctness or Rust compiler correctness.

The full sampler command currently **fails** Lean typechecking. The generated
`FnMut` callback use carries the updated mutable slice, whereas the backend
`FnMut` class expects only the unit result and updated closure. The closure's
`FnOnce` instance also mismatches its expected unit result. Elaboration then
reports `sorryAx` in the sampler dependency closure; the command exits
nonzero and its manifest records failure. No admitted sampler is accepted.
This is a concrete frontend/backend correspondence gap to resolve before the
full Rust refinement gate can pass. Broad extraction of Rust internals also
exposes unsupported pointer/transmute operations; the narrow inclusion rules
avoid those without hiding `div_ceil`.

Each run has a fresh directory under ignored `build/hasteboots-extraction`,
with the exact fixture, LLBC, generated Lean, import-only checked file,
commands, logs, source/tool/output hashes, backend diff fingerprint, root
manifest/toolchain, mathlib revision, and explicit pass/failure status.
Failures cannot reuse an earlier successful output. Constructor reproduction
passed; full sampler reproduction reached and rejected the callback mismatch.
Root proof sources and dependency pins remain unchanged. Joint oracle
semantics, unrestricted work conversion, PBS composition, and full verifier
correspondence remain unproved; the full objective remains active.


## Revised roadmap M1: normalized joint input-indexed oracle world

`InputIndexedOracle.lean` defines one probability measure on all SHAKE byte
coordinates `(complete input, output position)` and all SHA-512 byte
coordinates `(complete input, position < 64)`. The two primitive families
share one world and use disjoint coordinate tags. Only the base byte space
is discrete; the infinite world has the product sigma algebra. Normalization
is proved by the infinite-product probability-measure instance.

Readers retain an input and cursor. Every read consults the same fixed
world, and its cursor advances by the actual requested count. The proved
split/coalesced-read identity preserves both output and cursor pointwise;
empty reads preserve the cursor, and restarting a repeated input uses its
existing prefix. Cloning a reader is ordinary copying of that same state,
not resampling. The model does not place reader IDs or method labels in
oracle keys.

Distinct finite coordinates have the exact product byte law and the exact
uniform finite-vector marginal used by the byte-sampler proofs. The SHAKE
block law, complete SHA-512 digest law, and joint cross-primitive byte law
are derived from the same normalized measure. Finite mixed prequery
assignments are measurable and have mass `256^(-number of distinct
coordinates)`; adding a fresh coordinate multiplies mass by `1/256`.
Repeated coordinates remain one assignment, as covered by the regression.
This is a fixed finite-history extension theorem, not adaptive
conditioning, a Fiat–Shamir theorem, or a claimed fresh phase.

This implements the joint ideal-law and reader-consistency part of M1.
Native length framing (kinds 0–8), receipt and child transitions, native
extension basis descriptors, adaptive revelation/cached-handler equivalence,
and transcript compilation remain open. M0's full Rust correspondence gate
also remains open: specialization with `--monomorphize-mut=except-types`,

TODO. No generated terms or original Rust sources were rewritten to hide
these failures. Diagnostic artifacts are in

## Revised roadmap M1: mixed-oracle prefix replay and exact fiber laws

`ObservationReplay.lean` adds truthfulness and counterfactual replay for a
shared log containing SHAKE starts/chunks and complete SHA-512 digest
observations. The native observation type now also admits hash entries.
Truthfulness prevents replay certificates from holding vacuously for an
impossible observation log. The finite footprint counts distinct returned
coordinates across both primitives, retaining repeated calls in the ordered
log. Changing bytes outside that footprint preserves the complete execution.
The primitive hash action uses the same joint world; connecting the existing
Merkle cached handler to this action remains a separate bridge.

Whole-execution replay alone would not establish online query selection.
`OracleProgram.lean` therefore supplies explicit start/read/hash nodes whose
continuations receive results but no world argument. Every finite prefix
returns its actual residual program. Agreement with the observed prefix
preserves its log, residual program, and next request's primitive, complete
input, offset, and count. This proves that the next request is determined
before its response is supplied. The prefix budget is an analysis device,
not an implementation retry cap or a machine-work counter. Unbounded loops
still require compiled compatible prefix families and a completion bridge.

For any certified execution, its exact fiber is proved equal to a finite
coordinate-assignment event in the original product sigma algebra. It is
measurable and has exact mass `(1/256)^(number of distinct returned bytes)`.
Fixing any byte value at a coordinate outside that footprint multiplies the
fiber mass by `1/256`, without division by successful mass or a success-floor
premise. Whole-history use requires the program to include the complete
observed past. Native stage compilers must still establish the required
unobserved-coordinate premise; labels alone do not establish it.

`NativeTranscriptProgram.lean` represents the native-model operations as
online programs. Nine interpretation theorems preserve both the result
and ordered observations for queries, byte challenges, checkpoints,
field starts/reads/receipts/finishes, forks, and child finishes. A linked-child
interface composes an online body between native fork and finish and inherits
prefix replay. The body remains an explicit parameter: the actual typed
lookup protocol has not been compiled or proved secure by this interface.
The equalities relate Lean models; they are not Rust extraction certificates.

## Revised roadmap M1: canonical native sampler prefix compilation

`CanonicalTranscriptSampler.lean` compiles the canonical rejection subloop
into the online oracle-program language. Each attempt calls the existing
field reader for the configured byte width, decodes little-endian, applies
the native mask (including the full 128-bit branch), and accepts exactly
below the modulus. The source-aligned evaluator and compiled program have
proved identical outcomes and ordered logs. Native callers still require
`1 < p` and `p < 2^128`; the generic mathematical definitions also exist
outside that native domain and do not model invalid-constructor panics.
