Zero padding the unread suffix of the native 16-byte scratch array preserves
the decoded value, and that scratch value fits u128. The operational accept
test is exactly the existing canonical masked-vector test. Every accepted
value is proved below the modulus. Full raw chunks are retained, including
rejected candidates and high bits discarded by the mask.

The final field phase contains exactly the previous consumed prefix followed
by all new raw chunks. Reader coherence is preserved. Successful observations
are unchanged by every larger analysis depth, and suspended logs refine to
larger logs. An exact resumption theorem identifies execution at depth
`first + extra` with continuing the first observation, concatenating its
chunks and logs. Suspension emits no receipt. It is not a native rejection,
verification result, or implementation retry limit.

The typed raw observation is proved reachable in the existing private
canonical sampler for every world. This transfers the previously proved
support-level attempt bound and exact suspended attempt count. Actual added
reader bytes equal the earlier trace byte-cost function pointwise; the
unread scratch zeros are not counted as returned bytes. This is neither an
expected-work theorem nor a primitive-to-machine-cost conversion.

The support bridge does not assert equality of distributions for a stage
chosen after adversarial prequeries. That probability bridge still requires
the whole-history first-query compiler and its freshness premises. Also open
are the coefficient/vector collector and field finalization, native typed
basis descriptors, reciprocal/lookup body compilation, arbitrary-input
frame-decoder soundness, unrestricted stopping/work conversion, full PBS
composition, concrete certification, and checked Rust/scheduler refinement.
The full objective remains active and unproved.

## Native challenge fields and typed assembly

`NativeExtensionFields.lean` proves irreducibility of the actual native
challenge polynomials: Goldilocks `X^3 - 7` and BabyBear `X^6 - 31`.
Kernel-checked finite-field exponent witnesses establish the required
non-cube and non-square facts. For BabyBear, a norm argument over the
cubic extension excludes a square root of its generator; polynomial
composition then proves the degree-six polynomial irreducible. No extra
irreducibility axiom or external primality/certificate trust is introduced.

The resulting quotient fields have explicit power bases indexed by `Fin 3`
and `Fin 6`, with basis vectors equal to the corresponding generator powers.
Their cardinalities are proved to be the base modulus cubed and raised to
the sixth power. These are the native challenge fields, distinct from the
PCS degree-four/eight symbol fields. This establishes field structure and
size, without inferring a security bound from either cardinality.

`NativeFieldAssembly.lean` converts a length-checked list of accepted
canonical integers into indexed base-field coefficients. The canonical
representative of each converted value equals the original integer under
the established `< p` bounds. Extension assembly preserves every
coordinate at flat offset `coordinate + degree * element`. The
`finished_request_coordinate` theorem obtains both length and bounds from
the actual completed `NativeFieldVector.request`, including its native
receipt, for every world and finite analysis budget. Concrete assembly
functions use the newly proved Goldilocks degree-three and BabyBear
degree-six power bases. Assembly is pure and issues no oracle operations.

This closes the mathematical field-existence and typed-coordinate grouping
part of M1. It does not prove Rust lazy/Montgomery representation conversion,
extension-basis descriptor byte agreement, valid native request sizes, or
the whole-history conditional distribution bridge. Those obligations,
the actual lookup compiler, unrestricted stopping/work conversion, full
PBS security composition, concrete parameter certification, and checked
Rust/scheduler correspondence remain open. The final security theorem
remains unproved.

including zero high bytes; no alternate header representation is accepted.

parse is equivalent to a valid native frame encoding followed by exactly

complete-input corollary requires the returned suffix to be empty.

The new `decodeAll` consumes a complete frame stream, including the empty
stream. Termination follows from the strict decrease in remaining byte
length on every successful frame; it imposes no external frame-count cap.
Its soundness and completeness theorems characterize successful results
exactly as valid frame lists whose `encodeMany` equals the entire input.
Malformed or leftover bytes cannot disappear from a successful full parse.

in the earlier milestones, so arbitrary prequeries can now be interpreted

## Native extension descriptors and online challenge requests

`NativeExtensionDescriptor.lean` derives the complete multiplication table
from a power basis and its root relation. For `X^degree - w`, the product
of basis monomials has coefficient one at `i+j` when this is below the
degree, and coefficient `w` at `i+j-degree` otherwise; every other
coordinate is zero. Since both indices are below the degree, wrapping
occurs at most once. The canonical-integer theorem uses explicit modulus
and `w` bounds rather than assuming a native coefficient conversion.

The resulting computable descriptor matches the source layout of
`classical_transcript.rs::extension_basis`: u64le degree, then each
canonical coefficient as u128le, with `i` outermost, `j` in the middle,
and `k` innermost. Its length is proved to be `8 + 16*degree^3`; table
entries fit their u128 encoding whenever `w` does. The native power bases
proved earlier instantiate this theorem: Goldilocks uses degree three and
`w=7`, BabyBear uses degree six and `w=31`. Their mathematical basis
descriptors equal these closed byte formulas. This proves the descriptor
for the mathematical native fields; Rust multiplication, lazy/Montgomery
storage and `.value()` correspondence are still required to identify the
actual Rust descriptor computation with it.

`NativeExtensionRequest.lean` appends the native kind-1 `extension vector`
and `extension basis` frames before calling the online canonical collector
for `count*degree` coefficients. Its checked entry rejects zero degree and
64-bit product overflow before returning an executable oracle program.
Concrete entries select the native Goldilocks and BabyBear parameters.
Generic core requests still require the native modulus/degree/representation
contract; the checked entry models count arithmetic, not arbitrary field
validation or Rust cache locking/error behavior.

Theorems identify the exact prelude input and first reader-start event,
retain the collector's count and canonical-value invariants, and connect
finished requests to typed extension coordinates. Resumption preserves the
full result and ordered observation log without replaying the prelude or
a finished receipt. Zero-count requests retain descriptor binding, reader
start and the empty-prefix receipt. From the same prior transcript,
extension and prime requests cannot have equal field-reader inputs, even
with different request labels, moduli or counts. This is structural domain
separation, without a freshness assumption or a security probability claim.

The whole-history conditional law and actual lookup child compiler remain
open, including the typed child wrapper's checkpoint, zero-count field-identity
phase and parent-lineage composition. Unrestricted stopping/work conversion,
full PBS security composition, concrete certification, strict proof-byte
decoding, and checked Rust/scheduler correspondence also remain open. In particular the descriptor theorem does
not close the Rust refinement gate or establish the final security theorem.

## Typed detached extension children and lineage guards

`TypedTranscriptChild.lean` compiles the classical-state projection of
`transcript.rs::fork_classical_extension` and `finish_classical_child` into
online oracle programs. The successful fork orders raw framed child
creation, a checkpoint of the resulting parent, and the child's zero-count
`typed extension identity` request. The identity program is proved equal
to the existing native extension request at count zero for every analysis
budget, with its finished collector state erased. It retains all three
identity observations and preserves the inherited profile. The saved
binding records the post-fork parent's profile, exact 64-byte checkpoint
and child label. A legacy parent rejects without observations.

Finish checks the missing/spent binding, parent mode, child mode, parent
profile, child profile, and checkpoint bytes in native short-circuit order.
Profile/mode failures emit no queries. A checkpoint mismatch emits exactly
the checkpoint start/output and retains both states. Success queries the
child finish fingerprint, links it into the parent, and clears the returned
child's binding. The complete state-effect theorem proves that every
failure retains parent and child, and every success spends this stored
binding. A second finish of that returned child fails without observations,
even if evaluated in another world. This is a per-instance state effect,
not a global prohibition on copied states.

The interpreter theorems preserve complete results and ordered logs in the
same input-indexed world. The typed fork has seven observations; successful
finish has four. These are observations, not distinct random-oracle inputs
or a physical-work metric. Full and partial wrapper execution inherit
whole-observation replay. Forking and immediately finishing accepts for
every consistent world, without a fresh-input or collision-free premise.

The acceptance characterization requires equality of the computed
checkpoint bytes; it does not infer equality of parent transcript inputs.
A regression deliberately advances the parent in a constant-output world
and verifies acceptance via the colliding checkpoint. Therefore the model
does not erase a collision event that a later security bound must charge.

This closes the source-aligned detached wrapper/identity/guard model gap.
It does not prove Rust execution refinement or protocol-flag transport,
trusted field/cache success, scoped owned-child semantics, or the actual
lookup body compiler. Those remain separate, together with the whole-history
conditional law, unrestricted stopping/work conversion, full PBS security
composition, concrete certification, strict proof-byte decoding, and checked
Rust/scheduler correspondence. The final security theorem remains unproved.

## Online native lookup challenge selection

`TypedFieldRequest.lean` models the extension adapter's additional
`typed request kind` frame for scalar/vector calls. Its scalar-start
program exposes the actual reader before the first coefficient candidate;
beginning and driving this reader is proved equal to a native extension
scalar request. Complete draws have exactly the declared coefficient count
and canonical bounds. The coordinate theorem proves that total mathematical
assembly uses neither its default getter nor modular reduction on these
completed draws. A pending one-candidate drive logs its actual byte read
before any receipt or subsequent request start.

`NativeLookupChallenge.lean` compiles one iteration of the challenge-selection
part of `packed_extension_lookup.rs::challenges`, through the accepted
reciprocal offset. It first samples the compression scalar, builds powers
by the native multiplication loop, and compresses public rows with the
literal zip/fold. It then retries reciprocal scalars until nonzero and off
every pole of that compressed table. Native Goldilocks degree-three and
BabyBear degree-six entry points use the previously proved bases and
multiplication-table descriptors. Public table geometry and trusted field
contracts remain caller obligations; the literal zip semantics do not
replace native preflight validation.

Each analysis step drives one canonical coefficient candidate. A rejected
canonical integer retains the current reader and raw bytes. A completed
forbidden reciprocal retains its full coefficient state and receipt before
starting a new typed scalar request from the resulting transcript. Every
completed draw is retained, along with the actual reciprocal-rejection
counter. No rejected candidate is replaced with an independent field coin.
A completed pair emits no further observations when driven again.

The compiled programs and direct execution model agree on full results and
ordered logs. Exact resumption preserves the machine, all previous draws,
byte cursors and receipts for every split of the analysis budget. Exhaustion
returns a suspended analysis machine, not a verifier rejection or Rust retry
cutoff. The field-validity invariant proves every retained draw complete,
canonical, and equal to its assembled coordinates. The selection invariant
freezes the public powers/table and proves every returned reciprocal is
nonzero and off every pole in the table compressed by its own compression
challenge. The count invariant distinguishes the compression draw, all
rejected reciprocal draws, and the accepted terminal draw. Positive-degree
requests retain pending readers in every active state. These are operational
and algebraic theorems in the same joint world; they do not assume freshness
or establish a conditional sampling distribution or work bound.

This implements the native compression/reciprocal selection prefix for one
lookup repetition. Repeated/grouped request control, inverse-table arithmetic

## Whole-history posterior and continuation laws

`OraclePosterior.lean` proves the exact joint-world posterior after any
finite coordinate assignment. The observed finite tuple is independent
of the entire unobserved complement in the original product sigma algebra.
Consequently, conditioning fixes exactly the seen bytes and leaves all
unseen coordinates with their original product law. This applies jointly
to SHAKE and SHA-512, including arbitrary prequeries and partial overlap.
The generator depends only on the finite cached values, not on the witness
world's unobserved bytes. Reinstalling that cache preserves the recorded
execution pointwise by replay.

Both normalized and unnormalized forms are proved. The restriction of the
world law to the exact history equals the history mass times the cached
world law. Nonzero mass of each attainable finite history is derived from
its finite assignment; no numerical history/success floor is assumed.
There is no conditioning on verification success and no discarded failure
or suspended mass.

`OracleExecutionLaw.lean` proves that a replayable execution's countable
finite byte log determines its entire result. Reachable results are therefore
countable even when the payload type is not, so every execution predicate
and nonnegative score is measurable without making the infinite world
discrete. An adaptive continuation chosen from the complete retained past
has its exact conditional event law under one cached independent-world
generator. The same unnormalized identity holds for nonnegative integrals,
including infinite scores and infinite expectations, without bounded-work
or finite-mean premises. The score is evaluated on the actual continuation
result/log, not on virtual samples used by the mathematical generator.
Complete programs and paused prefixes with their residual programs have
explicit corollaries.

`CachedOracleResponse.lean` derives finite response laws from that posterior.
The response retains cached coordinate values and masks a uniform word
only on unseen coordinates. Partial overlap is handled explicitly; no
freshness premise is imposed on the general response theorem. Fully fresh
blocks have their uniform law, while fully repeated blocks have a Dirac law
at the previously observed answer. Native SHAKE offsets and SHA-512 digest
positions discharge within-block coordinate distinctness. The same generated
world feeds the whole future continuation, so these marginal laws do not
resample each read independently or introduce reader-instance entropy.

This closes the finite-history disintegration part of the joint-oracle
bridge. A smoke application instantiates the conditional work identity with
the actual native Goldilocks lookup-selection compiler after arbitrary
previous transcript/hash activity. Further work must derive cache-aware
bad-event charges, rather than treating prequeried field requests as uniform.
Native/private sampler distribution correspondence, private-coin averaging,
production Merkle-handler and scheduler coupling, and unrestricted stopping
still require composition. The remaining lookup body, full PBS security,
concrete certification, strict proof-byte decoding, and checked Rust
refinement also remain open. No numerical security or physical-work bound
is inferred from the new conditional identities; the final theorem remains
unproved.

## History averaging and unrestricted expected-work reduction

`OracleHistoryCharge.lean` partitions the joint world law over every
attainable full result/log history. The partition is countable by replay,
without a supplied query limit or countable payload assumption. Its
restricted measures sum to the original law exactly. Bounds on each
restricted bad event average into the same actual nonnegative score,
including infinite scores. Cache-conditional event/work inequalities from
the posterior generator have an explicit global-bound corollary.

An inherited-risk version is also proved. A prefix may already contain a
lucky bad answer, so conditioning on it need not leave a tiny future error
probability. The interface retains this risk as an unnormalized ledger;
the cache-conditional corollary weights each risk by its complete history
mass. Charging the ledger to earlier actual work remains an explicit
obligation. Neither a fresh-answer assumption nor zero inherited risk is
inserted by the averaging theorem. Prefix work can be retained in the
score payload; no work is invented by the reduction itself.

`UnboundedHistorySecurity.lean` connects limiting arguments to the existing
`SecurityExperiment` contract. A bad prefix means an accepted false
submission at any earlier observation slot. These events increase with
depth and their union is exactly `HistoryBad`, so later rejection or idle
slots cannot remove earlier bad outcomes. Finite actor costs are measurable
and monotone. The mean total work equals the supremum of all prefix means,
including infinite work and infinite expectations.

Per-prefix risk inequalities now imply the unrestricted `RiskBound`, with
the initial-risk term preserved. Multiplicative prefix inequalities imply
the exact `ExpectedWorkSecurity` interface for any supplied experiment,
adversary class and bit target, without dividing by success probability.
All prefixes are proof approximations, not runtime caps or assumed stopping
budgets. The source must still supply the actual experiment law and prove
the native numerical inequalities at every prefix. In particular these
conditional reduction theorems do not certify the HasteBoots 128-bit bound.

Averaging accepts arbitrary nonnegative scores, including primitive-work
scores. The limit specialization uses the contract's attacker `machineSteps`;
it does not identify primitive blocks with abstract machine instructions.
Their implementation/refinement bridge remains separate.

The observation alphabet retains the contract's discrete sigma algebra;
the infinite history space retains its product sigma algebra. Regression
histories check persistent accepted-false outcomes after rejection,
exclusion of verifier work, and genuinely infinite attacker work. A
zero-work accepting toy experiment satisfies only the risk bound with
initial risk one and is proved not to satisfy the 128-bit expected-work
contract. A separate oracle regression records a rare zero byte with
history mass `1/256` and shows its repeated query has conditional bad
probability one, preserving rather than erasing cached lucky outcomes.

This proves the history-averaging and unrestricted-limit reductions.
Native cache-aware charges, inherited-risk charging, the actual experiment
and chronological work-trace coupling, private-coin averaging, the remaining
lookup/PBS composition, concrete certification, strict proof-byte decoding,
and checked Rust/scheduler refinement remain open. The end-to-end security
objective remains active and unproved.

## Joint-world SHA-512 cache refinement

`JointHashCache` now computes the existing cached hash state directly from
mixed transcript observations. It decodes recorded full digests, keeps
repeated hash log entries, and deduplicates hash keys. Truthful histories
imply cache/log/key coherence and agreement with the world, without a
collision-freedom premise. SHAKE observations never populate SHA-512 keys,
even at identical input bytes. The footprint correspondence proves that a
hash input has either all 64 hash coordinates observed or none.

`JointHashKernel` proves the complete conditional answer law after any
replayable mixed-oracle execution: a new SHA-512 input is uniform on the
exact digest alphabet of cardinality `2^512`, and a repeated input returns
its recorded digest. It also proves equality of event probabilities for
the full updated state, including its chronological log. This connects
the joint world to the existing canonical cached hash handler rather than
assuming a separate independent hash execution.

The collision and root-wide Merkle payload checkpoint one-step charges
therefore hold in the joint world, conditional on the entire preceding
SHAKE/hash history. Fresh steps retain their concrete cache-key or
checkpoint target-union numerator over `2^512`; cache hits contribute zero
new loss. These bounds require safety or checkpoint stability in the
conditioned history. Earlier bad events are inherited risk and must be
retained in composition; these theorems do not declare already compromised
histories safe. They impose no global query cap and no SHAKE freshness
premise.

## Accumulated joint-world hash collision charge

`OraclePrefixTrace` proves the chronological successor equation for the
existing causal mixed-oracle interpreter. A paused prefix executes its
retained next primitive; completed prefixes remain completed, and every
successor retains the complete earlier log. Every completed inductive
program is exactly represented by one of its prefixes. This does not prove
termination or compilation of an unbounded native rejection sampler.

`OracleHistoryDrift` averages conditional bounds against the full attainable
history partition. Charges are functions of the pre-answer result/log;
inherited risk remains at its actual history weight. Its additive form
keeps the earlier-risk integral separately from the new-charge integral.

`JointHashPrefix` supplies the concrete application, rather than assuming
a per-prefix numerical hash bound. The next fresh SHA-512 input contributes
the exact current key count divided by `2^512`. SHAKE starts and reads,
repeated hashes, and completed continuations contribute zero new collision
loss. Previously colliding histories keep risk one. The inherited-risk
integral is exactly the earlier collision probability, so the conditional
bounds telescope over actual mixed prefixes.

The resulting prefix and terminal collision bounds use the expectation
of the pathwise sum of these charges on the same execution. Truthful cache
updates are proved monotone, so collisions persist through later reads,
repeated calls, completion, and rejection represented by return values.
The event of a collision at any observation prefix is bounded by the
expected supremum of its prefix charges; that expectation equals the
supremum of prefix expectations. No global query cutoff, finite-mean
premise, or conditioning on successful verification is introduced.

The ledger is a probability-loss quantity. It is not attacker work, and
it does not yet imply the 128-bit expected-work contract. Compatible
prefixes for native unbounded samplers, accumulated native Merkle checkpoint
stability with actual checkpoint placement, lookup/PBS composition,
private-coin and chronological work coupling, exact numerical certification,
strict proof-byte decoding, and checked Rust/scheduler refinement remain
open. The end-to-end goal remains active and unproved.

repetition or request can begin. This is one shared child's challenge
batch; the outer PBS group scheduler and complete child body are not yet
compiled.

The request marker uses `NativeUsizeMessage`: standard bincode 2.0.1

reciprocal avoids zero and every pole of its own request's table compressed

## Raw native field representatives and wire encodings

Inspection of `sumcheck::batch::verify` confirmed that its ordered messages
and initial claims are serialized field objects. Canonical mathematical
field values cannot simply be serialized in their place: Goldilocks keeps
lazy u64 representatives, while BabyBear stores canonical Montgomery u32
representatives. This was a prerequisite for a faithful native scalar-batch
compiler; that verifier has not yet been compiled.

`NativeFieldRepresentation` defines the raw domains and their mathematical
values. For Goldilocks, one conditional subtraction is proved sufficient
for every u64, with exact agreement with the mathematical field value and
native canonical-comparison semantics. The raw word itself is retained.
For BabyBear, the natural-word model explicitly represents low-word masking,
wrapping u64 subtraction, high-word extraction and wrapping u32 correction
of `from_monty`. Its canonical output, radix congruence and mathematical
field value are proved. The conversion to/from the canonical Montgomery
word is a bijection. Relevant `new` and Montgomery-multiplier products are
proved to fit a u64. This is a proof of the stated natural-number word
semantics; checked Rust/instruction refinement and other field arithmetic
operations remain open.

`NativeIntegerPrefix` supplies a self-delimiting integer reader and counted
vector reader, with suffix-preserving left-inverse theorems on the standard
encoder and an injective vector encoding. These are structural helper
readers, not a strict canonical decoder for adversarial proof bytes. In
particular the helper reader may accept a wider spelling of a small value;
no full native deserializer-equivalence claim is made.

## Raw Goldilocks arithmetic for native lookup claims

`NativeGoldArithmetic` now retains the literal natural-word carry/borrow
steps of `modulus/goldilocks/ops.rs` for addition and subtraction. It proves
the output fits a u64 and gives the required prime-correction balance for
every pair of raw u64 representatives. Negation follows the native initial
canonicalization and returns a canonical result. Each operation is proved
to agree with the corresponding mathematical Goldilocks field operation.

Multiplication retains the u128 product, its u64/u32 decomposition, the
conditional subtraction of `EPSILON`, and the final native fast-add
correction in `reduce128`. The proof covers every u128 and establishes both
native safety preconditions: the conditional subtraction cannot underflow,
and the fast addition lies below `2^64 + p`. Its output fits a u64 and has
exactly the input's field value. These are proofs of explicit natural-word
semantics, not a checked extraction or assembly-instruction equivalence.

`NativeGoldExtensionArithmetic` applies the native coordinate loops for
extension addition, subtraction, negation and multiplication by a base-field
word. Basis-coordinate theorems prove their mathematical meanings. The
native coordinate-comparison predicate is equivalent to mathematical
extension equality; therefore the individual sumcheck recurrence is checked
without changing the raw storage or its serialized bytes. Its `tableSum`
retains the native ordered zip/fold, including shorter-input truncation,
and proves its mathematical sum of multiplicity-scaled inverse values.
The supplied inverse words have not yet been computed by a refined native
extension inversion algorithm.

A fixture using the pinned native Rust algebra crate checks all 49 pairs
from `{0, 1, 2^32-1, p-1, p, p+1, u64::MAX}` against modular arithmetic.
Nine pairs additionally supply literal raw addition/subtraction/product/
negation outputs for kernel regressions, including both correction paths
and lazy products. A native degree-three extension table sum supplies a
further raw-coordinate regression. Thus this layer can preserve the native
initial-claim bytes once its inverse-word producer is refined.

## Raw degree-three multiplication and inversion

`NativeGoldInverse` models the Goldilocks addition chain in
`modulus/goldilocks::try_inverse`, including its initial canonicalization
and the canonicalization inside every specialized `exp_acc` power-of-two
call. Repeated squaring has a general field-power theorem. The chain is
proved to compute exponent `p-2`, and Fermat's theorem identifies its value
with inversion on nonzero inputs. The explicit option-valued base inverse
fails exactly at semantic zero, including raw zero and raw modulus. This
is the stated natural-word model of the specialized operations; a checked
Rust/control-flow refinement of `pow_reduce` and the inversion chain remains
required. The remaining generic exponent paths have not yet been refined.

`NativeGoldCubic` retains every operation in the native Karatsuba product,
with constant seven, and proves its three coordinate formulas. The checked
basis is expanded as a polynomial in the adjoined root, whose cube is seven.
These results prove that the raw product denotes mathematical multiplication
in the degree-three lookup field, while preserving the actual lazy words.

`NativeGoldCubicInverse` retains the native determinant, adjugate and final
left scalar multiplication. Their coordinate identities prove that input
times adjugate equals the embedded determinant. Irreducibility of `X^3-7`
rules out a zero adjugate on a nonzero input, and hence the scalar determinant
is nonzero. The literal base addition chain therefore succeeds and the
result denotes the inverse extension value. Division first performs this
inverse and then the native right multiplication; its successful result is
proved to denote field division. `none` represents a failed arithmetic
precondition: unchecked Rust inversion panics there. It is not claimed to
be a graceful native verifier rejection. The accepted nonzero-domain theorem
avoids that path.

A fixture using the pinned Rust algebra crate supplies raw base inverse
outputs for eight boundary words, including both zero representatives, and
raw Karatsuba and inverse outputs for seven degree-three vectors with
canonical and lazy coordinates. The native fixture checks each nonzero
inverse by multiplication. Kernel regressions reproduce all captured words
and the explicit failed arithmetic precondition. They do not normalize
results before comparison, so equality of field values alone cannot make
these regressions pass.

These modules complete the explicit natural-word Goldilocks cubic arithmetic
needed by the lookup compression and reciprocal producers. Linking those
producers to the existing sampler, helper and table-sum compiler is next;
the independent common-challenge scalar batch and optimized interpolation
still require refinement. BabyBear arithmetic, full protocol/PBS/commitment
composition, checked Rust/scheduler correspondence, unbounded chronological
attacker-work coupling, strict proof-byte decoding, numerical losses and the
final application 128-bit security theorem remain open.

The native Goldilocks reciprocal policy evaluates `EF::one() / denominator`.
Its producer must retain the final Karatsuba multiplication by one in
`divResult`; byte equality with the raw `inverseResult` alone has not been
established. This distinction matters when linking the new arithmetic to
serialized helper/claim values.

## Exact retained draw positions supply raw lookup inputs

`NativeLookupDrawHistory.Roles` identifies the complete ordered records,
not only their mathematical values. During compression the history is empty.
During reciprocal sampling it is the compression draw followed by exactly
`rejected` offset draws. On completion the last accepted offset is appended.
The first record's value is y, the last record's value is r, every middle
offset fails the actual fixed-table acceptance predicate, and the middle
length equals the rejection counter. Coefficient states, consumed chunks,
receipts and all rejected draw records are retained in that same list.

The invariant is proved for initialization, every actual sampler tick and
every resumed execution. An independent batch invariant lifts it through
request markers, zero-repetition requests, active jobs, completion and the
ordered batch execution. The existing sampler and batch programs are
unchanged. It is not an assumption supplied on an arbitrary execution.

`NativeGoldLookupProducer.sourceWords` reads the first and last coefficient
records only after the control has finished. Its checked constructor requires
exactly three canonical coefficients. The sampler's existing field invariant
proves those conditions, their exact raw spelling and their mathematical
values. The success theorem also identifies each raw coordinate with the
corresponding stored first/last coordinate. Intervening rejected offsets
cannot be mistaken for either input.

The producer then reconstructs the native raw powers, last power update,
compressed table, additive denominators and individual `one / denominator`
outputs. `executed_success` starts from the actual batch initializer and
derives both validity and history roles from execution. It no longer takes
raw y/r inputs, value-equality premises, a nonzero-domain certificate or a
reciprocal-value certificate. Its successful output has the sampler's exact
y/r values, powers, table and reciprocal values. `executed_tableSum` feeds
that actual output vector to the raw public table sum. The remaining raw-row
relation explicitly identifies the trusted public request's mathematical
rows with the supplied native raw rows.

This is a deterministic reconstruction/refinement view of retained native
arithmetic state. It does not execute an extra native arithmetic pass or
establish the time/cost of the original computation. Placing and charging

Likewise an absent decoded result on an unfinished analysis state is not a

## Raw helper construction and the packed PCS source

`NativeGoldHelper.fill` copies the selected raw extension words, stops at
capacity, and pads remaining cells with raw extension zero. Accessed invalid
indices are explicit failed preconditions; unread trailing indices are
ignored. Its exact copy/truncate/pad theorem and length theorem hold on the
actual result. Mapping the output words to the degree-three field is proved
to equal the existing `NativeLookupHelper.fill`, including failure paths.

The raw coefficient packer copies all three stored Goldilocks coordinates
in declared basis order and appends raw zero lanes. Every row-major address
is proved to return its exact raw word. Packing with width at least three is
injective on raw extension objects; equal field values cannot be substituted
for equal storage. Its field projection is exactly the old basis coefficient
packer for all widths, with the checked constructor enforcing adequate width.

`NativeGoldHelperPrepared` retains the existing 64-bit helper geometry checks,
explicit geometry/index errors, and the actual raw flat storage. Successful
preparation has exactly `2^numVars * width` words below the 64-bit size limit,
and its projected table satisfies the existing packed-table validity
predicate. Both raw building and preparation project to the old semantic
constructors. The initialized-execution composition theorem supplies the
actual raw reciprocal vector from the sampler's retained first/last draws;
no caller-provided inverse-value certificate is needed for this comparison.

The PCS query theorem evaluates the actual successfully filled raw helper
through its projected row-major source and returns the same encoded extension
MLE as the existing query proof. An accepted wrong extension claim therefore
forces a wrong base-field PCS claim, including the zero-variable post-map
case. This constructor specifies honest helper generation. It does not
restrict adversarial committed padding to zero; the existing PCS interface
for arbitrary unused lanes and adversarial source interpretation remains
necessary for application soundness.

The Rust fixture directly calls the pinned public
`snarks::packed_extension::table` constructor after evaluating the literal
native copy loop. It confirms meaningful lazy coordinates are retained and
padding lanes are raw zero. It also checks native geometry errors and an
unread invalid trailing index. The resolved `concrete-ntt` commit matches
the pinned native lockfile. Kernel regressions reproduce its raw filled and
packed vectors, and cover an accessed invalid index, geometry-first failure,
constant helpers, the variable-count/multiplication overflow boundaries,
and distinguish raw zero from raw modulus after packing.

Preparation is a checked natural-word model. Its explicit preflight errors
do not claim Rust panic/error-order correspondence. These are pre-row-code
helper words, not encoded Merkle-column bytes: row-code/NTT refinement,
column layout, hashing and actual helper commitment construction remain open.
The source/query arithmetic results alone do not establish a committed
helper or authenticate a malicious prover's values.

## Scalar-batch statement and round-message wire encodings

`NativePrefixCodec` composes raw usize words, products, bounded vectors and
fixed-degree sequences using suffix-preserving prefix left inverses. Each
constructed encoding has a unique decoded value and following suffix; in
particular its encoder is injective. The codec structures carry their
encoding-law proofs, and the concrete combinators are audited along with
the public theorems. Vector counts retain the native 64-bit usize bound.

`NativeScalarBatchWire` gives the exact Goldilocks payloads used by
`sumcheck::batch::{bind,challenge}`. `PolynomialInfo` writes maximum
multiplicands before number of variables. The statement tuple contains a
separately counted info slice and claim slice. Each extension value retains
its degree-three sequence prefix and three raw u64 coordinates. A round
packet contains the raw usize round index and counted ordered prover
messages; each single-field `ProverMsg` contributes its counted evaluation
vector. Borrowed message references introduce no additional wire wrapper.
Lazy Goldilocks coordinates are retained throughout.

The statement and round encoders are injective and their structural readers
preserve arbitrary following bytes on constructed messages. Binding either
payload to the existing native framed transcript is also injective at fixed
prior transcript input, under the explicit native frame-byte length bound.
A vector-count bound alone is not claimed to bound total encoded payload
bytes. These input-binding theorems do not assert collision freedom of
oracle outputs or global disjointness from other oracle-input roles.

The isolated Rust fixture directly serializes the pinned public
`PolynomialInfo` and `ProverMsg` types in the same borrowed tuple/slice forms
used by the private batch functions. It confirms the complete statement and
round payloads, wide usize metadata, separate counts, empty evaluation
messages and empty packet layouts. Kernel regressions reproduce every
captured byte. Suffix-preserving structured round trips use the proved
left-inverse laws and those independently checked byte encodings; deciding
equality of the dependent record objects directly hits Lean reduction limits.

These are payload encoders and structural readers. They do not implement or
validate the batch's native proof-shape/degree preflight, independent

The encoding fixtures deliberately include empty messages which native
preflight would reject. The readers may accept a wider integer spelling of
zero, as the regression records; they are not a strict-canonical proof-byte

## Scalar-batch preflight and checked round extraction

`NativeScalarBatchPreflight` now models the verifier's ordered front end.
It checks proof/metadata shape first, then the empty-batch case, metadata
dimensions, and interpolation-node collisions, before binding any statement
bytes. The error categories remain separate. The native usize `degree + 1`
overflow check is retained before evaluation-vector length checks. Successful
shape is characterized by a `Forall₂` relation between every trusted info
and its proof instance, including all round counts and evaluation counts.

The actual consecutive-node loop uses raw extension addition by one and
canonical field-zero comparison after every addition. Its theorem covers
all intermediate nodes. Starting from raw zero it accepts exactly degrees
below the Goldilocks characteristic. The characteristic follows from the
injective base-field algebra map into the checked degree-three extension.
Positive-degree and common-variable-count conditions follow from successful
preflight; no interpolation domain or degree certificate is supplied by the
caller. There is no introduced runtime iteration cap or replacement fast
range check. The characteristic boundary regression uses this universal
loop theorem rather than evaluating a characteristic-sized loop.

Each recurrence reads the first two actual message evaluations and compares
their raw sum using native semantic equality. The checker is the ordered
zip of these independent checks. Under the validated length invariant it is
exactly a `Forall₂` assertion checking every claim, and compensating errors
in two claims are rejected. Its round-binding helper rejects before any
round-message absorption. These are phase helpers, not a complete verifier:
standalone zip checks still have native truncation semantics, and the full
round driver must retain the proved count invariant after interpolation.

`NativeScalarBatchRoundPacket` extracts each instance's actual round-th
message with an explicit failed-access result and no default message.
Accepted preflight and an in-range round prove extraction succeeds in
statement order, its packet count fits usize and equals the claim count,
and each equation has the validated evaluation width. Positivity then
proves the first-two-entry access is safe for every matched equation.

The isolated native fixture directly calls pinned public
`sumcheck::batch::verify` with the classical extension transcript. It covers
shape-error priority, empty batch, wrong evaluation count, zero variables,
zero degree, claim-count mismatch, degree overflow, inconsistent variables
and compensating false claims. It compares subsequent challenge bytes with
a reference transcript having the expected statement prefix: preflight
failures have no binding, while recurrence failure retains only the statement
binding. A valid two-equation run returns one common point, the expected
linear evaluations and the matching transcript continuation. A separate raw
addition confirms that the first characteristic wrap is stored as raw modulus
and nevertheless compares equal to zero.

Kernel regressions cover the corresponding front-end guards, exact bound
input on success, lazy-zero node detection, the characteristic boundary,
independent rejection despite equal total sums, and ordered/failed round
extraction. They observe error tags and input bytes, avoiding equality tests
on transcript function fields. These tests and front-end theorems do not
establish optimized interpolation, the actual common-challenge/interpolation
loop or terminal authentication. Those are next, together with the scalar
batch's arithmetic/soundness composition.

## Literal scalar interpolation and raw field interpretation

`NativeInterpolationCore` now models the pinned private
`sumcheck/src/verifier.rs::interpolate_uni_poly` operation order: the
consecutive-node scan and early return, difference/product accumulation,
factorial loop, and descending interpolation accumulator. The numerator is
left-associated exactly as in Rust. The last interpolation step does not
perform the nonfinal denominator/counter updates. The factorial retains its
last counter update. The model has no replacement Lagrange evaluator,
normalization, default array entry or runtime cap. Empty input, missing
entries and failed inversion are explicit `none`; the corresponding native
unchecked precondition fails by panic rather than graceful rejection.

The core's homomorphism theorem preserves the complete partial result for
any arithmetic interpretation preserving every primitive, including
Boolean equality and partial division. Intermediate scan, factorial and
reverse-state maps are proved separately. A successful scan's node index
lies in the tested interval; an off-node scan retains exactly one difference
per input evaluation. Zero-node return preserves the original stored word.

`NativeInterpolationField` supplies ordinary field operations with checked
zero division and proves both factorial state components equal the natural
factorial and the next counter. `NativeGoldInterpolation` instantiates the
core with the proved raw lazy Goldilocks operations, exact Karatsuba cubic
multiplication and native cubic inversion/division. It proves raw equality
matches field equality and that all semantic-zero cubic representatives
fail inversion. Together with the nonzero inversion theorem, this gives a
total, branch- and failure-preserving division interpretation. The resulting
`interpolate_value` theorem maps the entire raw computation to the same
literal field loop, with no success certificate or nonzero-denominator
premise supplied by the caller. This is representation refinement; the
field loop's Lagrange/polynomial correspondence and nonfailure under valid
node conditions remain open.

An isolated Rust fixture includes the actual interpolation and factorial
function bodies extracted verbatim from the pinned verifier source; it
does not reimplement them or modify Rust. Its nine vectors cover linear,
cubic, quartic and degree-seven messages, node and off-node challenges,
lazy-zero and near-u64-maximum coordinates, and the diagnostic singleton
case (rejected by the batch front end). It additionally checks every node
of each tested message vector returns the exact stored raw word. Lean
kernel regressions reproduce all nine outputs, empty-input failure, and
all eight degree-seven node results. Off-node expectations retain raw
coordinates above the modulus. Agreement of these fixtures is regression
evidence, not a formal refinement of Rust source or machine work.

## Interpolation safety follows from actual preflight

`NativeInterpolationSafety` now proves a precise field description of the
literal scan. Its retained list is exactly the consecutive differences
`point - j`, including the zero node, its product is their product and its
check counter is the final node. A successful off-node scan rules out
zero in every retained difference. The preflight's condition that every
positive cast through the degree is nonzero implies a nonzero factorial.

The descending loop's safety proof maintains its actual remaining-node
counter and nonzero `up` accumulator. The count relation ensures that every
nonfinal multiplication by the negated counter is nonzero. It proves every
list access and division succeeds; no product/nonzero assertion or success
certificate is supplied by the interpolation caller. Combined with the
scan index bounds, this proves the whole literal field interpolation is
total for every challenge whenever its input is nonempty and its node
range passes the native check. The proof covers singleton diagnostic
inputs as well as all positive degrees accepted by the batch verifier.
There is no runtime cap or restriction to lookup degrees 1, 3 and 4.

The same checked node condition makes consecutive casts injective. At
every node the actual scan takes the matching early return, and field
interpolation returns exactly that received entry. These are proofs about
the literal implementation, rather than only the mathematical interpolant.

`NativeGoldInterpolationSafety` transports totality back through the full
raw-to-field interpretation. Its raw known-node theorem transports the
scan branch itself, so it proves exact original-word return, including
lazy challenge and evaluation representatives; semantic equality of the
result alone would not justify that claim. No canonicalization is inserted.

The bridge obtains nonzero casts from `nodesFrom_iff`, not an independent
characteristic or denominator certificate. Successful actual dimensions
and a matched message width therefore imply raw interpolation succeeds.
The ordered-round theorem combines actual proof shape, dimensions and
in-range extraction: the resulting packet has exactly the claim count and
every equation interpolates successfully at any common challenge. The
regression consumer derives those preconditions directly from a successful
`beginVerify` result. These theorems do not assume a completed round driver.

Regression consumers cover arbitrary raw messages and challenges through
the full characteristic-sized node range without evaluating or imposing a
cap on a characteristic-sized validation loop, exact arbitrary raw node
returns, and the actual preflight/round packet connection. A kernel test
also retains failed standalone inversion for a malformed reverse step;
valid preflight execution is proved to avoid that failure.

The off-node loop's Lagrange/polynomial correspondence remains open.
Safety and representation refinement do not establish it. Subsequent
work must prove that correspondence, implement and connect the actual
common-challenge round driver and terminal authentication, then complete
scalar-batch soundness. Full lookup/PBS extraction, checked Rust/scheduler
and strict decoder refinement, BabyBear arithmetic, chronological
attacker-work coupling, numerical certification and the final 128-bit
application security theorem also remain open.

## Literal scalar interpolation has polynomial semantics

The previously open off-node interpolation correspondence is now proved.
`NativeInterpolationWeights` identifies the signed factorial denominator
with the product of consecutive-node differences omitting its own node,
and hence with Mathlib's Lagrange nodal weight. The adjacent-index identity
matches both native updates, `up *= -remaining` and `down *= index`,
without replacing either update by an inverse operation. These identities
cover every degree admitted by the node check, with no restriction to the
current lookup degrees.

`NativeInterpolationAccumulator` keeps both actual denominator accumulators
in the execution. Its invariant is `up = down * denominator(index)` with
nonzero `down`. The exact nonfinal counter updates preserve that invariant.
Each checked division is proved equal to its barycentric summand only in
the mathematical interpretation; the literal raw operation order remains
unchanged. Induction over the actual descending loop proves the final
result is the initial accumulator plus the complete finite partial sum.
The final-index early stop is included, and there are no default entries,
iteration caps or caller-supplied evaluation correctness certificates.

`NativeInterpolationPolynomial` constructs a polynomial directly from the
received evaluation list and its validated width. Its natural degree is
at most the trusted degree, and it takes the received values at every
node. The actual scan's retained product equals the nodal polynomial's
evaluation. The descending-loop sum therefore equals the barycentric
Lagrange evaluation at every off-node point. Combining that theorem with
the scan's known-node branch proves the whole literal field interpolation
returns the constructed polynomial's evaluation for every challenge.

`NativeGoldInterpolationPolynomial` transports the result through the
full raw Goldilocks representation theorem. The complete partial raw
computation maps to `some` of the received polynomial's evaluation. No
successful execution, independently bounded polynomial or nonzero
denominator certificate is a premise. The node condition comes from the
literal native `nodesFrom` check. The first-two-entry raw recurrence is
proved equivalent to `P(0) + P(1) = claim` in the extension field. Successful
actual dimensions supply all positivity and node conditions for every
matched equation, giving both its derived degree bound and its actual raw
interpolation semantics.

Kernel regressions recompute two native Rust off-node golden vectors
(linear and cubic, including lazy coordinates and a near-u64-maximum
input), and then use the new theorem to identify those outputs with the
received polynomial's evaluation. Universal regression consumers cover
arbitrary messages and challenges throughout the full characteristic
range, and combine actual successful metadata, derived degree bounds,
raw interpolation and the native polynomial recurrence.

This closes the scalar interpolation arithmetic/polynomial correspondence,
not the entire scalar verifier or its soundness proof. The actual
common-challenge round driver, ordered updated claims and terminal
authentication still need implementation and composition. Full lookup/PBS
extraction, remaining helper/PCS bodies and child/parent linking, checked
Rust/scheduler and strict decoder refinement, BabyBear arithmetic,
chronological attacker-work coupling, numerical certification and the
final 128-bit application security theorem remain open.

## Actual common-challenge scalar verifier loop

`NativeScalarBatchUpdate` now implements the native expected-vector mutation
through a zip with the actual round messages. A missing message leaves the
remaining expected entries untouched; extra messages are ignored. These
malformed-state semantics are retained rather than replacing the loop by
a potentially truncating map of messages. Successful updates preserve the
original expected length. Under the validated count equality, a `Forall₂`
theorem proves each message updates exactly its corresponding output in
statement order. Interpolation success follows from the existing actual
preflight/message safety theorem.

`NativeScalarBatchVerifier` compiles the complete raw independent-scalar
round driver into the existing online oracle program. It runs actual
preflight, collects the actual ordered round messages, checks every
recurrence before any round binding, binds the native round packet,
starts the typed scalar request with the Goldilocks degree-three descriptor
and native challenge label, collects actual canonical coefficients, decodes
their raw word and performs literal interpolation updates. Only then does
it append the one shared challenge to the point and advance the round.
Finished output maps every ordered expected value to a subclaim carrying
a clone of that same point. These are unauthenticated subclaims, exactly
as in native `batch::verify`; caller-side terminal authentication is not
silently supplied by this model.

The machine retains active coefficient readers, rejected chunks, receipt
state and completed-round records. A completed-round record stores the
actual packet, canonical challenge coefficients, raw challenge and prior
and updated expected vectors; it adds no native transcript frames. One
analysis tick drives one candidate while sampling. Prefix exhaustion
returns the active machine instead of a native rejection, and the exact
execution-addition theorem resumes without repeating completed requests
or receipts. Program execution is proved equal to the direct interpreter,
and every compiled prefix has the existing counterfactual replay property.
Native rejection and finished states stutter without further queries.

`NativeScalarBatchVerifierInvariant` proves the expected count, trusted
round bound, ordered completed challenge list, and common point throughout
arbitrary analysis prefixes. Active requests retain the actual packet
widths/count, passed individual recurrence checks and canonical sampler
validity. From successful real preflight, all internal checked-model
failures are unreachable: any failed execution is specifically a native
individual-recurrence rejection. Finished runs return exactly the original
claim count, every subclaim has the same point, and that point has the
trusted number of variables. The explicit internal access/decode/inversion
failures are checked precondition failures, not additional reachable native
rejection paths.

Kernel regressions cover two equations across two actual rounds, updated
claims and their common point, exact observation counts, rejection of a
second-round recurrence before binding or challenge, an all-rejecting oracle
retained as a pending request at prefix exhaustion, and rejection followed
by successful canonical collection retaining the full consumed-byte sequence.
Malformed standalone zip cases retain the native untouched-tail/ignored-
extra behavior. A universal regression consumes successful `beginVerify`
and the no-internal-failure theorem without extra safety certificates.

A separate isolated fixture calls pinned public `sumcheck::batch::verify`
for two rounds and independent equations. Its reference transcript uses
the actual shared challenges and verbatim included private interpolation
body from the pinned verifier source. It compares exact raw subclaims,
common-point coordinates and transcript continuation. A corrupted second
recurrence rejects against the actual first-round interpolated claim and
retains exactly the transcript after round zero. This is native regression
evidence, not a checked Rust-to-Lean refinement or machine-work theorem.

Per-round polynomial meaning must still be connected to the retained
completed-round history and the soundness/extraction argument. Terminal
claims need authentication in the actual lookup/PCS caller. Full lookup/PBS
bodies and child/parent linking, checked Rust/scheduler and strict decoder
refinement, BabyBear arithmetic, chronological attacker-work coupling,
numerical certification and the final 128-bit application theorem remain
open. The driver and structural invariants do not establish those claims.

## Actual scalar history supplies the polynomial terminal contract

`NativeScalarBatchHistory` now derives a chained history from actual
initialized verifier execution. The chain begins with the statement's real
ordered claims. Each new link's prior expected vector is the preceding
link's output, its round ordinal is the prior history length, and its
packet is obtained from the actual submitted proof at that round. Every
completed record retains the passed independent recurrence checks, the
literal successful interpolation update, and the completed canonical scalar
request with its actual decoded raw challenge. Initialization, every tick
and every finite resumed prefix preserve this property. No caller supplies
a chain, trace correspondence or successful-draw certificate.

`NativeScalarBatchRoundMeaning` connects those operational records to the
received-vector polynomials. Every matched equation has the trusted degree
bound, its received polynomial satisfies `P(0) + P(1) = prior`, and the
actual interpolation output is `P(r) = next` at the retained common
challenge. The interface explicitly retains equal original counts for
infos, messages, prior claims and next claims, so its zipped per-equation
relation cannot silently omit a slot. The challenge is proved equal to
assembly of the actual completed coefficient list, with exact canonical
raw coordinates at every basis index.

`NativeScalarBatchContract` combines these results with the completed
verifier's structural invariants. Every successful actual run supplies
consecutive proof rounds of exactly the trusted variable count, a chain
from the original sums to the final ordered values, and exactly the
returned subclaims at the common point formed by those retained draws.
Every original equation remains present. The terminal output's expected
vector is the endpoint of that same chain; its common point has the trusted
length. The proof constructs the received polynomials and execution chain
from the run, rather than assuming independent semantic witnesses.

Kernel regressions observe both actual round packets, their exact prior
and updated raw claims, the consecutive ordinals and coefficient draws in
a two-equation/two-round execution. A finished-control tag from that run
then supplies the complete algebraic contract. Universal consumers cover
all actually completed records of arbitrary initialized prefixes, including
packet-source correspondence, and preserve the chain under a suspended
all-rejecting request. Consecutive ordinals are derived from initialization
without an externally supplied range assertion.

This closes the deterministic operational-to-polynomial history contract
for the scalar verifier. It is not a Fiat--Shamir probability bound or a
terminal authentication proof. The canonical shared lookup caller still
needs its actual helper equality and reciprocal-identity terminal guards,
source/helper query bridge and accepted PCS opening composition. The
existing source-independent terminal adapters are not substituted for those
bodies. Full lookup/PBS extraction and linking, checked Rust/scheduler and
strict decoder refinement, BabyBear arithmetic, chronological attacker-work
coupling, numerical certification and the final 128-bit application theorem
remain open.

whole loop to the already proved prefix-mask MLE, including zero count,

## Raw scalar lane maps and ordered checked matrix products

`NativeGoldLaneWeights` models the native low-point enumerated left fold,
retaining its original coordinate order, offset, raw accumulator and
shift-and-mask predicate. Its raw word embedding is proved not to wrap for
any validated lane. The existing matrix-square check derives the machine
lane bound and, for a power-of-two width, the required shift bound; no
arbitrary cap is added. The actual native bits are derived from the same
low-bit address equivalence used by `ExtensionQuery.nativeLanes`, so the
complete raw weight has the established tensor-weight meaning without an
external bit-decoding certificate.

`NativeGoldLaneMatrix` uses the ordered raw column-copy loop to store the
three weight coordinates for every original scalar lane. Only output rows
beyond the extension degree are left zero. Every original source column
participates, including columns ignored by helper extension projection.
The matrix's complete field meaning is derived from its actual payload and
equals the generic lane matrix with those native tensor weights. Applying
and projecting this actual matrix yields the weighted sum of all original
source entries, without an input-padding premise.

`NativeGoldMatrixProductLoop` models the exact native `a,c,b` loop order,
using the raw add/multiply operations. Its invariants show that each inner
loop updates every selected column once, later rows preserve completed
rows, and every final cell retains its ascending-c raw dot-product fold.
A row-major serialization theorem connects each finite-view write to the
corresponding single raw list-set write.

`NativeGoldMatrixProductPayload` then executes those same nested loops on
an actual square-length row-major payload. Every accumulator read carries
its proved address bound, and every list write preserves the full length.
Serialization commutes with each step, each nested loop and the complete
zero-initialized program. Thus the payload correspondence is derived
through execution rather than supplied as a final-matrix certificate.

`NativeGoldMatrixProduct` validates both original matrices against the
left matrix's width, reads each operand by bounded getters into its actual
payload, runs the literal row-major program, and performs the checked final
matrix construction. Malformed operands retain failure. The resulting
field matrix is left times right, in that order. Applying it makes the
right map act first, as required for the native first pair `M(weight) * L`.
These remain raw arithmetic/program models; instruction and scheduler
refinement is still open.

The matrix-product fixture covers widths 1, 2 and 4, lazy operands, malformed

`NativeSharedLookupPrelude` composes the existing initialized lookup sampler

root/job count agreement, actual equality machine and every raw point.
Its contract preserves the exact equality observations, while
`run_protocol` retains all lookup observations before them. Pure statement
construction adds no oracle calls. The ready statement has matching
infos/claims lengths, twice the original job count, and its child state is
the equality machine's actual final transcript.

## Shared preflight, proof dimensions and original-request bounds

`NativeSharedLookupPreflight` now models the numeric shared preflight in
native order: nonempty registry/requests, per-request column/slot bounds,
uniform logical geometry of every registry entry, ordered local gathering,
the existing numeric bind, common dimension/width comparison and checked
usize repetition addition. Computed binding records retain every original
request and source-slot copy, including aliases. Successful execution
identifies the accepted geometry with the original registry head and
preserves the independent helper-width-three option. Every original
request's logical bound and the full-point shift domain follow from its
computed binding. Physical PCS contexts are not equated by this numeric
registry test. Binding records are proof metadata, not extra native wire
payloads or a physical work metric.

The checked repetition count equals the actual expanded sampler-tag count.
No extra repetition cap or nonzero-total check is added. In particular,
zero repetitions can pass this isolated numeric window; earlier canonical
`Config` validation excludes them. Empty local sources return `none` in
the checked model, whereas native `sources[0]` requires the earlier
nonzero-column configuration domain. The matrix-square restriction is
still a later scalar-query check, not a preflight restriction.

`NativeSharedLookupProofShape` models the helper opening count followed by
the complete proof-dimension window: multiplicity/request and per-table
lengths, helper root/value counts, registry source-value count and every
source vector's width. Helper opening contents are not interpreted; the
openingCount argument represents their original vector length. Successful
checks pair all multiplicity vectors with the complete original request
list. Actual prepared tags supply original request-index bounds and exact
request getters. Consequently all multiplicity lookups succeed, initial
claims can be constructed, and helper/root/opening counts match the
actual prepared job count. Registry/proof dimensions also discharge all
original source-slot lookups and preserve complete vector width, aliases
and column count.

`protocol_complete` starts from the actual initialized lookup sampler and
the actual completed equality request. Numeric preflight and proof shape
checks supply the root/job, raw-producer and multiplicity domains needed
to construct a ready statement. No raw-word, order, root/job or getter
certificate is a theorem input. The explicit `2*jobCount < 2^64` premise
is the native infos/claims vector allocation domain; it is not a retry or
attacker-work bound. This module does not prove native allocation success
for unrealistically large vectors or add a machine-work cap.

`NativeSharedLookupPreflightLink` connects the same preflight and proof
values to the existing composed prelude and initialized scalar verifier.
It identifies the ready job, equality-point, metadata and helper counts
with the checked native repetition total. Every accepted terminal request
is looked up in the original request list, so its logical-prefix bound
holds at the actual returned scalar point, whose length is below 64. No
independent point-length, selected-bind or logical-prefix certificate is
supplied to this initialized-run linkage.

The native fixture compiles the exact extracted shared numeric preflight
body with the exact extracted numeric bind prefix and proof-dimension
window. Minimal records supply the fields/getters read by those windows;
context/framing operations are deliberately outside this fixture. It
checks ordered repeated slots, the last valid usize repetition total and
overflow, an unused registry entry with mismatched geometry, invalid slot/
column counts, empty inputs, zero repetitions in the isolated numeric
window and all seven proof-dimension failure branches. Kernel regressions
reproduce those outcomes, distinguish shape checks from raw value
validation, and instantiate the actual-run statement construction theorem.
These fixtures are correspondence evidence for the modeled windows,
not a checked Rust refinement or complete native caller/PCS verification.

## Backend value policies and gating child initialization

`NativeSharedLookupValues` now models the native used-slot construction and
proof-value validation window. Ordered slot marking retains every request,
including repeated slots, and its flags are true exactly for slots appearing
in the original requests. Earlier numeric preflight supplies index safety;
the checked model's out-of-bounds list updates are not a claim about native
indexing outside that domain. Earlier proof shape supplies complete source
coverage for the native zip loop.

The trusted backend selects the validation policy. Legacy non-hiding
Brakedown `Parameters<C>` retains the trait defaults: base-field value
validation accepts lazy representatives. The response backends for
PolyFRIM require canonical base values. This choice is an argument of the
compiler, not a proof field. Multiplicities and source values follow that
policy; helper extension scalars are always required to have canonical
coordinates. No extra canonical guard is added to the legacy backend.

Unused-source zeros use native field equality, not raw-word equality.
Consequently a lazy Goldilocks zero can pass in an unused legacy source
slot. A nonzero value fails in either policy, and a lazy helper zero fails
in either policy. Successful checking supplies semantic zero for every
unused supplied source coordinate and canonical coordinates for every
helper. With the canonical policy, unused zeros are also literally raw
zero. Original raw values and their wire spelling are retained throughout;
this validator does not normalize proof data.

`NativeSharedLookupValidated` gates the existing operational prelude on
both dimension and value checks. Successful execution supplies both
contracts and the actual original lookup/equality/statement run. Completed
valid runs still construct ready statements under the existing native
vector allocation domain. Rejected checks return no ready output and
issue no prelude observations.

The child-program entry places the actual initializer behind those gates.
Rejection skips its oracle calls entirely. Acceptance executes it once,
retains all of its observations before the prelude, and uses its actual
returned child state. Successful runs derive the full original prelude
contract from this same initializer execution; no parent/child transcript
equality certificate is an input. The stateful child-program entry additionally retains the initializer's
computed parent/private state alongside every ready result for later
finishing and authentication. Its source is identified with the actual
initializer output, without a supplied state-equality certificate. The
exact native multiplicity-bound child initializer and finish binding remain
to instantiate. Earlier PCS context/preflight framing is also separate.

The native fixture compiles the exact used-slot and value-validation
windows extracted from the shared caller, plus the actual legacy default
and unmasked PolyFRIM validation bodies. Native Goldilocks and extension
implementations perform the equality and canonicality checks; minimal
records/error wrappers provide the fields read by those windows. It
checks canonical values, lazy multiplicities, lazy used sources, lazy
unused zeros, nonzero unused sources and noncanonical helper coordinates
under both policies. Kernel regressions reproduce every outcome and test
that rejected gates skip an observable initializer, while accepted gates
preserve its issued observations even if sampling remains suspended.
This is correspondence evidence for the modeled window, not a full native
caller or Rust refinement theorem.

and statement-level helper-sum/identity meaning. Accepted helper/source

Rust/compiler and scheduler refinement, strict decoder refinement,
BabyBear arithmetic, chronological attacker work, numerical certification
and the final 128-bit application theorem remain open.

## Tuple configuration rebuilding and derived scalar metadata

`NativeTupleLookupConfig` now models the native tuple constructor and
backend normalization used by `canonical_config`. It derives columns from
the first row and checks positive logical length, width and repetitions,
rectangular rows, distinct semantic tuples, the rational-degree domain
and the excluded-reciprocal domain. Distinctness uses Goldilocks canonical
field keys; raw-distinct lazy aliases of the same tuple are rejected.
The model's redundant Request.columns field is recomputed: the actual
native Config stores no independent columns field.

Legacy Brakedown retains the original raw public words. Canonicalizing
response backends reduce those words before rebuilding the configuration.
Both policies preserve every row, row order/count, tuple width and
semantic field value. Normalization preserves constructor validity; it
never drops duplicates or repairs malformed tables. Successful rebuilding
also proves logicalLength is below the base-field characteristic, so a
positive native witness count cannot vanish merely by wrapping that
characteristic. The native reciprocal-domain lower bound is positive.
Natural arithmetic models the guards on native usize-sized inputs; this
is not a proof of Rust HashSet implementation or allocation behavior.

`NativeSharedLookupConfig` rebuilds the complete original request list in
order, retaining every slot descriptor, logical length and repetition.
Each output has a validated public table and its derived width. Its
semantic sampler action agrees with the original native num_columns
representation. This does not identify raw transcript inputs across
policies: the later request/context binding must use the actual rebuilt
raw public tables. Constructor positivity and the checked native
repetition total rule out the isolated numeric preflight's zero-job case.

`NativeSharedLookupMetadata` connects those rebuilt configurations to the
independent infos/initial-claims compiler and completed operational
prelude. Every info has the same positive bound dimension and degree one,
three or four; the fixed nodes are distinct in the base characteristic,
and degree+1 fits native usize. Actual prepared-job and claim lengths,
with positive repetitions, make the scalar batch nonempty. Consequently
all native scalar metadata and interpolation-node checks pass.

For actual completed prelude runs, scalar preflight now requires only
the original algebra proof's literal shape check. Its success returns
the actual statement-bound transcript; no nonempty-batch, metadata,
degree, node or transcript-equality certificate is independently supplied.
The final linkage consumes the actual backend-gated stateful child/
prelude execution from the preceding layer, preserving that same
initializer's returned child state and constructed statement.

## Typed shared proof data and concrete classical child

`NativeLookupRequestWire` models the native configuration and deferred request
field order, with nested vector length headers and original source slots.
Columns are derived from the table rather than serialized as an extra field.
The request codec has prefix and injectivity proofs; backend normalization
commutes with valid configuration rebuilding. Binding the first canonical
request message is injective under the native byte-frame length domains.
The remaining per-request PCS contexts and registry preflight frames are open.

`NativeLookupMultiplicityWire` derives the flat multiplicity vector from the
same grouped packet. Both native encodings retain their own length headers.
Different groupings may have identical flattened bytes, while the grouped
encoding distinguishes them. Bounds describe native vector/byte allocation
and encoding domains; they impose no retry or attacker-work cutoff.

`NativeSharedLookupProofData` supplies one typed proof containing multiplicities,
roots, algebra, source/helper values and backend opening packets. Its terminal
encoding has prefix/injectivity proofs. The backend opening packets remain
opaque and unauthenticated at this layer; structural codec readers do not
establish strict native deserialization refinement.

`NativeSharedLookupChild` absorbs grouped and flat multiplicities in native
order and executes the concrete classical detached extension fork, parent
checkpoint and direct zero-count extension identity. Its retained parent and
binding are computed by that execution. Projection preserves exact oracle
observations. The terminal-value message is encoded from the same proof.
Finishing with the retained parent succeeds exactly when the child profile
matches; this uses the actual checkpoint and does not assume checkpoint
injectivity. Successful finishing clears the returned child's binding; it
does not prohibit cloning an earlier immutable state.

The gated launcher uses this initializer with shape/value checks and opening
counts from that same proof. A successful launch establishes the original
lookup/equality execution from the initialized child, and connects rebuilt
configurations to scalar preflight on that proof's algebra packet.

An external native fixture imports the actual public request/configuration
and transcript types and extracts the actual child/finish wrappers. It checks
exact request, grouped, flattened and terminal bytes, seven seed/checkpoint/
identity observations, successful finishing and continuation, and rejection
when the parent advances. The 28 kernel regression examples reproduce these
bytes, observations, prefix reads, grouping distinction, normalization,
spent-binding behavior and pre-child value gates. Zero analysis fuel tests
suspension after initialization, not native verifier rejection. This fixture
omits per-request contexts and the lookup/algebra/PCS body and makes no full
proof-acceptance claim.

child finishing into one actual execution. PCS authentication and query
folding, lookup/PBS extraction, Rust/compiler and scheduler refinement, strict
decoder refinement, BabyBear, chronological work, numerical certification
and the final 128-bit application theorem remain open.
