## Ordered parent context hashing and preflight framing

`NativeByteCodec` provides raw u8, byte-vector and fixed-byte-array codecs.
Digest bytes have no sequence header. Byte vectors have one usize length
header and raw u8 entries, including values 251 through 255. Prefix-reader
proofs concern constructed values, not strict native proof deserialization.

`NativeBrakedownContext` builds the exact Goldilocks Brakedown context input:
the native domain bytes followed by the serialized tuple of decimal modulus,
number of variables, width, left variables, queries, row-code block width,
codeword blocks, row-code domain and complete row-code serialization. The
same parameter object supplies numeric geometry and metadata. Context calls
are actual common-domain hash-oracle programs, and repeated calls remain in
the observation log. Digests are not input certificates. Row-code accessors
and serialization are an explicit trusted interface; their instantiation and
Rust refinement, plus complete trusted-parameter validity, remain open.
A serialization failure produces no hash-oracle observation at this layer.

`NativeCanonicalLookupWire` encodes each bind tuple in native order:
configuration, degree three, helper context, then the vector of ordered
(context, commitment-root) pairs. The registry uses the native Brakedown
registry label and the same pair-vector encoding. No context equality is
inferred from equal numeric geometry. Payload and complete-message
injectivity retain native byte-frame allocation domains and make no
checkpoint-injectivity assumption.

`NativeSharedLookupParent` takes already rebuilt requests and executes the
native top-level dimension checks, request-list absorption, and each ordered
numeric bind, selected-source context computation, helper context computation
and bind absorption. Common-geometry checking and checked repetition addition
follow that message. Thus overflow retains the already absorbed bind message;
context serialization failure retains prior hashes but does not append that
request's bind message. Registry setup recomputes every source context before
absorbing the complete ordered registry. Alias-group construction and source
claim authentication remain separate; setup framing alone does not establish
an authenticated registry.

Successful framed steps, loops, preflight and complete preparation erase to
the existing numeric preflight on the same requests and source geometry.
Successful context collection preserves source count, so vector bounds used
when constructing framed payloads are native domains rather than work caps.
The new `begin` entry point passes the actual prepared parent into the prior
shape/value-gated child launcher with the native Brakedown retain policy.
Helper extension values still require canonical representations. Its success theorem identifies that actual
execution and derives numeric preflight. Rebuilt original configurations
then discharge scalar preflight on the same proof's algebra packet.
This does not yet execute the full scalar verifier, strict terminal guards,
terminal binding, child finishing and PCS checks in one combined body.

The external Rust fixture extracts the actual canonical `bind` and shared
`preflight`, calls the public `CanonicalOpeningBatch::new`, and uses actual
BlockReedSolomonCode/Parameters constructors. A Hash implementation records
exact inputs and delegates to standard SHA-512. The fixture uses sources with

context calls, and records the next native transcript request input. It also
checks repetition overflow after five hashes and both bind frames, initial
rejection without hashes/framing, and serialization failure after one hash
without a request bind frame. The 28 kernel examples reproduce metadata,
complete parent prefixes, exact hash inputs/outputs, these failure paths,
raw bytes, and integration into the actual child initializer. Zero sampling

## Composed child body and PCS boundary

`NativeSharedLookupBody` takes the actual ready prelude, retained child state
and single proof object into the existing scalar verifier. It distinguishes
scalar suspension from rejection and consumes only the verifier's returned
claims in strict terminal guards. Source variable count comes from the
original registry head; width comes from the computed shared geometry.
Terminal values are absorbed only after all guards pass, followed by the
actual typed child finish. Checked lineage failures prevent reaching the
bound result; the native wrapper uses `expect` on that path, so this is not
yet a Rust error/panic refinement theorem.

A `Bound` result is operational output before helper/source PCS checks.
Its contract identifies the executed scalar machine and returned claims,
the actual registry geometry, exact guard execution and successful finish.
Scalar completion derives its own initial preflight and first-info witness.
The existing independent scalar contract then supplies every sampled point
coordinate, per-equation recurrence/interpolation chain, original source
slots and sum/helper relation. Successful finishing spends the returned
child binding and has exactly four observations, retaining both the parent
checkpoint and child fingerprint even when oracle keys repeat. Terminal
guard failure emits no finish observations or terminal-value binding.

`NativeSharedLookupExecution` composes the parent/child entry point with
this body. The program accepts no supplied ready transcript, compiled
statement, point, terminal query or lineage certificate. Its success theorem
identifies the actual preparation and child execution and derives numeric
preflight. The terminal theorem derives every accepted original request's
logical-prefix bound and equality draw evidence at the actual computed
point, and proves the returned binding spent. The same proof provides
multiplicities, roots, algebra, terminal values and opaque backend packets.
Those packets have not been authenticated by this result.

A computational limitation is now explicit: the existing abstract
Goldilocks-extension lookup pole predicate reduces to a decision using
`Classical.choice`. Thus the complete abstract sampler is not directly
executable by a kernel `decide` regression. Its logical contracts remain
proved, but a computable raw unbounded retry machine and its refinement to
that abstract sampler are still required. This is additional native
execution/refinement work, not an assumption that any sampled pole is safe.
`NativeGoldLookupWords` supplies the computable accepted-draw producer:
actual coefficient records determine y/r, and powers, public compressed
table, pole check and individual reciprocals are computed without supplied
certificates. Its word-production function agrees exactly with the prior
producer when the actual source-word getter succeeds. This does not itself
implement the unbounded retry machine.

The external Rust fixture constructs an actual small Goldilocks Brakedown
lookup proof and passes the full native verifier, including PCS. It also
extracts the native canonical shared verifier prefix through finishing,
retaining actual private helper functions and native scalar/terminal code,
and records SHA-512 inputs/outputs, typed readers, returned scalar claims
and the parent continuation. Malformed algebra shape, recurrence tampering,
helper mismatch and reciprocal-identity tampering reject before finishing;
reader counts distinguish the pre-scalar and post-scalar failures.

The 15 kernel regressions reconstruct this fixture's accepted-first-offset
window using actual parent preparation, child creation, coefficient readers,
raw-word production and equality request/statement construction, then run
the new body. They check every native reader input through finishing,
exact scalar claims, the final parent continuation, spent binding,
suspension and the four rejection cases. The fixture window does not claim
to replace or execute the abstract sampler's unbounded retry loop. Backend
opening contents remain opaque in Lean; full native acceptance of the
fixture is not a Lean PCS-authentication proof. Large captured byte inputs
are chunked and declared noncomputable to avoid code-generator inlining;
the regression propositions are checked by the kernel at normal recursion
depth, without `native_decide` or new axioms.

## Computable raw lookup retries and exact projection

`NativeGoldLookupSampler` replaces the operational abstract-field pole
decision with the existing raw-word predicate. It retains the active
coefficient reader, canonical compression/offset words, powers and public
table, every completed draw including rejected offsets, and the offset
rejection count. A rejected coefficient stays in the same reader and at
the same coefficient index. A zero or pole offset is absorbed with its
receipt before another offset request starts. Neither path adds a native
retry cutoff; fuel specifies a resumable analysis prefix only.

Coefficient conversion is total by reduction modulo the field modulus.
It agrees with the abstract scalar interpretation for every input list.
On actual completed canonical coefficient collections it preserves every
original word exactly, with neither defaulting nor reduction. This conversion
applies to fresh challenge coefficients, not to retained Brakedown public
or proof base-field words.

Projection maps the raw selection into `NativeLookupChallenge` and preserves
the exact machine, complete coefficient records, rejected-draw count and
ordered oracle observations after initialization, each tick and any finite
analysis prefix. These are equalities for every world and budget, without a
freshness, probability, completed-draw or row-identification certificate.
The split-budget law retains state/logs across retries. The abstract
`Classical.choice` decision remains a mathematical specification; it is no
longer evaluated on the operational path.

`NativeGoldLookupBatch` preserves literal request ordinals and repetition
order, including request-binding frames. Its projection commutes with the
schedule, initial state, sample completion, each tick and any finite batch
execution. Raw row words map to their field interpretations only in the
abstract projection; runtime selection uses the original raw table.

`NativeSharedLookupPrelude.protocol` now executes the raw batch and compiles
its projection into the existing equality/statement preparation. Its public
`run_protocol` theorem still identifies exactly the same initialized
abstract batch execution and log. Thus all existing prepared-job, statement,
geometry, value-gate, terminal, scalar and child-finish contracts remain in
force through the same caller APIs. No separate ready transcript or
acceptance certificate was added to the full entry point.

The previous test-only accepted-first-offset reconstruction was removed.
All 15 native-fixture regressions now execute
`NativeSharedLookupExecution.protocol` directly for normal completion,

## Native PCS wire and concrete column authentication

`NativeGoldPcsWire` supplies exact constructed-wire codecs for a raw matrix
(width followed by its raw Goldilocks word vector), ordered zero/one matrix
pairs, query vectors, `(root, query, values)` binding payloads and
`(ordinal, slot, query, values)` deferred-claim payloads. The helper query
packer calls the actual raw coefficient-query construction and packs only
its PCS pairs. It proves packing succeeds under the existing native matrix
shape and usize count bounds and preserves every matrix. The local extension
post-map is absent from the PCS bytes, including for an empty point. Readers
are structural prefix inverses, not a strict adversarial native decoder.

`NativeHashOracleBridge` compiles hash-only VCVio computations into the same
causal mixed-oracle program used by the transcript, preserving their exact
result and ordered observations for every world. It proves truthful hash logs
replay their original computation from the projected common cache, also when
an arbitrary truthful earlier mixed log is present. Every repeated call is
retained in the log; repeated keys share one cache entry. Neither collision
freedom nor fresh hash inputs are assumed.

`NativeGoldColumnAuthentication` executes the raw whole-column hash and
bottom-up Merkle sibling loop. Its leaf bytes are the native column domain
followed by the original raw word-vector encoding; node bytes are exactly the
two ordered 64-byte digests. Paths include the claimed leaf first. Empty or
wrong-height paths fail without a hash, matching the outer PCS path-shape
gate; the standalone Rust `MerkleTree::check` relies on that gate. Digests use
an explicit byte-list equality decision, so the concrete checker reduces in
the kernel. For a decoded path the program is exactly the compiled existing
`NativeMerkleVerifier.verifyPayload`. Acceptance of a received column derives
a typed path and successful replay of that same payload/path in the common
cache projected from its actual earlier and column observations. No separate
replay or authentication certificate is an input.

## Native base-field and atomic column challenges

`NativePrimeRequest` models the classical typed prime request used by the
Brakedown base-field random linear test. It binds `typed request kind`
(scalar/vector), then `field challenge kind` (`prime vector`), with no
extension descriptor or multiplication table. It reuses the canonical field
collector, preserving every candidate, rejected chunk, suspended reader and
receipt. The count is a native usize; analysis fuel is not a native retry
limit. Completed requests have exactly the original count of canonical
values, and conversion to a raw Goldilocks word preserves each integer
exactly. Split execution/resumption retains the same request and ordered log.

`NativeIndexRequest` models the classical schedule-5 atomic index API. The
nonzero power-of-two domain and checked `count*8` guards precede any transcript
mutation or oracle operation. A valid request appends the raw eight-byte
little-endian domain, then issues one ordinary byte challenge of length
`count*8`. The complete ordered list comes from successive eight-byte words
masked by `domain-1`; it is retained separately from the sorted, deduplicated
transmitted indices. The adapter proves the original quota, every bound,
sortedness, no duplicates and exact original membership. Valid usize domains
also supply the bit bound needed by the finite-byte law. Invalid requests
produce no observations. Count zero still records its start and empty output.

For kernel evaluation, the executable ascending sort uses the library's
structural insertion sort. `distinct_eq_mergeSort` proves equality to the
existing merge-sort/dedup definition on every input, while sortedness and
membership proofs retain the same specification. This identifies the sorted
integer sequence; it is not Rust's `sort_unstable` instruction refinement.
The native whole-block decoder is identified with the typed with-replacement
positions used by the existing column-opening analysis, in literal word order.

`NativeAtomicIndexLaw` splits the whole byte block into discarded high bits
and retained low-bit positions at every word, by a bijection. It proves the
entire vector of positions is jointly uniform for a uniformly fresh block;
no per-word independence premise is supplied. The existing exact column
agreement probability then applies with the original quota, including
repeated positions. These are finite uniform-sample laws. Conditional
freshness in the actual adaptive transcript execution, including earlier
private/verification prequeries, remains a separate composition obligation.

`NativeGoldPcsWire` now also supplies the exact pair-of-vectors response
codec and its kind-1 `mw linear responses` binder. Its original raw words
and both vector headers precede the atomic index request. The native fixture
`/tmp/hasteboots-pcs-challenge-fixture` records a base-field vector, those
responses, atomic draws, sorted indices and the following parent challenge.
It separately records scalar requests, empty prime/index requests, a
one-column domain, and invalid domains/overflow with unchanged continuation.
It invokes the actual native public transcript APIs. This checks the atomic
API, not the trusted caller's feature-flag selection.

## Native single-opening parameter, binding and random-test prefix

`NativeBrakedownParameters` models the checked `Parameters::new_encoded`
constructor for the selected 64-bit machine model. The original code object
supplies message length, block count and block width, together with the same
row description already used by its parameter context. The basic dimension
and query-count guards precede exponentiation; code-message/stride checks
precede checked table, encoded-matrix, linear-test and Merkle-tree sizes.
The returned geometry and native random-test count are computed data.
The constructor proves that the next power-of-two leaf count minimally covers
the code blocks and that every accepted path length is below 64.

No atomic-only domain or quota constraint is added to this constructor. The
native constructor can accept a non-power-of-two code length and very large
nonzero query counts; the atomic index API checks its separate domain and
`count*8` bounds later. Geometry accessors do not certify a code's distance,
encoder correctness, serialization or actual native parameter instantiation.

`NativeGoldPcsOpening` supplies the original non-hiding single-opening record:
raw test/evaluation vectors followed by a vector of raw columns with complete
leaf-first paths. Its codec matches the native struct order and has a proved
constructed-wire prefix inverse. Outer shape gates check both response lengths,
a nonempty column list, the `min(queries, blocks)` cap and every column's value
and path lengths. No column authentication is performed by this shape gate.

`NativeGoldPcsBinding` checks the original query/value counts and every actual
zero/one matrix before computing the code context in the common hash oracle.
Only a successfully serialized context contributes its hash observation.
The original digest, commitment, ordered matrices and raw values are then
appended under the native two binding labels, with kind-1 frames. The digest
is computed from the same parameter object, not supplied as a certificate.
Invalid shapes or code serialization fail before any oracle observation.
`NativeSharedLookupHelpers.completed_binding_checks` now derives that every
helper call from the actual completed lookup run passes these native binding
shape checks. Its matrices and coefficient vectors are computed by the caller.

`NativeGoldPcsPrelude` composes parameter initialization, proof-shape checks,
binding and the actual base-field random-test sampler. It accepts no prepared
geometry, bound parent or randomness certificate. Its returned `sampling`
state retains the actual sampler and computed geometry, including analysis
suspension. Rejection and suspension remain distinct. Successful finished
states have exactly `rows*width` canonical samples, with exact raw Goldilocks
conversion. The execution theorem preserves binding observations before field
sampling. Parameter initialization here represents native construction before
verification; it does not claim Rust repeats its constructor at each opening.

## Native raw PCS weights and suffix folding

`NativeGoldMatrixAccumulate` computes the native `Matrix::add_mul` row loop
with its original accumulator. Its field projection is the previous output
plus the matrix-vector product. In particular, the one-branch fold starts
from the actual raw output of the zero-branch fold; replacing that execution
by two independently zero-initialized products can change lazy representatives.

`NativeGoldMatrixWeights` executes `matrix_weights` on raw query matrices.
The initial identity has literal raw zero/one entries, with checked-square
rejection before allocation. Each round emits all zero products before all
one products, and each later query matrix acts on the left. Valid queries
produce exactly `2^query.length` validated matrices. Every output product's
field projection, and the complete expansion's projection from identity,
are proved against the same ordered semantic expansion. Identifying this
native prefix expansion and its flattened layout with the existing semantic
Boolean-cube tensor remains a composition obligation.

`NativeGoldPackedFold` computes checked packed-table folding and evaluation,
including the native constant-lane optimization. The shortcut compares field
values via the proved canonical-word equality test, while preserving cell
zero's original words. No constant flag or semantic-table certificate is
supplied. Successful folds preserve table validity, decrement the variable
count by exactly one and retain the width. A completed checked evaluation
returns exactly that width's number of words.

`NativeGoldPackedMeaning` proves the raw fold's field interpretation. The
rectangular flattening lemma recovers each original raw cell at its native
address. The computed constant predicate proves the first cell is equal in
the field to every selected input, including inputs with different lazy
representatives. Both fold branches therefore refine the same adjacent-cell
matrix-vector operation. The complete raw loop and checked evaluation refine
the existing `FlatMatrixFold.foldAll` on the actual payload and actual query
matrices, with the least significant variable eliminated first.

`NativeGoldPcsArithmetic` copies prefix weights in lane/left-cell/source-lane
order and transposes the lane-major response without normalization. The
structured constructor's successful size is `width*(2^leftVars*width)`.
Its checked finishing wrapper exposes the native private routine's existing
constructor/query/response preconditions; it does not add a verifier
acceptance claim. `finish_value` proves that the computed suffix output is
exactly the existing flat MW-MLE fold of the original lane-major response.
`finish_length` proves its final width. Native in-place writes, allocation
behavior and Rust instruction refinement remain separate obligations.

## Native Goldilocks scalar NTT and response encoding

`NativeGoldSolinas` models the canonical arithmetic used by concrete-ntt's
`PrimeModulus for Solinas` at locked revision
`cdeba793e46208320b30d78be19f7be78d49016a`. This is distinct from algebra's
lazy Goldilocks arithmetic: add/subtract return canonical words, and the
wide-product reduction retains the source's two wrapping corrections.
`reduce_spec` proves that reduction returns a canonical representative for
every 128-bit input. The field interpretation of add, subtract, reduce,
multiply and the sequential power accumulator is proved in Lean. No integer
kernel result or transform-correctness certificate is supplied as an input.

`NativeGoldNtt` supplies functional buffers for the actual scalar forward
algorithm: bit-reversed twiddle writes, canonical input conversion,
breadth-first butterfly stages and depth-first recursion above the native
1024-element threshold. The complete plan twiddle table is retained when
recursing into sub-buffers. The size proofs cover every recursion branch;
valid-stage source-pair and twiddle-address bounds are proved, including
recursive depth/half offsets. Forward outputs have exactly the original
buffer length and all raw words are canonical.

The universal correspondence between this scalar execution and the existing
`NTTButterfly`/`NTTBlockEncoder` field evaluation/code is supplied by the next
implementation layer below. Successful buffer construction alone does not
establish code membership: the actual root must be primitive and the message
coefficients must fit the chosen code degree. Root discovery, plan/cache
instantiation, the Div64 implementation, SIMD dispatch/lane operations,
mutable buffer refinement and native work-cost coupling remain open.
The scalar model preserves the real radix-two dataflow and cutoff rather
than replacing its output with a polynomial evaluator.

`NativeGoldRowEncoding` computes block-RS rows and PCS response lanes from
the original raw inputs. Its checked wrappers expose existing successful
native plan/shape preconditions; `none` represents a failed precondition,
not a claim that native assertions return a verifier `Err`. The retained
code root is compared in the field with the trusted plan root before the
zero-row shortcut. The shortcut tests literal raw zero, proved equivalent
to native canonical-and-field-zero, so lazy zero inputs take the transform
branch. The Goldilocks wrapper canonicalizes the gathered coordinate buffer
immediately before the integer kernel, without changing the original response
bytes already used by transcript binding.

The gather handles each coordinate of consecutive input blocks, a partial
final block and all zero padding. `payload_get` proves the final
symbol-major scatter contains exactly the corresponding raw coordinate
transform output. Row encoding produces `2^logSize*blockWidth` canonical
words. Response encoding independently processes every packing lane's
exact-length message chunk and concatenates lane outputs. Its completeness
and shape theorems rule out truncation under the checked preconditions.
Neither API accepts encoded responses from the proof. The code/plan
configuration is trusted input; its construction and linkage to the original
serialized native code object are not yet established.

## Scalar NTT-to-code correspondence

The functional canonical scalar NTT now has a universal evaluation proof and
a block-RS code-membership proof. The operational encoder is unchanged:
its original twiddle initialization, breadth/depth loops and 1024-element
cutoff still compute the returned raw words. The proof does not replace that
computation with a polynomial evaluator or accept an encoder-correctness
certificate as a protocol input.

`NativeGoldNttTwiddles` proves bit reversal reverses concatenated bit blocks,
is involutive on valid addresses and makes distinct writes non-aliasing.
The actual ordered initializer therefore puts the exact computed power in
every reversed slot. Each lookup's field value is the corresponding power
of the actual root, including the first twiddle of every recursive subtree.
These facts hold for arbitrary roots; no table-correctness premise is used.

`NativeGoldNttStages` proves contiguous-half separation for lower butterfly
stages, retaining stored-word equality. `NativeGoldNttSchedule` extends this
to all remaining breadth-first rounds and proves both complete breadth-first
execution and the actual cutoff-based depth-first execution equal one
recursive raw butterfly tree. This covers every size, including recursion
above 1024; the tree is a proof intermediary rather than a substituted
operational transform.

`NativeGoldNttMeaning.tree_value` connects each actual tree output to the
existing `NTTButterfly.transform`, with coefficients from the original
buffer and the computed full-plan table. The proof derives child roots,
subtree twiddles, source slices and output addresses. `depthFirst_value`
and `forwardData_value` lift this to complete flat output vectors, including
raw-u64 canonicalization. For a primitive root of order `2^(logSize+1)`,
`forwardData_evaluation` and the checked `forward_evaluation` API theorem
prove evaluation on the native bit-reversed odd-root domain.

`NativeGoldRowMeaning` proves coordinate gathering and all zero padding equal
the semantic coefficient table, including partially filled input blocks.
The scalar transform and original symbol-major scatter therefore compute
`BlockEncoder.encode` on that table. The raw-zero shortcut is proved to
compute the same codeword; lazy zero inputs remain on their original
transform branch. A successful encoded row lands in `BlockCode.code`, the
same whole-symbol distance code used by the opening argument. The retained
code-root version derives its agreement with the actual plan root from the
successful encoder's root check.

`NativeGoldResponseMeaning` extracts every ordered row from the actual
successful response encoder. Each comes from its original exact response
chunk, and uniform flattening preserves the native lane-major addresses.
`encodeResponses_lanes` proves that every lane of the returned flat raw
vector equals the semantic encoder of those original coefficients and is
coded. `encodeResponses_retained_lanes` states this using the original
retained code root; the required plan-root equality is derived from actual
successful checks, not supplied as a cache-consistency certificate.

The code-membership theorems require a primitive actual root, a chosen
coefficient count `m` no larger than the domain and message length at most
`m*blockWidth`. These are explicit mathematical parameter conditions, not
an assumption that the scalar transform or encoder is correct. Deriving
them from the actual native constructor/cache and linking the trusted
configuration to its serialized code object remain open. Packing-lane count,
code-symbol width and the total interleaved dimension `blockWidth*m` stay
separate.

All earlier raw native golden examples are retained. Seven added proof
instantiations check the forward API, nonconstant/partial rows, the retained
root on a zero row, and membership/coefficient linkage for arbitrary
three-lane raw responses. Two private kernel computations validate the
actual native 32/64-point root literals before applying these theorems.
All 46 new public theorems have guarded audits using only `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The combined HasteBoots suite now has
2,646 guarded audits. Default heartbeat and recursion limits are unchanged.

`NativeGoldPcsColumns.protocol` still stops at the atomic column boundary.
Next is trusted code-object linkage and composition of this computed scalar
response encoding with raw column authentication, coordinate checks and
suffix/claim equality. Actual root generation/cache behavior, Div64 and
SIMD/instruction refinement are not proved by the scalar correspondence.

registry/alias/query folding, adaptive freshness/work coupling, lookup/PBS
extraction, production parameter/profile instantiation, strict decoding,
Rust/compiler/scheduler refinement, BabyBear, numerical certification and

## Retained block code and PCS response encoding

`NativeGoldBlockCode.Stored` retains the actual native struct fields in
serde declaration order: message length, symbol width, padded message-block
count, domain-block count, modulus string bytes and the raw domain root.
Its compositional prefix codec serializes the complete object, preserves raw
root spelling and has a proved prefix inverse and injective encoding.
`description` supplies parameter accessors and serialization from this same
object, replacing the earlier fixture-only accessor/serialized-byte pairing
in the new PCS entry point.

`build` models the native constructor arithmetic: nonzero message/symbol
width; power-of-two blowup at least two; overflow-safe ceiling division;
checked next power of two; checked domain multiplication; minimum domain 32;
and checked interleaved output size. Generation, initialization and root
loading are separate backend responses with distinct failures. The stored
root comes from the actual modeled load response. This is a functional
source model. The backend calls' implementation, mutable cache, allocation,
Rust machine operations and scheduling have not been refined into it.

`NativeGoldBlockCodeMeaning` proves ceiling coverage/minimality, least
power-of-two padding, the exact domain exponent and strict expansion.
Constructor success therefore derives the coefficient count and all padding
and output-size inequalities required by the scalar correspondence. The
Brakedown code-shape gate follows when the constructor message length matches
the native left/right split; no independently chosen coefficient count or
code-shape certificate is needed.

`primitive_log_upper` proves that a Goldilocks primitive root for degree
`2^(logSize+1)` forces `logSize <= 31`, since `2^33` does not divide `p-1`.
With a primitive retained root, the constructor's own loaded backend derives
root agreement and every scalar encoder precondition. Exact-size response
encoding is consequently total. `response_lanes` connects every returned
lane to the original response chunk and `BlockCode.code` at the constructor's
own `messageBlocks`, removing the earlier free degree/padding premises.
Root primitivity is still an explicit mathematical backend obligation;
it has not been derived from concrete-ntt's repeated-square-root discovery.

`NativeGoldBlockCodeContext` computes the complete native parameter metadata
and hash input from the retained object. Structural injectivity of that input
recovers all parameter fields and the complete stored code, including the
padded coefficient count, modulus bytes and raw root. This is injectivity of
hash inputs, not a claim that hash outputs are collision-free. The structural
prefix readers are not a strict adversarial Rust decoder refinement.

`NativeGoldPcsEncoding.protocol` continues the original checked single-opening
PCS prefix through response encoding after the distinct column count check.
The exact same retained object supplies context bytes and encoding geometry.
A loaded plan root is obtained from the backend; both response vectors are
computed by the original scalar encoder, never passed in as certificates.
The prior random state, structured weights, sampled indices and observation
trace are preserved. Loading/encoding unavailability models the native trusted
cache/assertion boundary separately from verifier rejection or analysis
suspension. The functional backend response is shared at the retained size;

`columns_complete` derives both response shapes from the actual checked

vectors are coded and have coefficients from their original exact chunks.
This is an encoding boundary, not PCS acceptance. Column authentication,

## Raw column workers and checked PCS preparation

`NativeGoldColumnChecks` computes the original lane/coordinate loop from raw
Goldilocks words. Products and ascending left-to-right accumulation use the
verified lazy u64 arithmetic; equality compares canonical field values, as
native Goldilocks comparison does. Every dot product is proved equal to its
semantic row sum and to the existing `NativeColumnLayout.dot`. The complete
boolean loop is equivalent to both coordinate equation families. Native
indexing preconditions are explicit as `Shape`; `addresses` proves every
weight, payload and encoded-response access is in bounds under that shape.
Optional getters totalize the source model outside these preconditions; they
are not used to justify accepting malformed arrays.

`NativeGoldColumnWorker` hashes the original received `Row`, parses its
leaf-first path, checks the native sibling chain, and computes coordinate
checks only after authentication succeeds. Its hash-only VCVio computation
compiles to the same mixed-oracle native authentication/coordinate program.
The shared hash encoding is the existing injective raw-row encoding. No
semantic field list is serialized in place of the raw payload; distinct lazy
representatives remain distinct hash inputs.

The raw workers instantiate the existing `HashWorkerPool`. Arbitrary
individual hash advances, interleaving, shared scheduler work, cancellation
and retained earlier calls are covered by that pool's operational theorem.
Its computed final all-accepted flag derives replay of every original raw
payload/path and the actual coordinate flag from the final shared cache.
`NativeGoldPcsWorkerSoundness.accepted_checks` turns those flags into both
semantic coordinate families. It does not take supplied worker traces or
external Merkle-acceptance/replay certificates.

`NativeGoldPcsWorkers.protocol` continues the actual retained-code PCS
encoding entry point into prepared worker inputs. It preserves every earlier
rejection, suspension and backend-unavailability outcome. Recursive pairing
requires both lists to end together; its projections recover the complete
ordered received columns and sampled indices. The preceding actual distinct
count check proves this pairing succeeds. Preparation retains the computed
random/structured weights, both computed encoded vectors, original root,
geometry, packing width and resulting atomic transcript for later steps.
It emits no additional oracle observations and is not an acceptance result.

`prepared_shape` derives every worker's array preconditions from the actual
checked prefix and retained block-code constructor. It uses the original
received-column shape checks, actual bounded sampled indices, computed
random/structured matrix sizes and actual response-encoder output lengths.
There is no caller-provided geometry or response-shape certificate in the
entry point. Packing width and code-symbol width remain separate.

The mixed-oracle prefix and probabilistic shared-cache pool still have
separate execution interfaces. Their checkpoint/observation-state coupling,
native Rayon scheduling/completion refinement and a full PCS acceptance
entry point are not established by these local worker theorems. In
particular this does not yet connect authenticated raw payloads to the
prefix-frozen semantic word used by proximity analysis. Final suffix/claim
enforcement and full lookup/helper PCS composition remain open.

## Raw frozen-word availability and pool loss

`NativeGoldPcsPaths.prepared_paths` derives every prepared job's typed Merkle
position and exact leaf-first path length from the actual checked PCS prefix.
It uses the original column/path guards, bounded sampled indices and computed
Merkle height. This part needs neither primitive-root correctness nor a
caller-supplied path/geometry certificate.

`NativeGoldRawRequests.fromJob` computes the typed availability request from
the original job: its sampled index, original raw `Row`, retained root and
parsed leaf/siblings. The context tag and height family identify the trusted
checkpoint configuration. Out-of-range positions or incorrect path lengths
return `none`. `entries` requires every original job to convert successfully;
it retains each job alongside its request and never drops, truncates or merges
a worker, even when two positions coincide. Its proved first projection is
the entire original job list, and every second component is its actual
computed request. `replay_of_worker` transfers replay from the literal raw
worker computation to the generic raw-payload availability interface.

`NativeGoldRawAvailability.frozenRaw` selects the immutable total raw word
from a recorded checkpoint's cumulative prefix log and root, with an empty
raw-row fallback. Only after that selection do `frozenValue`/`frozenWord`
interpret coordinates in Goldilocks, with zero for missing coordinates.
The frozen object depends on the checkpoint and trusted layout dimensions;
it has no later query, response, worker-result or challenge input. Placing
the actual native checkpoint before the opening challenges remains part of
the state-coupling obligation. This is the information-theoretic prefix
resolver, not an efficient decoder claim.

Outside the existing `ParallelColumnAvailability.Failure` event, an accepted
raw request equals this frozen raw payload. Field-value projection therefore
preserves the original native coordinate equations against the same frozen
word. Both random and structured response families use one conjunction of
equations. No projected field list is substituted into a hash input, and no
injectivity of Goldilocks value projection is assumed (it is false for lazy
aliases). Missing/unavailable payloads and malformed unqueried raw lengths
still give a total semantic word; native queried lengths remain established
by the earlier checked-prefix array-bound theorem.

`NativeGoldPcsRawAvailability.prepare` applies that lossless adapter to an
actual prepared PCS result. Its completeness theorem derives all request
preconditions from the checked prefix when the trusted context height matches
the computed native height. Actual pool acceptance then derives raw replay
and the coordinate checks for every computed request from the final shared
cache, without incoming replay/acceptance certificates. `pool_equations`
transports those checks to every recorded matching root's frozen semantic
word outside the same joint availability event.

`NativeGoldRawAvailability.failure_le_charge` and its empty-initialization
version reduce failed semantic transport to the existing joint root-wide
hash hazard for arbitrary adaptive programs returning request views.
`NativeGoldPcsRawFailure.failure_le_charge` additionally specializes this
reduction to the actual worker-pool computation: the event requires its
computed all-accepted residual-worker flag, yet the frozen equations fail.
The reduction uses support of that actual pool run, not arbitrary fabricated
pool outputs. All original scheduler work, interleaving, cancellation and
issued hashes stay in the charged program. No per-worker, per-lane,
per-coordinate or extra response-family union factor is introduced. This is
a symbolic expected-hazard bound, not the final numerical security claim.

Eight new kernel adapter cases reuse the pinned native raw-column fixtures.
They check the complete original payload/root/leaf and index/path geometry,
reject invalid indices and context heights, preserve distinct lazy payloads
at duplicate positions, and reject an invalid later job without returning a
truncated prefix. Two additional checked-prefix fixture cases compute the
requests from the actual prepared state and recover the original received
payload list in order. All earlier native hash/arithmetic/lazy-alias tests
remain intact. All 19 new public theorems have guarded audits using only
`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`; the combined HasteBoots suite
now has 2,711 guarded audits. Default proof limits are unchanged.

coupling, lookup/PBS extraction, production profile instantiation, strict
decoding, root generation/cache, Div64/SIMD/Rust/compiler/scheduler refinement,
BabyBear, numerical certification and the final 128-bit application theorem

shared-cache/recorded-checkpoint interface; it does not by itself close

## Original-draw semantic opening checks

`NativeGoldPcsDraws.typed` checks both the exact original quota length and all
position bounds, then retains the complete draw vector in original order.

entire original list; `typed_complete` proves conversion succeeds when the
existing native request bounds hold. Malformed lengths or positions return
`none`, rather than truncating or substituting a fallback draw.

`prepared_sample` extracts the original actual atomic-request result from the
checked PCS execution. The full request equation includes the actual
response-bound transcript and the original native label/domain/quota.
Prepared job indices equal its sorted/deduplicated indices, but its ordered
draw list still has the original query quota. Every draw, including each
repeat, is bounded by the computed Merkle domain and covered by an unchanged
prepared job. The resulting transcript is retained. `prepared_typed` derives
the typed original vector and this coverage directly from execution success.
These results identify samples; they do not assume or establish fresh
uniform production challenges.

`NativeGoldPcsAgrees.pool_position` transports the existing raw-pool equations
to a fixed recorded checkpoint at any covered position. It recovers the
actual request's tag, root and index from the lossless raw adapter; those

challenge-dependent weights and computed responses are separate arguments.
The source continues to project the prefix-frozen raw word after extraction;
no semantic field list is hashed.

`agrees_of_equations` identifies the original raw coordinate sums with
`StructuredOpening.combine` and `ColumnOpening.Agrees`. `pool_agrees` proves
both random-test and structured-response agreement families on every covered
ordered draw, including repetitions, against that same fixed source.
Sorting/deduplicating transmitted columns introduces no extra loss and does
not replace the query quota by the number of distinct received columns.
The existing shared raw-availability exception is unchanged.

`NativeGoldPcsOpeningChecks.prepared_parameters` derives that geometry is the
deterministic checked construction from trusted parameters, with the original
root and packing width. The query, challenge values and oracle world do not
supply that geometry. `original_draws` computes the actual quota-sized draw
function at the matching trusted checkpoint height. Finally,
`prepared_agrees` combines actual checked-prefix success, the original atomic
request, actual raw-pool acceptance and the fixed recorded checkpoint to
establish both existing semantic opening-check families. It takes no supplied
draw vector or coverage certificate. The raw request list is the checked
adapter's computed result; its completeness is supplied by the preceding
layer.

## Computed PCS completion and suffix claims

`NativeGoldPcsClaim.verify` computes the native suffix fold from the original
unencoded `opening.evaluation` and compares the result with the original raw
claimed row using Goldilocks field equality. It does not compare serialized
words or take a supplied finished vector. `equal_iff`, `accepted_iff` and
`accepted_value` connect the executable check to the semantic suffix equation.
The prefix continues to bind the original serialized claim without replacing
it by its canonical representative.

`NativeGoldPcsFinishComplete` proves completeness of the raw packed fold loop,
its evaluator and the PCS suffix wrapper. `prepared_finish` derives all
matrix validation, query/response dimensions, nonzero width and allocation
bounds from the actual completed checked prefix. Consequently
`prepared_no_finish_error` rules out the defensive suffix-shape failure on
that prefix; a wrong final claim can still be rejected.

`NativeGoldPcsAcceptance.program` maps the existing general interleaved worker
pool to a computed completion status. Acceptance requires that every residual
worker has actually returned true, followed by a successful suffix/claim
check. A returned false worker rejects columns; an unfinished pool is an
analysis suspension. The latter is not a native verifier error. The scheduler
cannot supply an acceptance flag. `failed_iff` and `anyRejected_iff` identify
rejection with actual false-returning residual programs.

`program_origin` and `accepted_origin` retain the original pool result,
scheduler memory and shared final state/cache, with no additional oracle
queries. `NativeGoldPcsAcceptanceSoundness.accepted_workers` derives raw
payload/path replay and both native coordinate checks for every original job
from this supported accepted execution. `accepted_value` additionally uses
the actual checked prefix to derive the semantic final claim equation. The
statement deliberately retains separate checked-prefix and supported-pool
execution premises: coupling these interfaces into one native transcript and
checkpoint/cache execution remains required.

observation. Their single-worker harness is test-only; the production
acceptance program uses the existing general interleaved pool.

## One shared PCS prefix and pool execution

`NativeCheckpointProgram.compile` translates the existing online native
`OracleProgram.Program` into the existing shared checkpoint oracle spec.
Every native SHA-512 call goes through the same canonical cached handler as
later worker and scheduler calls. SHAKE starts and reads retain their complete
native ordered observations. The reader is an explicit functional backend;
compilation assigns it no fresh-uniform or independent probability law.
There are no additional primitive queries hidden by the compiler.
`hash_record` identifies each actual cached step, including hits and repeated
calls. `supported_hash_state` proves the complete outgoing hash state is
exactly the fold of those retained native observations over the incoming
state, including its cache, chronological hash log and populated keys.

`supported_replay` proves that every supported compiled prefix equals the
original native computation, including its complete return value and
observation list, in any world matching its reader and final cache.
`supported_actual` constructs such a world from the actual cache, with zero
only at unqueried hash inputs. `supported_later` preserves that equation after
later shared work extends the cache. This world completion is a deterministic
replay construction, not a distributional coupling or a claim that unqueried
hashes have constant production answers.

`NativeGoldPcsExecution.program` compiles the actual checked parameter,
binding, field sampling, structured weights, response framing, atomic draw,
response encoding and raw-job preparation prefix, then continues with the
existing general interleaved worker pool and final suffix/claim check. The
same state flows through their monadic bind. Prefix rejection, pairing
failure and analysis suspension remain distinguishable from a completed
worker tail. The context consists solely of the original protocol inputs and
backend/fuel parameters; it contains no supplied finished vector, transcript
log, prefix-success certificate or pool-start state.

`completed_origin` obtains the real intermediate state and both supported
subruns from the complete supported execution. `completed_native` recovers
the original native prefix and its complete observations against the actual
final shared cache. `accepted_value` and `accepted_workers` therefore derive
the original final claim equation, raw payload/path replay and both native
coordinate families from one accepted run. The independent prefix-success
and pool-state premises of the previous acceptance layer are discharged.

`NativeGoldPcsExecutionAgrees.accepted_agrees` connects this same run to both
semantic opening-check families at one fixed recorded checkpoint. The raw
request list is computed by the adapter, its completeness follows from this
run's checked prefix, and the original quota-sized draw vector is recovered
in full order, including repetitions. `Failure` existentially packages the
existing root-wide availability exception for that unique computed request
list. Matching the fixed checkpoint root uses the original context root,
with prepared-root equality derived from execution. Recording the correct
checkpoint before the outer lookup challenge, including all registered
representative roots, remains a separate placement obligation.

The native CANONICAL and ZERO_BAD fixtures now also execute this full

## Source checkpoints before native lookup challenges

`NativeHashPrefix.HashOnly` excludes SHAKE starts and reads on every adaptive
hash-answer branch. Its bind closure and native-log theorem retain all hash
observations. `compile_independent` proves that changing the complete reader
backend leaves the compiled hash-only program unchanged. This is a structural
statement conditional on the same inputs and preceding state, not a new
probability or transcript-input freshness assumption.

`NativeSharedLookupHashPrefix` establishes this property for the actual
context computation, selected-source contexts, framing, numeric preflight
steps/loop, complete registry registration and parent preparation. All
failure branches are included. Thus the actual parent metadata processing
and all original registry context hashes precede the child/outer lookup
challenge stage, rather than using a late checkpoint before PCS randomness.

`NativeCheckpointBoundary` executes a compiled native stage, records its
computed root family using the existing passive `RecordRoots` operation,
then executes the native continuation in the same shared state. Its origin
lemmas recover the actual intermediate states. Every snapshot uses the same
actual pre-recording hash log; recording preserves the hash cache/log/keys.
`native_replay` proves exact erasure of the ghost annotations, including the
whole original native value and ordered observation list. `program_recorded`
retains each snapshot through the complete continuation without conditioning
on acceptance, collision freedom or an unset stability monitor.

`NativeSharedLookupCheckpoints` factors the original complete shared lookup
entry point into parent preparation followed by its existing child launcher
and scalar/terminal/finish body. `native_eq` proves equality of the native
programs themselves. The wrapper records every original registry slot after
successful preparation and before that continuation. Failed preparation
records no roots and retains its actual partial hash work. Root selection
uses the original ordered registry, independently of which slots later open.
It includes unused slots and unused earlier aliases of a later used source.
A configuration-tag embedding permits the same shared state to contain later
helper checkpoints with different trusted shapes. No slot is truncated,
sorted or deduplicated by this layer.

`freeze_independent` proves the complete preparation/recording computation is
unchanged by the reader supplying the later lookup challenges. `native_replay`
recovers the complete original lookup entry point from the final shared cache.
`recorded_sources` derives successful parent preparation and actual earlier,
recorded and final states from one supported run returning a body result.
Every original source root has a snapshot of that earlier prefix log in both
the pre-child state and the final state. The caller supplies no independent
prepared transcript, successful parent prefix or checkpoint-membership proof.
Existing checkpoint-history lemmas retain these same snapshots through
subsequent PCS/scheduler work.

The existing native parent fixture now checks unchanged context hashes and
native observations together with the computed recording requests. A
three-slot case uses slots one and two while slot zero is an unused earlier
alias of slot two; all three roots are recorded in original order. Changing
the reader leaves preparation/recording unchanged, while invalid preparation
emits no recording requests. The existing complete native body fixture also
executes the new annotated entry point and checks its bound result, every
original native observation and all hashes plus the passive source record.

`NativeSharedLookupHelperCheckpoints` computes the actual outer lookup batch

Helper snapshots are placed after the outer sampler and before

Snapshots persist through equality/statement construction, including all

`NativeSharedLookupChildCheckpoints` integrates the existing proof/value

`native_replay` recovers the original complete child/body continuation.
`recorded_helpers` derives successful preparation, the actual child/raw batch,

`NativeSharedLookupCheckpointExecution.program` combines the earlier source

## Persistent SHAKE cache and lazy native programs

`NativeShakeCache` owns a persistent cache keyed by the complete SHAKE input
and byte offset. A hit returns the saved byte without an oracle request;
a miss consumes one private uniform byte and installs its answer. No reader
identity occurs in the key. Every possible read preserves all previously
exposed answers and records its entire returned interval in the final cache.
Consequently, rereading an interval returns exactly the same bytes without
new randomness. Splitting a read preserves byte order and the complete cache.
These laws apply to arbitrary initial caches, including partial overlaps.

`NativeLazyProgram.compile` executes the original causal native program in
this cache state over the existing shared checkpoint specification. All
SHA-512 requests still use that specification's canonical hash interface.
The compiler retains every ordered native observation, including repeated
reads and hash calls. Native continuations receive only their returned
answer; they cannot supply or replace the cache. Composition threads one
cache through both programs, and every possible compiled branch preserves
previously exposed bytes.

`NativeProgramPrefix.take` retains the actual residual program at an analysis
boundary. Its world semantics is the existing `OracleProgram.runPrefix`.
Binding the residual continuation reconstructs the original program exactly.
`NativeLazyProgram.compile_resume` transports that identity to the stateful
interpreter, including both observation lists and the persistent cache.
Thus analysis fuel does not impose a native retry limit or refresh challenges.

and the remainder use only `propext` and `Quot.sound`. Focused regressions cover
complete-input separation, retained prequery answers, fresh-coordinate updates,
compiled cached reads and suspended next requests. No original fixture,

The full formal security goal remains active.

## Native prequery-aware index laws

`NativePrequeryIndexLaw` proves the actual native atomic-index phase's exact
conditional law after the entire mixed SHAKE/SHA-512 history. It retains the
old byte on every previously exposed coordinate and samples only the unseen
coordinates. This covers partial reads, overlapping and cloned readers,
off-path queries, and request inputs selected after prequerying them. It
conditions on the complete prior result and ordered log, rather than success
or a purported first verifier visit. The product-world sigma algebra is
unchanged; no full-reader conditioning or zero-probability fiber is used.

The native decoder transports that masked byte law to the complete ordered
draw vector. The usual Hamming-agreement probability is recovered only under
an explicit disjointness premise for every byte in the requested block.
Complete overlap instead yields a deterministic vector, including on the
verifier's first visit. A separate law preserves the native ordered list,
without reducing the quota when equal positions occur.

The native request theorem includes its entire `Option Result`, updated
transcript, sorted/deduplicated transport indices and both native observations.
Adaptive request parameters—including transcript, label, domain and original
quota—and the tested predicate may be selected from the whole prior result
and log. The unnormalized law retains that history's exact mass, without a
success floor or query cutoff. Validity is required only for the selected
request on the analyzed history, not for unrelated histories.

`NativeGoldPrequeryIndices` identifies the checked Goldilocks PCS draw adapter
with the original literal draw vector. Its conditional event law consequently
uses the same cache-masked generator. Successful parsing and transport
deduplication introduce no new independence or freshness assumption.

## Rectangular proximity and shared-column opening

`ModuleCodeProximity` separates the scalar field used for test coins from the
module used for whole code symbols. It generalizes the pinned ArkLib AHIV22
affine-line and row-span argument, retaining its Apache 2.0 attribution. The
module proves common-support alignment for sparse subspaces, a far direction
in the source-row span, affine-line counting and the uniform coefficient law.
The scalar-field-size premise `radius < |F|` is explicit, along with
`3 * radius < minimum distance`; no small-field alignment exception is omitted.
Dependent source rows are allowed through proved uniform fibers.

For minimum distance `delta` and `testWidth` independent base-field rows, the
proved proximity term is `(delta / |F|)^testWidth`. The alphabet may be
`Fin codeWidth → F` with no equality between `codeWidth` and `testWidth`.
This is the conservative repeated-row bound, not an assumed extension of the
older square bound `delta / |F|^testWidth`. The two expressions are not
interchangeable. No numeric production security level follows yet.

`RectangularBaseProximity` specializes that law to the existing semantic
`BlockCode`, `StructuredOpening.combine` and the common-source decoder's
complete-column metric. Every column includes all source rows and all symbol
coordinates. Its explicit-distance corollary uses the existing checked
`BlockCode.minDist` theorem and retains independent test and code widths.

`RectangularOpening` now composes the far and near branches for a fixed
available word. Malicious coded responses may depend on the preceding random
matrix. The encoded far-branch corollary derives their code membership from
their coefficient arrays using `BlockEncoder.encode_mem_code`. Every response
uses the same ordered column vector. The near/far column terms are combined
by a maximum; shared column acceptance probabilities are not multiplied.
All structured queries use one total common decoder for that available word.

There are eighteen new public production theorems, each with a guarded axiom
audit using only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The focused
suite supplies an inhabited width-3/code-width-4 example over `ZMod 5` with
proved code distance 2 and a far word. A second example instantiates the actual
semantic `BlockCode` bridge at those unequal widths, deriving the distance and
common-source far premise. Honest encoded zero responses accept for every
matrix and shared draw. A separate regression proves that three identical
checks sharing one column draw accept with probability `1/2`, rather than a
product of three independent column probabilities.

This closes the rectangular fixed-word proximity and shared-column interactive
opening interface. It does not yet connect rectangular response finishing to
the native matrix query, instantiate the retained native constructor and all
production roles, or certify numeric 128-bit feasibility. Global first-exposure
Fiat–Shamir causality, the lazy/world distribution bridge, native batch and
helper composition, application extraction and concrete attacker-work
realization remain open, together with native refinement and BabyBear. The
full security goal remains active.

## Lazy SHAKE read law and native index execution

`NativeShakeKernel` identifies the physical cached-or-uniform byte sampler
with the joint world's exact conditional byte law after the entire mixed
SHAKE/SHA-512 past. Its initial cache comes from that finite observed footprint.
The kernel transports arbitrary byte predicates and predicates on the returned
byte plus updated cache. The actual shared interpreter step leaves every
SHA-512/checkpoint field unchanged. A prior observation of SHA-512 on the same
input does not populate a SHAKE coordinate.

`NativeShakeHistory` reconstructs the exact byte-cache effect of every supported
read and compiled program from the complete retained observation list. Hits,
repeated reads and partial overlaps remain in that list. The same property
holds after any typed shared oracle implementation, using proved support
inclusion rather than an external cache-coherence certificate.

`NativeShakeReadLaw` extends the physical byte step to a whole read. Its
actual shared execution preserves the entire shared state and uses the
private cached sampler. The sampler has exactly the eager finite-vector
masked law, including its final byte cache. This is an equality of probability
laws: the eager generator's unused coins at cached coordinates are analytical
and are not charged as native work. Output order, interval writes and every
previously exposed answer are retained. The final event theorem compares the
joint world's whole-history conditional read with the actual shared execution,
including both states and allowing arbitrary partial overlap. No fresh-block,
first-reader, or successful-verification premise is used.

`NativeLazyIndexExecution` applies that read law to the actual checked native
atomic-index program, compiled by `NativeLazyProgram`. It proves equality of
the complete native result, updated transcript, ordered observation list,
owned byte cache and shared hash/checkpoint state under the full conditional
past. Native framing and decoding coincide with the earlier finite-vector
index law. Invalid dimensions return before drawing bytes and preserve both
prior interpreter states. Sorting and transport deduplication leave the
original with-replacement draw quota intact.

All twenty-six new public lemmas have guarded axiom audits using only
`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Thirty focused regressions cover
an actual mixed read/hash history, namespace separation, input separation,
partial/cached/empty reads, cache reconstruction, physical zero-query cache
hits, native framed partial prequeries, ordered duplicates versus unique
transport indices, and invalid native dimensions.

This completes a conditional distribution bridge for a real native atomic-index
phase and its physical lazy read. It does not yet prove the general mixed
program's finite-prefix distribution law from empty interpreter states, nor
integrate the worker scheduler and source/helper checkpoint compiler. In
particular, cache reconstruction alone is not the probability theorem.
First-exposure root freezing, parent/child guessing exceptions, rectangular
matrix finishing and actual batch/helper PCS composition remain open, followed
by full application extraction, numeric profiles, concrete attacker-work
realization and the final 128-bit expected-work theorem. Native refinement
and BabyBear remain separate required gates. The full goal stays active.

## Conditional mixed-program execution and final byte cache

`NativeLazyExecutionLaw.execute_law` proves exact conditional event probability
for **the actual `NativeLazyProgram.compile` interpreter** under the shared
`CheckpointExecution.handler`, against the original joint product world.
The event may inspect the arbitrary result and complete ordered native log.
The initial history is any replayable execution, including prequeries; its
observed SHAKE cache and projected SHA-512 cache supply the interpreter state.
Read lengths, offsets, inputs and subsequent read/hash instructions may depend
on preceding responses. Repeated inputs, partial overlaps, reader restarts,
zero-length reads and cached hashes require no disjointness premise.

The proof has these independently checked layers:

- `OracleHistoryComposition`: exact total probability over the countable range
  of complete replayable histories, for any finite measure, then exact
  refinement inside an earlier history conditional. Zero-mass refined fibers
  remain in the partition; no successful-execution normalization is used.
- `OracleHistorySnapshot`: retain the whole prior result/log and the actual
  next response in the analysis payload. Later fibers fix both the earlier
  history and the response without adding oracle observations.
- `NativeShakeProjection`: a truthful log fold reconstructs the observed byte
  cache; appending a read updates precisely its interval, while starts and
  hashes leave the SHAKE cache unchanged. A whole-history fiber fixes this
  cache even when other coordinates remain unknown.
- `OracleKernelComposition`: exact score and arbitrary-continuation transfer
  for physical SHAKE sampling and canonical cached SHA-512 answers, using the
  whole-history posterior and exact history-refinement averaging.
- `NativeLazyExecution`: literal code equalities for pure/start/read/hash
  execution, including the canonical hash-state and passive-monitor update.
  `executeWithCache_records` derives the owned final SHAKE cache from supported
  executions of that actual handler and the retained complete log.
- `NativeLazyExecutionLaw`: structural induction over mixed programs combines
  those laws. `prefix_law` retains the actual residual program, `from_empty`
  discharges both initial-cache premises, and `cache_law` extends the exact
  event equality to the owned final byte cache of the old-plus-new history.

This closes the general finite-program and finite-analysis-prefix
**value/log/SHAKE-cache probability bridge**, beyond the prior one-request laws.
It does not yet assert equality of all final shared monitor/checkpoint states,
an infinite sampler completion theorem, native Rust refinement, or complete
Fiat–Shamir/application security. The syntax is a causal well-founded program;
unbounded retry processes still need compatible prefix families and limits.

The next Gate A obligations are final SHA-512/monitor state recovery and
compatible-prefix limits, followed by the first-exposure ledger and earliest
relevant-byte root freezing across raw/off-path/descendant prequeries. Gate B
still needs rectangular native finishing and constructor instantiation, then
an inhabited numerical Goldilocks profile and query-feasibility certificate.
The final work theorem, BabyBear profile and fail-closed Rust refinement remain
mandatory. No verifier-work substitution or query cutoff is introduced here.

## Full shared-state execution and causal lifetime limits

`NativeLazyStateExecution.state_law` extends the exact mixed-program
probability bridge to **the entire actual compiled outcome**: arbitrary result,
complete native log, owned SHAKE cache, canonical SHA-512 cache, checkpoint
registry and passive failure flag. The implementation is the existing
`simulateQ CheckpointExecution.handler ((NativeLazyProgram.compile p).run cache)`
with both state layers retained, rather than a replacement oracle interpreter.
Supported executions reconstruct both state layers from the literal ordered
log; this gives an equality of actual `ProbComp` computations before applying
the conditional event law. `fold_project` identifies the final shared hash
state with the canonical projection of the old-plus-new native log.

The shared-state fold applies the actual `afterHash` update on every hash,
including cached repeats. It retains a failure detected before later queries
repair source stability. Starts and reads leave the shared state unchanged.
This program syntax issues no checkpoint-registration query, so it preserves
the **initial** registry; this theorem does not insert or relocate native root
registration. `prefix_law` retains the residual program and every state field,
and `from_empty` discharges the initial-history premises.

`OracleMachine` supplies a causal interface for truly unbounded retry loops.
A local state chooses a done/start/read/hash command; response continuations
receive only the corresponding response. Local state can include the entire
attacker memory and an initially chosen random tape. Finite `take` prefixes
return the real residual local state or completed result. They do not impose
a runtime retry limit. The syntax permits machines with no terminating run.

`take_resume` proves exact prefix compatibility. `compile_resume` carries the
owned byte cache, and `execute_resume` carries **both caches and the complete
shared state** across suspension. Thus longer prefixes use the actual cached
execution, with no independent rerun of already sampled bytes. Their ideal
logs extend by prefix. Completed results/logs are absorbing at all later fuel.

`conditional_lifetime_law` proves that the probability of ever seeing a
persistent bad-log event equals the supremum of the actual full-state prefix
probabilities after any replayable prequery history. `lifetime_law` starts from
empty caches. `completion_lifetime_law` gives the corresponding exact limit
for bad completed results, with no termination assumption, query cutoff,
success floor or conditioning on successful completion. `eventual_measurable`
proves measurability of arbitrary eventual prefix-result events in the original
joint product sigma algebra. These are lifetime **event-probability** limits;
no claim about a general infinite-trace distribution or almost-sure termination
is needed or made.

Gate A now has a full-state finite-prefix bridge and compatible causal
lifetime-event limits. Its next substantive obligation is the first-exposure
ledger and earliest relevant-byte root freezing, including raw/off-path and
descendant prequeries, followed by native phase/registration composition.
The attacker-work coupling, rectangular native finishing/constructor and
numerical-profile gates, final application/extraction theorem, BabyBear and
fail-closed Rust/scheduler refinement remain open.

## Raw first-seed exposure and cache-aware guessing risk

`OracleFirstExposure` finds the earliest returned-coordinate exposure directly
in the complete raw native observation log. Its minimality certificate splits
that **same** log into the earlier history, first relevant observation and
suffix; every earlier coordinate set is disjoint from the relevant set. Starts,
empty reads and SHA-512 coordinates cannot expose SHAKE bytes. Complete input
bytes and offsets identify cells, so clones/restarts share exposure while
prefix-related but unequal inputs do not. Appending observations cannot move
an existing first exposure. Arbitrary, unclassified, duplicate and rejected
queries remain in the original ordered log; this index is not a work metric.

The seed specialization includes all 64 coordinates of a native parent seed
under its exact complete SHAKE input. It detects a first read at any seed
position, rather than assuming a verifier read or offset zero came first.
`OracleMachineExposure.log_take` identifies log truncation with an actual
causal-machine analysis prefix. `pre_exposure_fresh` therefore gives a replayable
**actual** pre-exposure history with all 64 seed coordinates unseen.
`pre_exposure_targets` derives exact fixed-target hit probability
`targets.card / 2^512` under that complete-history conditional.

`OracleMaskCounting` separately counts full raw-mask fibers. A target
inconsistent with any known byte has no fiber. Each compatible target has
exactly `256^known.card` raw responses, and distinct targets have disjoint
fibers. Cancellation gives the exact masked uniform target-hit probability:

```
compatible_target_count / 256^(coordinate_count - known_coordinate_count)
```

`OracleSeedGuessing.target_law` transfers this count to the whole-history SHAKE
posterior, retaining arbitrary partial overlap and mixed prequeries. Its
`risk_read_average` and `risk_hash_average` prove exact conditional averaging
across an actual later read or shared hash query. A partial read can increase
or decrease the pointwise completion risk; only its conditional average is
preserved. No per-byte `2^-512` claim is made. `fresh_seed_targets` uses the full
`2^512` denominator only with the explicit all-64-unseen premise.

These results supply the earliest-seed-exposure and orphan-guessing
probability primitives. **They do not yet freeze native roots.** The next
required bridge must parse complete raw native inputs, extract context/root
keys and quoted parent seeds, retain orphan descendant queries, prove that
the target set and next request are selected from the prior history, and
place proof-only availability registrations before the first relevant
response. In particular, a target set chosen using future seed bytes cannot
be substituted into the fixed-target theorem. Native root/context classifier
completeness, parent-child guessing exceptions, protocol composition and real
attacker-work coupling remain open, along with the other application and
native-refinement gates.

## Native raw-input root and parent-seed views

`NativeExactCodec` turns existing structural prefix codecs into exact input
views: recognition requires an empty trailing suffix and byte-for-byte
canonical reencoding. `read_iff` proves that recognizing a value is equivalent
to the input being its exact encoding. This is an analysis parser; it does not
replace or refine the native adversarial proof deserializer.

`NativeChildSeedView` reads the fixed sixth frame (index 5) of a **complete**
raw framed input. It recognizes the immediate-parent-seed label only there,
with exactly the canonical 64-byte digest payload. A forged later frame with
the same label does not add or replace the candidate. Soundness identifies the
actual decoded frame and exact bytes. Completeness is proved against the real
`NativeTranscript.forkChild` output, with the native frame-length bounds.
A `HasHeader` invariant preserves that seed through any valid absorption,
byte-challenge request and field-reader request, including zero-length field
requests. The unframed consumed-field-byte receipt domain is explicitly
rejected by this framed view; its raw observations remain in the execution.

The collector takes at most one quoted candidate per nonempty raw output or
hash observation, retains repeated observations in the underlying log, and
deduplicates only the guessed-seed target set. Its cardinality is at most the
actual raw observation count. `orphan_probability` combines this native
collector with the earlier first-exposure law: the event of the logical
parent seed matching a candidate parsed from the **actual prior machine log**
has exact probability `candidate_count / 2^512`. The target set is fixed by
conditioning on the complete prior result/log, rather than chosen using later
seed bytes. The all-64-unseen premise comes from the actual pre-exposure
prefix. This count is not an attacker-work certificate and includes no claim
that verifier queries can be charged to the attacker.

`NativeRootInputView` recognizes context/root source vectors in the actual
Goldilocks canonical-bind and deferred-registry encodings. Its binding reader
checks the serialized extension degree 3, helper context and full source
vector. Exact canonical guards reject trailing or altered payloads. Single
PCS openings recognize the adjacent native row-code-context and
commitment/query frames using the complete opening codec. Complete raw input
views first decode the entire framed stream, then retain ordered mentions.
Recognition is proved for the actual `registry`, `bind` and
`NativeGoldPcsBinding.appendBound` functions. Original source vectors survive
as ordered sublists, retaining repetitions and unused entries. Adjacent single
opening pairs remain present after any earlier frame prefix.

The mention list is **not** the native opening registry or its first-original
representative map. Flattening mentions must not substitute a first-mentioned
alias for the native first original registry slot. The exact decoded frames
and registry vector remain the authoritative evidence for that later bridge.
The views also do not establish that a parsed context digest names trusted
parameters, that a quoted seed authenticates parent ownership, or that a
mentioned root has an available word.

Next, associate parsed descendants and helper roots with their actual parent
contexts, prove causal selection of the parent request from the prior machine
state, and insert availability snapshots before the first relevant raw
response while proving erasure to the actual interpreter. Receipt-linked
future prefixes need their own guessing/freshness argument; a guessed consumed
field block does not automatically have 512 bits of entropy. Native first-slot
alias/group order, full protocol composition, attacker-work coupling and the
remaining rectangular/numerical/application/refinement gates stay open.
