## Causally selected seed exposures and online direct-root snapshots

`CausalSeedExposure` selects the pending native request from the actual local
machine state retained by a replayable prefix. An eligible first read is
nonempty, intersects positions 0–63, and has no earlier exposure of any of the
64 logical seed coordinates. Both its complete input and the guessed-seed set
parsed from the prior raw log are fixed on the complete history fiber. The
exact conditional event probability is therefore `prior_candidate_count /
2^512`, with no selection of a request input from later witness data.
`event_measurable` and `averaged_event` prove measurability and exact averaging
over the actual countable range of complete histories; no measurable local
state or payload assumption is added. This event concerns a **new** first
exposure. It does not reset inherited bad risk or assign 512 bits of entropy
to receipt guesses or partially exposed seeds.

`NativeDirectRootFreeze` now instruments the **actual owned-cache lazy
compiler**, rather than only recording roots at a verifier phase boundary.
For each nonempty raw read, it parses the complete input with
`NativeRootInputView`, removes duplicate context/root keys and those already
present in earlier nonempty read observations, and issues `RecordRoots`
checkpoint annotations before the byte read. Context digests are the ghost
configuration tags; an application must still prove their trusted shape and
parameter interpretation. Empty reads keep their original native observation
but record no root. Starts and shared hash calls remain in the complete
history; neither is silently charged as a SHAKE exposure.

The operational guarantees are proved as follows:

- `erase_compile` erases only checkpoint requests and recovers the original
  `NativeLazyProgram.compile` computation, retaining its complete result/log,
  owned SHAKE cache, and literal private/hash queries.
- `canonical_compile` and `execute_erasure` reuse the existing canonical
  checkpoint-erasure theorem. Under the actual shared handler, result/log,
  owned byte cache and shared hash cache agree exactly with the original
  execution. The proof-only registry and failure monitor intentionally differ.
- `execute_read` identifies the root state recorded from the actual pre-read
  cumulative hash log before the private byte sampler. `read_snapshot` proves
  that every supported continuation retains that exact checkpoint, without
  assuming monitor success, collision freedom or a query bound.
- `fresh_after_output` prevents a cloned read of the same input from recording
  the keys again. Key identity is the complete `(context digest,root)` pair;
  equal roots under different contexts remain distinct.
- `compile_bind` and `compile_resume` thread the real ordered history and the
  same owned byte cache through composition and finite-prefix suspension.
  A suspension does not refresh root snapshots or challenge bytes.

These guarantees apply to directly parsed source mentions. They do **not**
yet cover helper-root frames lacking their parent helper context, associate
orphan descendants with parents, or establish availability of every root used
by an accepted verifier run. Earliest-exposure application requires the initial
history, owned byte cache and prior checkpoints to come from the same
instrumented prelude (or the empty initial state). Passing a historical log
alone is not a certificate that its earlier roots were registered. Similarly,
the flat mention order does not replace the native first-original-slot alias
map or ordered-prefix query grouping.

Next, retain compatible pending-parent contexts during partial seed reads,
use those contexts to register helper roots before their equality challenges,
and prove the whole native root/exposure coverage statement with explicit
orphan/receipt exceptions. Then compose source availability and arithmetic
with the real attacker-work ledger; raw log cardinality is not substituted for
attacker cost, and no verifier/setup work is charged to the attacker. The
remaining rectangular/numerical/application and fail-closed refinement gates
remain mandatory.

## Partial-parent association and causal helper-root snapshots

`NativeParentInputView` recognizes the actual native parent-seed request
(kind 6 fork followed by the kind 2, 64-byte classical-child-seed request),
canonical helper contexts in bind messages, and canonical helper-root
vectors. `parseParent_request` links recognition to
`NativeTranscript.requestInput (absorb parent 6 label context) ... 64`.
Compatibility inspects only already observed positions of the seed, and
`compatible_observed` proves that the actual logical seed remains compatible
after arbitrary partial reads. A single unknown final byte retains all 256
possible values.

`NativeParentLedger` stores every compatible pending parent, its resolved
source keys and its inherited helper contexts. A child header can resolve
helper roots against several compatible parents; the resolver does not pick
the first seed match or require a complete seed read. Stored metadata also
allows source/context propagation into later descendants. Discovery uses the
old parent table and old byte cache. Its frozen set is unchanged: a parent
discovered after an earlier child read cannot backdate that read's snapshot.
Only preparation for a subsequent nonempty read adds resolved keys to the
persistent frozen set. Duplicate keys are removed, complete context/root
pairs remain distinct, existing parents are retained, and previously frozen
keys are never requested again.

`NativeParentRootFreeze` threads this ledger through the actual owned-cache
compiler. Starts, hashes and empty reads may discover parent structure;
nonempty reads issue newly resolved root checkpoints before reading any
bytes. The compiler never supplies its ghost state to the native continuation.
`erase_compile`, `canonical_compile` and `execute_erasure` prove exact
projection to the original native value/log, owned SHAKE cache and shared
SHA-512 cache. `compile_bind` and `compile_resume` preserve the ledger and
cache across composition/suspension. `read_snapshot` retains the actual
pre-read cumulative hash-log checkpoint through every supported continuation,
even after monitor failure. `actual_helper_snapshot` combines that guarantee
with actual-parent compatibility after partial seed reads.

These are structural and operational guarantees. An initial parent table is
not evidence of authenticated lineage; use an empty ledger or prove it arose
from the same instrumented prelude as the caches/checkpoints. Whole native
root/exposure coverage remains open, including explicit orphan and
receipt-linked exceptions, causal parent selection and trusted context/shape
interpretation. Late discovery is not retroactive security coverage. The
first-original-slot registry map, ordered-prefix grouping, native protocol
composition, attacker-work coupling, rectangular/numerical certification,
BabyBear and fail-closed Rust/scheduler refinement remain mandatory.

## Reconstructed parent state and declared-helper coverage

`NativeParentHistory` reconstructs the complete final ledger and owned SHAKE
cache from the ordered native observations. `compile_records` holds on every
supported free compiled execution, and `simulated_records` transports it
through any typed shared handler. Cache writes retain every returned byte,
including repeats and overlaps. Parent entries and frozen keys are monotone
under arbitrary later observations; splitting the history preserves the same
state by `record_append`.

`NativeParentStateExecution` extends reconstruction to the actual shared
checkpoint handler. The observation fold records newly resolved keys at the
pre-read hash log, advances the owned byte cache with the returned interval,
and updates the common SHA-512 cache/log and passive monitor at real hash
calls. `execute_records_support` proves this full-state invariant for every
supported execution. `execute_records` identifies the entire instrumented
computation with deterministic reconstruction from the original native
value/log computation. No additional coins or ghost-state input to native
continuations are introduced.

`state_law` and `from_empty` give exact conditional/unconditional event
probabilities including ledger, caches, checkpoints and monitor. `prefix_law`
also retains the actual residual native program; `execute_bind` threads every
field across composition. `after_prelude_law` derives all initial fields by
replaying the **same** complete prior log from empty initialization. Its
observed SHAKE cache and canonical shared hash cache are proved equal to the
caches required by the existing posterior law, removing separately supplied
initial ledger/checkpoint certificates for this case.

The `Covered` invariant means that every frozen context/root key has an
actual retained checkpoint. `record_covered`, `fold_covered` and
`execute_covered` preserve it, with `empty_covered` discharging initialization.
This certifies registration, not Merkle availability. `resolved_snapshot`
handles both cases: an already frozen key retains its earlier snapshot; a
newly resolved key is recorded at the current actual pre-read cumulative
hash log. Monitor failure does not prevent retention.

`NativeParentCoverage` now derives pending-parent membership from an earlier
observed input rather than assuming a parent-table entry. Any recognized
parent request observed in a start, raw read (including an empty read), or
shared hash declares its helper contexts. `binding_helper` obtains a context
from the exact canonical bind payload in those decoded frames. Later raw
activity preserves that declaration. With a truthful whole history and the
actual logical 64-byte parent seed quoted by the child, the helper root is
resolved using the history-owned cache even after partial seed reads.
`declared_helper_snapshot` consequently proves a retained checkpoint through
every supported continuation of a later nonempty child read, starting with
all fields reconstructed from the same prelude.

`prior_quote_target` and `prior_quote_event` connect earlier positive-read or
hash child-header candidates to the existing causally selected first-seed
exposure event. Its exact conditional probability remains the previously
proved prior-candidate count divided by `2^512` when **all** logical seed
coordinates were unobserved. This is not yet exhaustive orphan classification
or a lifetime union/work bound, and it gives no 512-bit claim for receipt
inputs or partially exposed seeds.

## Lifetime seed risk and inherited helper-context chains

`CausalExposureLifetime` accumulates the existing causally selected
first-seed-exposure risk over every finite analysis prefix of an unbounded
machine. Its local state is initialized from the actual prelude result, and
every prefix retains that prelude's entire raw log. Earlier child-header
candidates therefore remain in the target set. `lifetime_le_totalCharge`
bounds the union of an inherited bad event and all new exposure events by
the inherited event probability plus the expected sum of the per-step risks.
The nonnegative sum and integral may be infinite. No termination, finite mean,
query cap, discarded rejection path or success floor is assumed. This is a
**probability-risk charge**, not attacker work.

The conditional version retains the prelude result and log boundary as
proof-only data. `retained_history` projects it back to the original history;
it issues no oracle observation. `retained_replay` and `retained_event`
justify its full-history posterior, then `conditional_step_event` composes
that posterior inside the original prelude fiber. `conditional_lifetime_le`
preserves inherited bad probability and averages the same infinite risk sum
inside that fiber. Both the lifetime event and total charge are measurable.
The all-unobserved 64-byte seed premise remains exactly the earlier
first-read predicate; partial seeds and receipt guesses do not receive a
new 512-bit bound.

`NativeParentLineage.Known` is a finite chronological certificate made of
observed native parent requests. It starts with a directly parsed helper
context, follows actual logical seed quotes into later recognized parent
requests, and permits arbitrary intervening raw observations. It has no fixed
ancestry-depth limit. `Known.sound` proves that every such context occurs in
the actual table reconstructed from the same truthful history. The inherited
step uses every compatible old parent and the history-owned partial byte
cache, rather than requiring full seeds or selecting the first seed match.

`resolve_known_helper` extends helper-root resolution to those inherited
contexts. `known_helper_snapshot` consequently proves a retained checkpoint
through every supported continuation of a later positive-length raw read,
with ledger, byte cache, hash cache and checkpoints replayed from the same
empty initialization. A context need not occur directly in the descendant's
own frames. This does not backdate a snapshot for an earlier orphan read,
authenticate native ownership, or establish Merkle availability. Registration
through all compatible partial parents also does not yet supply a
single-context arithmetic loss; partial-seed association/collision accounting
remains part of the global Fiat–Shamir argument.

The next global obligation is to classify every security-relevant native
root/challenge exposure using chronological coverage or an explicit exception,
including inherited source keys and receipt-linked inputs. The risk charge
must then be coupled to an actual attacker-work machine, with prior work and
failure/abort paths retained. Native registry aliases/grouping, trusted
context/shape identity, rectangular/numerical certification, BabyBear,
application soundness/extraction and fail-closed Rust/scheduler refinement
remain required.

## Inherited source keys and causal seed-prequery coverage

`NativeSourceLineage` extends chronological metadata inheritance to complete
source `(context digest,root)` keys. Its `Known` certificate starts with a
source key parsed from an observed parent request, follows actual logical
seed quotes through later parent requests, and permits intervening raw
activity. `binding_source` obtains those keys from the exact canonical bind
payload, including duplicate and otherwise unused entries. `Known.sound`
places every certified key in the table reconstructed from the same truthful
history, using its actual partial byte cache. `resolve_known_source` and
`known_source_snapshot` then provide a retained checkpoint through every
supported continuation of a later nonempty read, even when the descendant
input contains no direct source mentions. Equal roots under different context

slot aliases, query grouping, parameter identity or source availability.

`CausalExposureCoverage` closes the link from a first hit in the complete raw
log to the machine's causally pending request. `read_hits` shows that a seed
hit uses the same complete input, positive count and offset below 64.
`firstRead_of_next_hit` excludes completed states, starts and shared hashes;
`selected_at_first_exposure` proves that the earliest seed hit in an actual
finite machine execution selects exactly the earlier prefix's pending read.
The proof uses actual suspension/resumption and ordered log prefixes, rather
than assuming that an input picked from a later witness was fixed earlier.

`prior_quote_lifetime` places an earlier matching child-header quote in the
existing causal lifetime event. `SeedPrequery` describes this witness using
the first-hit position in a complete machine log. `SeedPrequeryAfter` retains
an arbitrary replayable prelude and uses the pending next read. Both events
are measurable without a measurable/countable attacker-state assumption;
their characterizations combine ordinary replayable prefix events and the
existing first-exposure event. The probability bounds transfer to the same
expected lifetime risk charge, with unconditional and prelude-conditional
forms that keep inherited bad probability. No input-space factor is added to
the loss: the actual pending request selects the input for the bound.

These events concern prior raw observations and an entirely unobserved
logical 64-byte seed. They do not classify a quote appearing for the first
time in the pending input, partial-seed association/collision cases, or
receipt-linked guesses. Exhaustive accepted-verifier coverage must still
prove input-role separation or account for such cases. The risk charge is
still probability accounting, not physical attacker work. Completing global
Fiat–Shamir composition, native registry/group order, trusted contexts,

## Pending seed quotes and derived native ancestry

`PendingSeedQuote` covers a seed quote first appearing in the currently pending
input. Its exact conditional guessing risk is 1/2^512 when all 64 logical seed
bytes remain unseen. This risk combines with earlier quoted-seed risks over an
unbounded execution, retaining prelude and inherited bad events.

`SeedQuoteOrder` proves that outside these two events, every observed input
quoting a producer's seed occurs strictly after that producer's first logical
seed exposure. This includes positive reads outside the seed window and shared
hash calls. Any finite closed dependency graph therefore implies a bad event.

`NativeSeedAncestry` starts from semantic source/helper ancestry and actual
producer-read occurrences, without assuming chronological parent order. It
derives chronological metadata, concrete root resolution before descendant
reads, and retained snapshots in the reconstructed shared oracle state. The
regressions include a distinct-output execution with a partial producer read,
an intervening shared hash, and a descendant read outside its seed window;
the absence of both bad events is proved for every execution prefix.

The two new smoke modules contain 20 examples and 35 guarded public-theorem
axiom reports. These results do not yet establish native accepted-run ancestry,
Merkle availability, partial-seed or receipt risk bounds, arithmetic soundness,
physical attacker-work coupling, or Rust/scheduler refinement. Probability
charges in these lemmas are not a physical-work accounting model.

## Native fork execution and program-machine bridge

`OracleProgramMachine` interprets each native program constructor as the
corresponding causal machine command. Its finite prefixes equal the existing
native program-prefix semantics exactly, including the retained continuation.
Every finite native program execution has a path-dependent completed prefix,
and every shorter machine log is a prefix of that same full native log. This
introduces no uniform retry bound, native cutoff, or physical-work model.

`NativeForkAncestry` obtains the producer seed read from execution of the actual
native fork. Canonical source keys and the helper context survive the shared
lookup's grouped/flattened multiplicity frames and are realized by its actual
initializer. Header preservation through the typed zero-count identity includes
its real receipt frame. Subsequent executed forks inherit source/helper facts
from that header without supplied seed-link equalities or producer-read indices.
The exact program-machine bridge transfers the existing risk-conditioned
chronology theorem to the full native program log.

The new regression uses a native parent with a canonical binding, a raw
prequery, shared lookup initialization, a nested fork and a final challenge.
It checks both equal-root/different-context source keys, helper ancestry,
retention of the raw query, metadata/root resolution before the final read,
and retained checkpoints through supported continuations. Reader starts alone
cannot realize a producer. Sixteen regression examples and twenty guarded
public-theorem axiom reports cover these additions.

The chronology/resolution/snapshot assertions retain the explicit absence of
prior/pending seed-quote bad events. Accepted native application runs still
need exhaustive certificate coverage and byte/domain validation. Merkle
availability, partial-seed and receipt risks, native stage admissibility,
full arithmetic/PCS composition, numerical certification for both fields,
attacker-work coupling, extraction and Rust/scheduler refinement remain open.

## Causal PCS and ordered helper verification

`CausalHashWorkerPool` executes the original raw hash workers inside
`OracleProgram`. Scheduler selection is itself a mixed-oracle program, so
scheduler SHAKE/hash prequeries and worker authentication calls belong to the
same causal history. An accepted pool replays every original worker in the
common final hash cache, including when earlier and later work surround it.
Increasing worker analysis fuel extends the history; it does not impose a
native retry cap. Cancellation preserves the selected scheduler memory and
the complete observed prefix. This is an execution model; physical cost,
fairness, termination and native Rayon refinement remain open.

`NativeGoldPcsProgram` combines the actual native checked PCS prefix, that
worker pool and the existing computed suffix/claim check. The SHAKE reader
is no longer an external functional argument at this entry point. A completed
result derives its preparation, pool result, status and complete history
from the actual program execution. Accepted results enforce the original
claim fold and authenticate every original raw column/path, together with
both coordinate checks, in any truthful enclosing history containing the
actual run. No prepared-prefix or authentication certificate is supplied.
Because the whole execution is an `OracleProgram`, the existing shared lazy
SHAKE/hash interpreters and causal machine translation apply to it.

`NativeGoldHelperVerification.program` runs the actual parent/lookup/equality/
scalar/finish handoff and then verifies its computed helper calls in native
order. Each accepted call advances the transcript and scheduler memory and
records its computed result. The first nonaccepted call stops the loop,
retaining the last accepted progress and the complete failed or suspended
PCS outcome. A derived trace identifies precisely the passed prefix and the
first unpassed call. On completion, receipt order equals the actual helper
plan and its length equals the original helper-root count, using upstream
geometry gates to discharge the literal zip's lengths. Every recorded
helper's raw authentication replays in the final cache of the entire combined
execution, including later helper observations. A `.helpers ... (.done ...)`
result means helper verification completed; it does not mean final source
verification or application acceptance.

The regressions reuse the existing native canonical PCS and false-claim
fixtures without changing their bytes. They check exact mixed-oracle logs,
acceptance, native claim rejection, worker suspension, cancellation and
ordered helper stopping. Synthetic interleavings check scheduler prequeries,
shared hash reuse and cancellation memory. These tests do not constitute a
new full native accepted PBS fixture.

Remaining obligations include grouped source `verify_many`, exact ordered
left-prefix matrix grouping modulo the native field, root/word availability,
global Fiat–Shamir risk accounting, physical-work coupling, both native
parameter profiles, strict adversarial decoding and Rust/Charon/Aeneas/NTT/
SIMD/Div64/scheduler refinement. The full false-PBS/extraction and 128-bit
expected-work theorems remain unproved. The new deterministic authentication
results do not discharge those probability or implementation obligations.

## Original source ownership and native batch binding

`NativeSourceRegistry` computes alias groups from the full original ordered
registry, using both the complete computed context digest and the root.
Each group selects its first original slot, before any unused-source filter.
The owner is at or before each aliased slot, has exactly the same key, is
idempotent and is minimal among original slots. Equal roots with different
contexts remain distinct. These are digest-key facts; parameter equality
still needs the separate context-collision argument. Tests deliberately
include a colliding context oracle to preserve that boundary.

The metadata-bearing initializer erases to the existing native registry
initializer with the same returned parent and complete oracle log. Successful
preparation recovers that metadata and its original registration observations.
`bound_metadata` and `helpers_metadata` derive the original parameter/context/
root correspondence from the actual completed lookup body or helper pipeline;
callers do not supply an alias map or a successful-registration certificate.
An existing native completed-body fixture exercises this derivation.

`NativeGoldQueryGroups` groups response rows by the exact ordered list of
left-prefix matrix pairs. Every matrix retains its width and all ordered
entries; equality compares Goldilocks entries modulo the base field. Group
representatives are first original queries. Suffix differences may share a
response; reordered left matrices do not share merely because another
algebraic summary agrees. Equality keys do not replace the original raw
query bytes. Native binding/shape gates must precede use of the total key
functions.

`NativeGoldBatchBinding` implements native `bind_many`: reject empty or
mismatched counts and invalid query/value/matrix dimensions before context
hashing, compute the actual row-code context, and append the original raw
context/root/queries/values tuple under `mw batched row-code v1`. Returned
bindings retain precisely those checked queries and values for subsequent
response grouping. Serialization failure and rejected binding preserve their
actual observed prefixes. This is the binding prefix of `verify_many`;
shared random-test sampling, responses, ordered columns, worker authentication
and finishing every original claim are now executed by the following layer.
Source-claim/seal/dispatch and application-security composition remain open.

A new differential fixture runs successful native `open_many` and `verify_many`
at HasteBoots commit `dff353006322693cab3dc6b654f82151f658f294` with four
claims and two left-prefix response groups. Lean kernel checks match the
115-byte context-hash input, its 64-byte digest, original query/value encodings,
and the complete 783-byte native transcript prefix ending at batch binding.
It includes a lazy representative equal to zero in the field whose raw wire
bytes differ. This small fixture checks correspondence; it does not certify
the target native parameter profiles or replace Rust refinement.

The final target remains both native Goldilocks/BabyBear profiles, original
degree 1024/LWE dimension 728 and public keys, full protocol/schedule execution,

bridges. Twenty-five theorem axiom guards use only `propext`, `Classical.choice`
and `Quot.sound` (the list-block helper uses a subset).

Remaining work includes native all-group/random/finishing probability
composition with production Fiat–Shamir freshness and complete causal lineage,
application soundness and efficient independent public extraction, native
BabyBear integration, physical attacker-work/numerics, and strict decoder plus
Rust/Charon/Aeneas/NTT/SIMD/Div64/scheduler refinement.


## Native acceptance view and interactive finishing soundness

`NativeGoldBatchRectangularData` projects the actual native response groups and
every original query onto the rectangular message interface. Actual group
encodings equal padded original message chunks; owner-group indices round-trip,
and group-owner left weights equal each original query's ordered left weights.
Accepted original values equal their own right finishing of the assigned shared
response. Every encoder and shape fact is derived from preparation, retaining
backend constructor and primitive-root correctness as explicit premises.

`NativeGoldBatchRectangularChecks` transports actual random and grouped column
checks to the same reindexed source and original typed draw vector. Repeated
draws remain repeated, while actual authentication jobs remain deduplicated.
`NativeGoldBatchRectangularAcceptance.accepted_view` obtains the full analysis
view from native accepted execution, truthful history and absence of source
inconsistency. Its context digest, common log and all 64 snapshots come from the
strong actual-context source witness. These are theorem conclusions, never extra
native verifier inputs. `false_iff_error` identifies falsity of any original
claim against the common analysis table with the rectangular batch error event,
with every random and structured check attached.

`NativeGoldBatchInteractiveSoundness.soundness_bound` composes the actual pure
native `finish` gate with that batch kernel. An arbitrary probabilistic response
procedure can retain private coins/state and depend on the entire earlier test
matrix. Its raw opening payload supplies message chunks without response
enumeration, losslessness, a success floor or a trial cap. Under the interactive
uniform-matrix/fresh-shared-draw experiment, any false original native claim
passing native finishing and all common-source checks has loss
`(minimumDistance / fieldSize)^packingWidth + max(miss(distance-radius), miss(radius+1))`.
No query/group/lane factor is inserted, and packing width is independent of the
code-symbol width.

The regression uses a real prepared three-packing/four-code-width batch with
two original queries and one response group. Ordered draw checks retain
`[7,1,7]`. A second fixture has identity left matrices and different original
right queries. Its honestly encoded nonzero source table makes the second
original claim false, avoiding a vacuous false-event regression. The response
experiment retains the earlier matrix and a private coin, and native finishing
rejects a shared response that passes only the first original query. Thirteen
axiom guards use only the allowed three axioms (owner-group round-trip uses a
subset).

This does not prove that production SHA512/SHAKE execution has the interactive
challenge law: complete first-exposure/causal lineage, including prequeries,
partial caches and orphan/pending/receipt cases, still needs composition. The
common decoder remains an information-theoretic analysis extractor; efficient
independent public extraction and full PBS application soundness remain open.
Native BabyBear integration, physical attacker-work and final 128-bit numerics,
and strict decoder plus Rust/Charon/Aeneas/NTT/SIMD/Div64/scheduler refinement
remain mandatory unfinished work.


## Native shared-budget field and first-stream matrix laws

`BudgetedUniformSequence` models one candidate budget shared across all
coefficients. Rejection consumes a candidate without advancing the coefficient
index. It proves the exact successful tuple law as the actual completion mass
times the joint uniform law, its two-branch completion recurrence and
monotonicity. It does not replace the native global candidate budget with a
separate retry budget per coefficient.

`NativeFieldVectorValues` and `NativeFieldVectorProgram` give exact typed-value
and complete ordered-log projections of actual native execution, including
rejected chunks, accepted prefixes and resumption. Final receipt emission does
not change the completed collector state. `FreshShakeTail` handles the real
cache: arbitrary entries outside the unread tail remain, earlier installed
bytes do not affect later positions, and any entry inside the tail prevents
freshness. `NativeFieldVectorFresh` derives the interpreter's single-candidate
law from canonical masked bytes and uses the actual shared cache transitions.

`NativeFieldVectorLaw` transfers the compiled law to the posterior after a
replayable whole mixed SHA512/SHAKE history. Its finite law retains the computed
completion factor. Native completed events are increasing under actual
resumption; their union over all candidate prefixes is bounded by the joint
uniform event probability. No completion conditioning, success floor or native
attempt limit is imposed. `NativeFieldMatrixLaw` transports this law through a
lane-major finite bijection, keeping modulus, test rows and source rows
independent.

`NativeGoldBatchRandomLaw` derives the actual completed prime request, geometry
count and canonical raw-word conversion from checked native batch preparation.
Its sampler matrix equals `work.random` at native lane-major addresses, then
reindexes to exactly `NativeGoldBatchRectangularChecks.random` on the common
left-cell/source-lane rows. The conditional law and unbounded domination apply
to this same rectangular matrix.

`CausalStreamExposure` selects the actual next first positive read of a complete
input. A first read can occur at any offset. All earlier positive reads of that
input count, including partial/far-offset reads; starts, empty reads and SHA-512
observations do not expose SHAKE coordinates. Eligibility proves the whole
stream is absent from the observed cache. `NativeGoldBatchFirstReadLaw` supplies
the checked native rectangular matrix law at this causal first-read point,
without an external freshness certificate.

Regressions use modulus three to force a rejected first byte, retained partial
coefficients and byte chunks, correct resumed values and read offsets. They
check shared-budget recurrence values `9/16` and `27/32`, actual posterior laws
after a cached read of a different input, rejection of overlapping-cache
freshness, far-offset first exposure and earlier-partial-read exclusion. The
actual three-packing/four-code-width Goldilocks batch supplies its eighteen
coefficients and instantiates the first-read rectangular law. Generic canonical
sampler/matrix transport also typechecks at BabyBear's modulus and width six;
this does not establish native BabyBear Montgomery/PCS integration. Forty-six
new axiom guards use only the allowed three axioms or subsets.

Remaining production obligations include complete first-exposure coverage and
past-measurability of the source/phase metadata through orphan, pending,
partial-seed and receipt lineage; the response-bound ordered-column law and
full global risk composition; efficient public extraction and PBS application
soundness; native BabyBear integration; physical attacker-work and final
128-bit numerics; and strict decoder plus Rust/Charon/Aeneas/NTT/SIMD/Div64/
scheduler refinement.


## Native response-bound column challenge laws

The native Goldilocks batch column request now has an exact first-read posterior
law. Its computed typed vector retains the original ordered draws and duplicates;
a shared-column miss bound applies to all checks without a group or lane factor.
The complete request input binds the raw test row and every raw group response.
Field-equal lazy word aliases therefore remain different committed responses.
Authentication columns and paths are later data and do not enter this nonce.

The native field completion bridge identifies the actual receipt-derived parent.
Receipt replay works when all 64 receipt coordinates are already known, including
split or cloned reads; it does not require a previous complete receipt read.
The regression covers two 32-byte reads, rejects a single partial receipt as
sufficient knowledge, preserves draws [7,1,7], and exercises two response groups
with three original claims. All 24 new theorem axiom guards permit only propext,
Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

This closes a local column-law interface, not the final security theorem. The
law requires receipt knowledge and an actual first read of the complete bound
input. Global causal coverage must still handle earlier unknown-parent guesses,
partially known receipts and seed lineages, orphan/pending requests, and all
attacker histories. Physical work accounting, the public evaluator/extractor,
BabyBear native integration, strict decoding and implementation refinement, and
the final 128-bit application-security inequality remain outstanding.

## Complete-stream chronological coverage and adaptive index charges

`CausalStreamCoverage` locates the first positive read anywhere in a complete
SHAKE stream. Its coverage theorem retains arbitrary inherited mixed histories:
a stream touched in a finite machine prefix was either touched in the prelude
or selected by `CausalStreamExposure.firstRead` at an actual earlier prefix.
Starts, empty reads and SHA-512 observations do not expose SHAKE coordinates.
The locator handles far-offset reads that leave seed coordinates 0–63 untouched.

`NativeGoldBatchStreamCoverage` derives the real ordered-column output and its
positive quota from native preparation and parameter validation. Together with
the existing actual field read, this supplies both stream coverage witnesses.
The native-program interpreter yields a path-dependent completion prefix after
an arbitrary prelude, without a caller-supplied native-log embedding or a
uniform termination/trial bound. The first exposures need not follow the
verifier's later order of use.

`NativeIndexExposureRisk` selects requests and event predicates from the current
complete history and checks eligibility against the actual pending first read.
It retains the complete native result and ordered observation log, proves the
exact conditional and averaged charge, and sums those charges over every
analysis prefix of an unbounded machine. Invalid dimensions, repeated streams
and mismatched pending requests contribute no event or charge. A shared-check
charge has one witness miss bound with the original ordered quota; it does not
acquire a group or lane factor.

Regressions cover far-offset exposure versus the old seed-only locator, empty
reads/hash/start observations, same-stream versus foreign cached reads,
inherited native column prequeries, native field/column coverage, quotas three
and one selected from causal state, overflow rejection, and the shared native
miss bound. Twenty-two theorem axiom guards use only the allowed three axioms
or subsets.

Chronological coverage alone does not prove past-measurability of metadata
selected from a future accepted request. The probability monitor still needs
the protocol-specific history-based selector and the reduction of every false
native acceptance to its charged events, including unknown or partial receipt
and seed lineage. Physical work, public extraction/application semantics,
native BabyBear, strict decoding/refinement, and the final 128-bit inequality
remain open.

`NativeIndexInputView` now recovers an atomic index request from its complete

`NativeGoldBatchColumnInputView` additionally decodes the preceding response

`NativeGoldBatchColumnExposure` selects directly from the actual pending first
stream read, checks the native column label and positive batch quota, and uses
the parsed request and responses in the exact conditional, averaged and
unbounded-lifetime probability charges. No external history-to-request selector
or future prepared work is an input to this selector. In particular, selecting
the complete nonce does not require knowing whether the receipt digest quoted
inside it is valid. A history with only 32 known receipt bytes instantiates the
law and still recovers the actual ordered native draws [7,1,7] and distinct
transport indices [1,7]. The shared-check charge retains the original quota and
one witness miss bound, without a response-group/lane factor.

Regressions also cover every raw group, a lazy Goldilocks word in the second

frames, wrong challenge labels, zero batch quotas and repeated-stream exclusion.
Twenty new theorem axiom guards permit only the allowed three axioms or subsets.

The new parser is an analysis view of complete SHAKE inputs, not a refinement of
the Rust proof deserializer. Trusted parameter/profile identity, source ownership

`NativeGoldBatchFieldInputView` recovers the exact Goldilocks field request

`NativeGoldBatchChallengeLink` recovers the field prefix and exact 80-byte raw

## Early receipt keys as guesses of consumed field-byte prefixes

`NativeFieldConsumedPrefix` now proves that actual collector completion consumes

`NativeReceiptPrefixView` extracts raw field-byte prefixes named by receipt query

`NativeEarlyReceiptPrefixRisk` selects an actual pending first column read,

keys name that field stream's raw prefix. Exact conditional and averaged laws

the denominator is 2^576. The measurable lifetime event and total probability

Twenty-five theorem axiom guards permit only the allowed three axioms or subsets.

This closes the earlier-receipt-key prefix-guess charge, not the full early

## Fresh receipt digests and the combined early-receipt bound

`NativeFieldObservationScope` proves that every actual collector observation is
an output under its original field input, including rejected candidates and
resumed states. Collection preserves the absence of every distinct receipt key.
`OracleProgramHistory` retains the entire selecting result/log alongside a
history-selected native program's result and full log, with replay and
measurability lemmas for posterior refinement.

`NativeFreshReceiptDigest` uses the actual native collector in that retained
history. Once its result is known, its receipt key is also known. If that key
was unseen in the original history, the collector has not exposed it: the
parsed field input is disjoint from the receipt domain. A full native receipt
payload matching the pending quote implies a match of its 64-byte digest, giving
the conditional 2^-512 bound. The full 80-byte payload is retained in the event;
no consumed-length decoding, nonwrapping premise or completion normalization is
introduced. Complete and suspended collector outcomes remain in the averaging.

`NativeFreshReceiptLifetime` proves stability after completion and takes the
increasing union over all collector budgets. A second lifetime bound ranges
over every actual machine prefix. Only selected early nonces have a fresh-digest
charge, so completed/repeated/ineligible machine prefixes add zero.

`NativeEarlyReceiptBound` combines this branch with the earlier receipt-key
prefix branch. For a recovered Goldilocks phase with at least nine coefficients,
a matching completed receipt at any budget lies in one of those two events.
An eligible nonce has charge qPrefix/2^576 + 1/2^512, where qPrefix is the
cardinality of the deduplicated raw-prefix target set in the original history.
Exact posterior refinement, measurability, averaging and the unbounded-machine
lifetime inequality are proved without a rejection or attacker-lifetime cap.
The native test-width-at-least-three geometry supplies the coefficient bound.

Regressions exercise a previously unseen receipt key chosen from newly collected
bytes, genuine full receipt matching, one-byte prior receipt knowledge, exclusion
of that partially cached key from the fresh branch, both combined charges,
completion stability, rejected-byte log scope, and retention of the full old
selecting history. Thirty-one theorem axiom guards permit only the allowed
three axioms or subsets; the history projection equality is axiom-free.

## Native field-to-column posterior composition

`NativeGoldBatchChallengeScope` proves that a parsed complete column nonce
strictly extends its recovered field input in encoded byte length. Thus the
actual native collector, including rejects and suspended prefixes, cannot
expose that column stream. This separation requires neither a correct receipt
quote nor a collision assumption.

`NativeIndexUnseenLaw` extends the original ordered-index laws to arbitrary
replayable retained histories. `NativeGoldBatchFieldColumnLaw` retains the
entire original selecting history and the actual field collector result/log,
derives column freshness from the original pending first read and the input
separation theorem, and proves the exact conditional uniform law on each
retained fiber. Averaging those fibers gives an exact original-posterior
identity for every predicate depending on the collector state and the ordered
column vector. Incomplete outcomes keep their original mass. Prior partial
field and receipt queries are permitted; no complete receipt knowledge or
field-stream freshness certificate is required for this column law.

`NativeGoldBatchFieldColumnBound` applies that identity to a family of column
checks depending on all collected field values. Given a disagreement witness
for each reachable completed state in the original posterior, the probability
of all checks passing is bounded by one shared ordered-quota miss term.
Completion stability gives the same bound over all collector budgets, with
no retry, group, or lane factor and no completion normalization.

The regression uses the actual native 32-column fixture with ordered draws
[7, 1, 7], two state-dependent checks, a single disagreeing column, a partially
queried field input and one prior receipt byte. It checks suspension versus
completion, retention of the original history, and the unchanged single miss
term (31/32)^3. Fourteen new theorem axiom guards cover the production lemmas.

This establishes the field-to-column sampling composition. It does not yet
lift arbitrary false native acceptance into the required source disagreement
witness, bind the recovered field matrix to the first-field-exposure source,
or provide the independent public extractor. Global lineage coverage, PBS
semantics, native BabyBear, physical attacker work, strict implementation
refinement and the final 128-bit theorem also remain open. Auxiliary collector
reads are posterior analysis, with no physical-work claim.

The next integration step is to express the random/group check family in
`NativeGoldBatchRectangularChecks` using only trusted fixed parameters, the
recovered nonce binding/responses, the retained coefficient state, and a source
fixed by the selecting history. Its present `Prepared`-indexed representation
cannot simply be treated as past-measurable. Then prove that actual native
acceptance supplies these same checks and the disagreement witness outside
the field-proximity event, while retaining every original finishing claim.
This representation/ownership obligation precedes combining the native
first-field law and the column law into the full Fiat–Shamir reduction.

## Parsed response families and pointwise false-claim witnesses

`NativeGoldBatchFixedResponseData` defines the ordered original-query left
weights, first-original group owners, finishing right weights, raw response
messages and original claimed values from fixed parameters and serialized data.
The definitions take no oracle world, prepared work, plan root or scheduler.
Total indexing is analysis only: equality with native projections is proved
at the original validated indices, preserving low-bit matrix order and all
original right queries. Test and code packing widths remain independent.

`NativeGoldBatchParsedResponseData` derives the binding of those data to a
successfully parsed actual native column nonce, using the native preparation
and explicit framing bounds. Its derived analysis facts retain every raw test
and group response, query and claimed value. Each resulting function is proved
equal to the corresponding native response or finishing projection. The
analysis binding is not a verifier input or a freshness/source certificate.

`RectangularBatchDisagreement` separates the deterministic disagreement facts
from the interactive probability theorem. In the near branch, a false original
message finishing forces one structured response to disagree on at least
code-distance-minus-radius columns. Outside the random-matrix proximity event,
a coded random-test response disagrees on at least radius+1 columns.

`NativeGoldBatchFalseClaimWitness.near_witness` derives the near witness from
actual accepted native finishing and a false original claimed value against
the common analysis extraction. Its result uses a natural group index bounded
by the parsed query data and a lane of the fixed width; no future Prepared index
is needed in the response-family definition or witness predicate. The far
witness uses the recovered-state matrix and parsed raw test response. Neither
witness introduces a query/group/lane factor or a probabilistic independence
assumption.

Regressions exercise B*A versus A*B, lazy field representatives, first-original
owners, the three-test/four-packing geometry, parsed response transports, and an
actual accepted native run with distinct finishing suffixes for two original
claims in one group. A separately supplied coded analysis word makes the second
original claim false and produces the near-branch distance witness. This tests
the pointwise finishing implication; authentication of that analysis word is
supplied separately by the earlier selected-source results. Eighteen axiom
guards cover the new production lemmas.

Next, combine these witnesses with the earlier-history-selected source and
native first-field/column posterior laws into the complete causal probability
reduction. The column history must recover the same source prefix used by the
first field exposure, rather than silently replacing it with a future source.
Registry/context ownership, complete seed/lookup lineage coverage, independent
public extraction, PBS semantics, native BabyBear, physical-work accounting,
strict implementation refinement and final 128-bit numerics remain open.

## Recovering the first field source and bounding witnessed column events

`CausalFirstStreamPrefix` recovers the complete mixed-log prefix preceding a
stream's earliest positive read. Its soundness theorem identifies the actual
output, offset and nonempty bytes. Starts, hashes and empty reads remain in
the prefix but do not count as exposure. Once recovered, that prefix is
unchanged by arbitrary suffixes; no seed-window or lifetime cap is used.

`NativeGoldBatchFirstFieldSource` uses this prefix to recover the earlier
selected common source log from a later history. The strict linked-column
parser supplies its exact canonical field input. If that stream has already
been exposed, recovery succeeds; the recovered source has all 64 checkpoint
snapshots and remains unchanged after suffixes or actual auxiliary collector
reads. The source is computed from the old selecting history and parsed data,
not a future native preparation or a later hash log.

`NativeGoldBatchRecoveredSourceAvailability` proves that actual later native
acceptance uses that recovered source for every authenticated payload and
native column equation, outside the existing global disagreement event. Its
column-history theorem derives the actual field phase from the parsed native
column input, preserves the source through all later verification queries,
and needs no future source-log witness or supplied checkpoint certificate.

`NativeGoldBatchWitnessedColumnBound` bounds the event that a completed state
both has a distance witness and passes every shared column check. Unlike the
older unconditional-witness lemma, it does not require every completed state
to have a false response. Unwitnessed and suspended states retain their full
original probability mass. Exact posterior refinement gives the single
ordered-quota miss bound, and completion stability extends it over all native
collector budgets without a retry, group or lane factor. Measurability of the
all-budget event is also proved.

Regressions exercise ignored starts/empty reads, a first field read at offset
999, retention of hashes and other-input reads in the recovered prefix,
arbitrary suffixes, and preservation under auxiliary collection. An actual
accepted native run uses the source recovered before an intervening hash in
its column history. The probability regression includes a completed correct
state with no disagreement witness, demonstrating that no unconditional
witness premise is needed, as well as a witnessed passing state. Eighteen
new axiom guards cover the production lemmas.

Next, instantiate the witnessed event with the concrete combined random and
structured response family and the recovered old-history source. Map accepted
false original claims into that event or the first-field proximity event,
then apply complete causal exposure coverage and lifetime averaging. The
registry/context binding, remaining seed/lookup lineage, independent public
extractor, PBS semantics, native BabyBear, physical attacker work, strict
implementation refinement and final 128-bit inequality remain open.

## Concrete native column family and causal lifetime charge

`NativeGoldBatchConcreteColumnFamily` instantiates the test family with a sum
of random rows and parsed structured group/lane pairs. Both branches use the
same recovered source word and one ordered column vector. Raw combinations
use the actual retained coefficient state or the ordered structured weights;
claimed responses are computed from all parsed raw test/group rows. All
claimed responses are proved coded. These definitions take fixed parameters,
parsed data and the selected source log, with no arbitrary response callback
or future prepared work. Test width and code packing width remain separate.

`NativeGoldBatchConcreteColumnBound` instantiates the all-budget witnessed
bound with this family. Its source is computed from the selecting history by
first-field prefix recovery. The winning event contains its own disagreement
witness and all shared checks; correct or suspended states are not normalized
away. The distance is min(code-distance-minus-radius, radius+1), and its miss
term is proved equal to the maximum of the two branch miss terms. No union
factor is introduced for choosing a branch or response test.

`NativeGoldBatchConcreteColumnExposure` derives selection from the actual
pending first positive read and complete linked-column parser, checks the
native label, positive ordered quota and fixed code domain, and computes the
source from the old history. It proves the local conditional inequality,
measurability, averaging and a lifetime inequality over all causal machine
prefixes and all collector budgets. The risk is zero for ineligible/repeated
inputs and when no earlier field source is recoverable. The latter case
remains covered separately by the early-receipt reduction; zero column risk
does not assert that the complete native security loss is zero there.

`NativeGoldBatchConcreteColumnWitness` lifts the actual accepted-native
near-branch false-claim witness and the recovered-matrix far-branch witness
into this sum family at the minimum distance used by the causal bound.
The near lift retains the false original claim and parsed group bound.

transported columns in the native three-test/four-packing fixture. They check

column reads, source preservation over arbitrary suffixes, and the full
unbounded lifetime theorem. Fourteen new axiom guards cover the production
lemmas. These are probability charges, not physical attacker-work costs.

Next, prove that every accepted native false claim outside the first-field

This still needs the exact parsed-request draw identity and transport of all

## Independent private coins for the native lifetime bound

`PrivateCoinLifetime.prelude_bound` now integrates the existing native
Goldilocks lifetime bound over an independent private-coin measure. The coin
space can be arbitrary and can contain an infinite random tape. Both the
prelude and continuation strategy may depend on the coin outcome. The event
still quantifies over all finite continuation lengths; the theorem introduces
neither a fuel limit nor a union-bound factor for the number of coin outcomes.
The charges include the causal prelude through the existing clean-machine
rebasing theorem. Public parameters/profile remain fixed as before.

The product measure explicitly specifies independence of private coins and the
ideal oracle. Joint measurability of the failure event is required for arbitrary
coin spaces. `failure_measurable_countable` discharges it for countable spaces
with measurable singletons using the existing causal replay theorem.
`failure_measurable_selection` also discharges it when an arbitrary tape makes
a measurable choice among countably many strategies. General adaptive use of
an infinite native random tape still needs its own joint-measurability
refinement; sectionwise oracle measurability alone is insufficient.

`independent_work_bound` and `independent_scaled_work_bound` preserve a
per-coin calibration under averaging, including the intended finite factor
`2^128`. They use an unconditional expectation over entire executions and
require joint almost-everywhere measurability of the proposed work function.
Their work-calibration inequalities are explicit hypotheses. No native
physical-work calibration, public PBS security theorem or final 128-bit
security claim has been established by these lemmas.

coin event, a countably infinite family with coin-dependent oracle offsets,
the instantiated native lifetime inequality, measurable selection from an
infinite Boolean tape with its product sigma algebra, and preservation of the

## Joint measurability from finite private-tape execution

`PrivateCoinReplay` now derives joint measurability on the product of an
infinite byte tape and the existing ideal-oracle world from finite tape use
and causal oracle replay. For every actual finite execution, `FiniteUse`
requires some finite tape prefix to fix its oracle log at that world. The
prefix length may depend on both the tape and oracle responses. There is no
uniform bound on that length. Each such prefix and log determine a whole
product cylinder by replay. Countably many finite byte certificates establish
measurability; the probability bound still integrates over tapes and does not
apply a union bound over them. Impossible oracle logs are handled explicitly
when proving their agreement sets measurable.

`PrivateCoinNativeMeasurable` applies this result to native accepted-false-claim
witnesses using the existing replay-to-history characterization. Joint
measurability follows if each finite native history satisfies `FiniteUse`.
The union over continuation fuel retains all lifetime witnesses.

`PrivateCoinMachine` gives compositional conditions that establish that
finite-use property for causal machine histories. `FiniteResult` preserves the
entire prelude result/log under a sufficiently long finite tape prefix;
`FiniteStep` preserves each chosen command under such a prefix. The command
condition includes its stored response continuation, rather than merely its
request input. Finite-result preservation is closed under bind and is proved
for every finite machine prefix. Prelude and command bounds are combined only
along the actual execution, so later oracle responses can select different
private coordinates and total coin use can grow without limit.
`PrivateCoinMachine.failure_measurable` consequently discharges the previous
joint-measurability premise for these machine families.

The regression begins with the actual native verifier prelude, samples an
initial cursor from a private byte, and then chooses later tape coordinates
from oracle responses. It proves finite-use conditions, their composition,
the native failure event's measurability, and the lifetime probability bound
under an infinite product law of private bytes independent of the oracle.
A separate regression proves that no one finite tape prefix fixes all its
commands. Five examples and two named fixture lemmas exercise the connection;
twelve guards audit every new production theorem, with only the usual three
allowed axioms or subsets (three proofs use none).

This closes the model-level measurability gap for finitary private-coin
commands, including strategies that cannot be selected by inspecting just one
fixed finite tape prefix. It does not establish that the Rust random source,
its command boundaries, local divergence, compiler, or physical work refine
this model. Those implementation obligations remain, together with trusted
registry/parameter binding, public extraction/PBS security, BabyBear coverage,
and the physical-work calibration needed for the final 128-bit inequality.

## Private-coin scores and specified byte-work bounds

`PrivateCoinScores` extends the finite-certificate argument from oracle logs
to entire execution results. Private state can vary even when every oracle
log is empty, so log-only measurability is insufficient for work counters.
Full-result finite tape dependence and causal oracle replay now make every
result/log predicate and nonnegative score jointly measurable, without a
measurable-space or countability assumption on the state type. Countable
indices are finite byte-prefix/oracle-log certificates; the chosen payload
itself need not be used as a countable index.

Lifetime scores are suprema over all finite prefixes. Their measurability
and exact product-expectation formula require no finite mean or termination
premise. For increasing cumulative scores, expected lifetime score equals
the supremum of expected finite-prefix scores. The monotonicity condition is
explicit and is discharged by the existing closed interpreter's work theorem
in the concrete instantiation below.

`PrivateCoinClosedWork` connects these results to the existing closed byte
interpreter's actual work counter. Installed private data may depend on the
infinite random tape, provided each installation depends on some finite tape
prefix. Work includes the existing initialization charge, silent local
instructions, unsuccessful instructions and stopped-state behavior. The
product expectation equals the average of the previous fixed-private-input
expected-work function. Both expected initialization work and the sum of
expected actual tick costs are bounded by that same lifetime expectation.
No acceptance-conditioned distribution or incomplete-run filter is used.

`PrivateCoinClosedGoldRisk.lifetime_le_work` now bounds the existing
field-proximity/column-exposure lifetime event under private random
initialization by `(17 / 2^141)` times unconditional expected specified
byte-work. The bound is derived from the existing calibrated interpreter
theorem, not supplied as an extra per-coin work-calibration hypothesis.
`scaled_exposure_bound` consequently proves the `2^128`-scaled inequality for
this exposure component in those specified work units. Joint measurability
of the exposure event is derived using the countable space of installed
finite byte inputs and their measurable tape fibers.

These are still specified interpreter prices, not physical attacker-work
prices. The exposure event excludes source/hash/receipt exceptions and full
application coverage. Moreover, this concrete closed-interpreter theorem
randomizes installed finite private data; it does not yet add a priced
runtime random-tape instruction. General finitary runtime coin choices are
covered by the score-measurability theorem and its adaptive-machine regression,
but connecting all their consumed coins to a priced native execution remains
open. The final false-PBS security theorem is not established.

## Runtime private-byte instructions and complete work accounting

`PrivateCoinByteMachine` now extends the existing closed byte instruction
set with a runtime `coin` instruction. Base instructions call the original
`ClosedByteMachine.issue` semantics. A coin reads the private tape at the
persistent cursor, stores that byte in the selected register, and advances
the cursor once. It emits no oracle observation. The cursor is separate from
the ordinary machine state, so base instructions cannot rewrite it. Oracle
requests still use the original shared world.

The specified price of a coin is two work units: one for the instruction and
one for its consumed private byte. This is a declared interpreter price,
not a measured native RNG cost. Initialization installs finite code/private
input and charges one additional unit for the private cursor. The infinite
tape is not installed or charged in advance. Stopped states stutter without
consuming coins or work; out-of-code and failed ordinary instructions retain
their existing charged abort behavior.

The operational proofs establish exact per-tick work and cursor changes,
prefix suspension/resumption, work monotonicity and a prefix invariant that
twice the consumed-coin count is bounded by that same work counter. Every
finite prefix depends on finitely many private tape coordinates, while the
complete execution can consume arbitrarily many. The finite-use proof bound
is not used as a work charge or a preloaded tape length.

`PrivateCoinByteWork` proves exact summation of actual instruction costs and
joint measurability of the new prefix/lifetime counters. Expected work is an
unconditional expectation on the private-tape/oracle product law and equals
the supremum of expected finite-prefix work. Initialization, local steps,
coin reads, unsuccessful termination and infinite execution remain in it.
The sum of expected executed tick costs and expected lifetime consumed-coin
cost are bounded by that expectation. No termination or finite-mean premise
is introduced.

`PrivateCoinByteEmbedding` proves conservative behavior for base-only code:
from the same charged ordinary state and any private cursor, the full
ordinary result and oracle log are retained exactly and the cursor stays
unchanged. Installing base-only code adds exactly the declared one-unit
cursor initialization charge to the previous initial work. Thus the runtime
extension does not replace or reinterpret the old instruction semantics.

Fourteen regressions and two fixture lemmas check one- versus two-coin
halt/reject paths with work 20 and 22, unused coins after halt, charged abort,
a private byte selecting the next actual SHAKE input, exact unconditional
averaging of the two branch costs, measurable lifetime work, prefix-limit
expectations, consumed-coin accounting and base-code embedding. A finite
coin/jump loop is proved to consume exactly `n` private bytes after `2*n`
instructions for every natural `n`, with no maximum iteration count.
Twenty-six guards audit all new production theorems. Both root libraries
import the new modules.

The earlier quantitative executable-extractor/configuration-union theorems
still apply to their original closed-interpreter/private-initialization
model. They have not yet been transferred to arbitrary programs containing
the new runtime coin instruction. Next, extend the request classification,
lineage and root/receipt/field/column hazard-to-work proofs to this operational
extension, preserving the actual shared history and work counter. The new
model accepts fixed finite installed private input; random initialization
can run as explicit coin-consuming code before oracle queries. Binding this
to actual native randomness and its initialization/generation cost remains
open, together with application coverage, actor-cost separation, public PBS
semantics, native BabyBear support and physical/native implementation
refinement. The final security goal remains open.

## Runtime-coin requests, lineage and executable-failure coverage

`InstructionClock` provides reusable iteration of single-instruction commands.
A `done next` command returns that instruction's next state and iteration
continues; it does not terminate the whole machine. Finite prefixes resume
exactly, retain the actual residual state and append the same mixed oracle
history. First positive stream exposures are located on that instruction
clock and recover the complete earlier history, including inherited prequeries.

`PrivateCoinByteRequest` constructs the exact command of the runtime-coin
interpreter. Base instructions lift the existing ordinary request and retain
the private cursor in every response continuation. Coin/local instructions
are silent commands returning their real next state. `command_exact` and
`take_exact` link this classification and the reusable clock to the actual
priced interpreter, without a replacement evaluator or an assumed request
trace. A newly positive read supplies the existing first-read selector;
private coin steps cannot fabricate such an exposure.

`PrivateCoinByteLineage` derives first-read packets and full history splits
from the actual runtime-coin execution. It locates the instruction index,
proves the conditional-law selector chooses that input there, recovers the
same earlier mixed log and retains the first positive output plus the entire
later suffix. There is no observation-count proxy for instruction time and
no fabricated start or reset of the private cursor/oracle history.

`PrivateCoinByteNativeCoverage.accepted_coverage` now extends the native
accepted-false-analysis-claim coverage theorem to this interpreter. Actual
native acceptance/log inclusion, parsed-view and response-fit premises are
retained. First-read packets and source-history splits are derived rather
than supplied as additional premises. The conclusion is source disagreement,
early receipt, field proximity or column exposure on this same runtime-coin
execution.

`PrivateCoinByteFailure` defines the lifetime executable-source-extractor
failure event for runtime-coin programs. It reuses the existing executable
witness type, which is independent of the interpreter's state type, and
proves its log-level equivalence to the analysis witness under the existing
calibrated target certificate. Its `failure_covered` theorem derives the
combined root/source, early-receipt and field/column hazard event. Joint
measurability of every finite failure prefix and the unbounded lifetime event
follows from full-result finite tape use and oracle replay; no new

## Quantitative executable soundness with runtime private coins

The runtime-coin hazard-pricing gap above is now closed in the specified
interpreter work model. `PrivateCoinByteFixed` exposes sections of the actual
joint execution/work functions with an arbitrary private tape fixed. It
neither replaces the interpreter nor installs a fuel-dependent finite tape.
Its positive active-instruction cost and tick-sum bound use the existing
runtime coin counter, including the two-unit cost of each consumed byte.

`PrivateCoinByteGoldRisk` transfers the calibrated field/column exposure
laws to this execution, bounding their lifetime probability by
`(17 / 2^141)` times expected work for that fixed tape.
`PrivateCoinByteLogWork` and `PrivateCoinByteRootBudget` derive log length,
receipt-guess, actual input-byte, registry-pool and hash-key budgets from the
same executed instruction counter. Silent coin instructions add work without
adding oracle inputs or source-ledger mentions.

`PrivateCoinByteRootFailure` locates the first global source/hash failure at
an actual hash instruction. `PrivateCoinByteRootWork` pays its low-work
hazard with the derived budgets and its high-work branch by Markov, yielding
the existing `1 / 2^159` rate. `PrivateCoinByteReceiptWork` analogously obtains
the `1 / 2^255` early-receipt rate. Their work thresholds are analysis splits,
not operational caps; no long run, large query, retry or private-coin tail is
removed. The numerical threshold inequalities reuse the previously proved
arithmetic results, while the execution and work bounds are derived for the
new interpreter.

`PrivateCoinByteAllRisk` combines all four hazards on that same fixed-tape
execution. Its total rate is
`1 / 2^159 + (17 / 2^141 + 1 / 2^255)`, bounded by `18 / 2^141`.
`PrivateCoinByteSoundness` then uses the previously proved executable failure
coverage and joint measurability. It first derives the failure probability
bound for every fixed private tape and then averages the failure event itself
over the independent tape/oracle product law. No joint-measurability premise
for individual hazard events, no assumed per-tape work calibration, and no
finite expected-work or termination premise is introduced.

The resulting `scaled_lifetime_bound` proves
`2^128 * P[an accepted false executable-source claim at any prefix]`
is at most `9/4096` times unconditional expected specified interpreter work.
This covers arbitrary runtime coin use, rather than only randomized finite
installed data. Initialization, silent computation, private generation steps,
unsuccessful termination and infinite running remain in that work expectation.
The native acceptance/log and parsed-view premises are retained by the failure
predicate; the claim is still the executable common-source extraction claim.

`PrivateCoinByteConfigurationUnion` extends the quantitative result to any
finite family of calibrated targets sharing that execution and counter.
Its scaled factor is the target count times `9/4096`; at most 256 configured
targets give `9/16`. This is not a cap on attacker attempts, execution length,
queries or consumed coins. Coverage of actual application contexts by the
configured family remains to be proved.

Thirteen regressions check positive coin work with zero field/column,
root and receipt risk, actual mixed-log/input budgets, per-tape receipt and
source bounds, the combined fixed-tape and product-law executable bounds,
and the shared-counter family allowance. Fifty-seven guards audit all new
production theorems. Both root libraries import the modules. The fixtures
remain operational/calibration fixtures, not a complete native PBS run.

The prices are still declared byte-interpreter prices. Native cache reuse,
RNG generation, compiler/ABI/lifetime behavior and actor-cost separation have
not been refined to these counters or to physical attacker work. The work
also assumes the existing calibrated target geometry and trusted query quota;
native registry/profile/quota binding and application-family coverage remain
open. Public PBS semantics, efficient public extraction and native BabyBear
coverage remain open. The final physical-work security goal is not achieved.

at a root of `X^N+1` turns negacyclic multiplication into field multiplication.
The proof accounts explicitly for upper coefficients wrapping with a minus
sign; it does not assume convolution or transform correctness.

The existing odd, bit-reversed root-domain theorem then supplies multiplicativity
of the proved butterfly transform. Distinct nodes and the existing polynomial
encoder injectivity theorem supply transform injectivity. Consequently, a
pointwise transformed external-product identity uniquely determines the original
coefficient-domain result. The theorems cover arbitrary prime modulus, arbitrary

polynomial output point. Truthful digit, public-key and result NTT relations

optimized loop equals ordered matrix folding of the geometric coefficient
cells. Query matrices are never commuted. Lane initialization includes the
shift of its lane-only reversed address by the coefficient-bit count, matching
reversal over the entire polynomial width.

identity as a premise. The single coefficient-step identity is valid over a
commutative semiring; monomial materialization uses the prime-field setting.

## Ordered accumulator shift and endpoint row queries (2026-11-10)

`AccumulatorShiftQueries` proves the exact row-query transformation used by
`packed_accumulator::shift_queries`. Its non-wrap query list selects the first
set bit of the source row in increasing bit order. At that bit it places the
pair's zero-branch matrix, multiplied on the right by the accumulated lower one-matrices;
previous bits are zero selectors with identity matrices, and higher query
pairs are retained. The wrap query selects row zero and places the complete
ordered lower product at its first selector. This matches the native placement,
including its explicit zero-row-variable case. Lists retain every branch;
the number of returned shift queries is proved to be `row_variables + 1`.

A pointwise matrix-weight proof shows that the sum of these
branch weights at source row r is exactly the original weight at r-1 modulo
the padded row domain. The low accumulator always multiplies each one-matrix
on the left. Carry and wrap proofs never commute matrix factors. The indexed
query's weights are connected to the existing list-weight semantics, and its
fold is connected to the weighted evaluation of that same source. Reindexing
by a proved predecessor/successor bijection then gives `shifted_fold`: summing
all branch evaluations equals evaluating the input table at cyclic successor
rows. `successor_index` identifies that successor with `(t+1) % M` in the
original flat row addresses, yielding `shifted_fold_flat`.

The same module formalizes the row selector used by `select_row` and proves
that its fold returns exactly the selected row. This supplies the row-block
meaning of the initial/final endpoint queries, without a supplied row-selection
certificate. These results apply to arbitrary source vectors and arbitrary
field-valued matrix query pairs; the row-variable and lane counts are generic.

and the preceding modulus-17 noncommuting matrix fixture. They check original

zero-dimensional row equality needs no axioms). Both root libraries import

## Complete packed accumulator query identities (2026-11-10)

`AccumulatorPackedQueries` embeds the preceding row-query algebra into complete
coefficient/row/half queries. Its indexed append preserves the original list
order and has a proved split-fold identity. The full-query coordinate theorem
puts coefficients in the low cell bits, then rounds, then the ciphertext half,
with address `cell + 2^c * (row + 2^r * half)`. `whole_fold` gives the staged
matrix evaluation of that same complete source. No query-dependent source or
supplied prefix/suffix equivalence is introduced.

`shiftWhole` changes only the row block, retaining each original coefficient
pair and the final half pair in every carry/wrap query. Its list theorem states
those literal blocks, and `shiftWhole_fold` sums their complete-source evaluations
to the cyclic row-successor evaluation. `selectWhole_fold` gives the initial/
final row-selection meaning while preserving both other query blocks.
`selectHalf_fold` retains the sum of the two original half matrices, and
`duplicate_fold` proves equality with an appropriately duplicated source under
its explicit pointwise duplication relation. These are the complete-query
identities used for the native decomposition-a/decomposition-b input links.

The fixed-row impulse fold is the ordered row-weight matrix acting on the
endpoint vector. Coefficient evaluation commutes with this fixed row support.
`whole_impulse` therefore gives the endpoint correction with row weighting on
the inside and the original half matrices on the outside, matching
`row_weight`/`mix_halves`. `continuity_check` combines the full shifted-input
sum, the output opening and the two endpoint corrections: the literal native
check follows from the pointwise cyclic coefficient/round/half equation. No
matrix factors are commuted. Source-fold additivity and subtraction are proved
as well; the remaining arithmetic equations use those same fixed queries.
This implication is exact algebra, not randomized-check soundness or a converse.

The seven original source positions and their per-source query order are
specified without merging slots: INPUT_ACC, MONOMIAL_PRODUCT, EXTERNAL_INPUT,

`AccumulatorQuerySplit` gives fixed coefficient/row/half coordinates for the

`AccumulatorMatrixSoundness` constructs five fixed residual sources from the

links and corrected cyclic continuity. Half copying, row advancement and the

ordered endpoint corrections from the preceding checkpoint.

`CoreCheck` states the five literal equations on truthful complete-query source

`KeySwitchExtraction` fixes the public coefficient mask and target used by

The three sources preserve native factor order: signed increment, public mask,
public target. Packing retains all coefficient/lane/half coordinates through
the existing canonical polynomial equivalence. The equality between `c+1` and

`false_zero_relation` exposes a false extraction as a false fixed ZeroCheck
