The native extraction verifier does not authenticate three separate factors:

increment. `values` mirrors those literal terminal roles using the same full
ordered query. `checked_truthful_or_wrong_increment` specializes the terminal
alternative to exactly that private increment value. A checked terminal
therefore produces a truthful reduced subclaim or a wrong increment value;

That identity can be supplied by the preceding NTT/canonical-digit bridge.

The kernel-checked degree-four modulus-17 fixture checks both public mask

`SingleOpeningFirstFieldSource` selects the source from the actual history

`SingleOpeningFieldExposure` selects the strict single-opening field view from

`SingleOpeningChallengeScope` derives strict encoded-input length separation

for every budget and world, including rejection and suspended outcomes.

`SingleOpeningFieldColumnLaw` extends the original replayable history by the
actual native field collector and retains its whole result and observation
log. On each refined posterior fiber, the original ordered column vector is
jointly uniform. The original-posterior law averages every collector outcome;
it neither resets the history nor conditions away noncompletion. First-read
eligibility comes from the original machine packet, with arbitrary earlier
hashes and reads at other inputs retained.

`SingleOpeningWitnessedColumnBound` bounds completed collection with both a
column-distance witness and all shared checks by one `ColumnOpening.missBound`.

states do not require a disagreement premise. Completion makes these events
monotone over collector budgets; the union over all budgets has the same bound.
There is no retry, lane or number-of-tests multiplier. This is a generic
sampling bound: concrete fixed-source error families and actual false-claim
coverage still have to instantiate it.

`SingleOpeningRecoveredMatrix.random` depends only on the fixed original
context dimensions and retained collector state. The actual native sampling
receipt identifies this matrix with the rectangular native random weights.

state. `acceptance_random_checks` transports the actual accepted native checks

## Single-opening early receipts and first-column classification

`SingleOpeningEarlyReceiptPrefixRisk` selects an actual first positive column
read with a strictly parsed single-opening nonce and wholly unseen recovered
field stream. The original atomic-column label is checked, but is shared with
the batch protocol: protocol separation comes from the original single field,
binding, response and receipt framing, not distinct column labels. A positive
partial read of a receipt key contributes its complete raw-prefix candidate;
starts and empty reads contribute none. The exact conditional target law uses
the original replayable past. The 72-byte prefix risk is the number of distinct
prior receipt-prefix targets divided by `2^576`, including arbitrary read
offsets. Native collection derives the prefix from actual completion, with
all rejected candidates retained.

`SingleOpeningFreshReceiptDigest` retains the complete actual native collector
outcome and log. The encoded field input cannot equal any receipt key. Thus
collection cannot expose a receipt key that was unseen in the original past,
even though this key depends on the collected bytes. On each retained fiber,
a fresh receipt digest has probability at most `2^-512`; averaging includes
both completed and suspended collector states. Whole original receipt payloads
are compared; no consumed-length decoding or nonwrapping assumption is added.

`SingleOpeningFreshReceiptLifetime` takes the monotone union over all collector
budgets and all actual machine prefixes, with inherited events explicit and
no retry or success-floor normalization. `SingleOpeningEarlyReceiptBound`
combines the already-queried-key and fresh-key branches. For at least nine
Goldilocks coefficients, its selected risk is
`(# distinct 72-byte prefix targets)/2^576 + 1/2^512`.
Conditional, averaged and unbounded lifetime bounds retain actual history;
these are probability charges, not yet physical attacker-work bounds.

`SingleOpeningEarlyReceiptNative` derives the nine-coefficient lower bound
from actual preparation at packing width at least three, independently of
code-symbol width. At the actual first column read, it derives either earlier
field exposure or the matching early-receipt event at the original native
collector budget. The true quote and completion come from the native sampler
receipt and strict linked nonce recovery; no caller receipt-match certificate
or new freshness assumption is supplied. Any successful parse of this actual
column nonce then gives either that early event or recovery of the original
first-field source log.

`SingleOpeningFirstColumnCoverage.accepted_first_column_cover` combines this
split with actual native false-claim coverage. It leaves shared checkpoint
disagreement explicit. Otherwise, an actual accepted false claim lies in the
early-receipt event or has the recovered source log and the profile-restricted
column event / concrete field-proximity obstruction. This removes the need
for a supplied first-field packet in the first-column classification. Global
machine-prefix classification, inherited exposures and placement of the
remaining proximity obstruction at the appropriate earlier field boundary
remain to be composed into the accepted-false-claim lifetime theorem.

`SingleOpeningCausalCoverage.accepted_coverage` derives the original first

`SingleOpeningEventContext` proves that field and profile-column event

future verifier's root, opening, parent transcript, tables, collector budget
or scheduler. Equal parameters transport the concrete raw/claimed families;
primitive-root proofs are irrelevant. Lifetime witnesses still require the
same original public parameters and profile; this does not merge different

`SingleOpeningLifetimeSoundness.Witness` retains the original candidate

over every accepted false single opening at every finite prefix of the same
unbounded machine lifetime.

`failure_covered` and `lifetime_bound` combine global causal coverage and the

charges. There is no retry, root, lane, owner or number-of-calls multiplier.
The explicit numerical conditions remain packing width at least three,
radius below Goldilocks cardinality, and three times radius below the retained
code minimum distance. `failure_rebase` and `prelude_bound` retain every
recorded causal prelude observation inside that same charged machine; earlier
partial field/column reads are not discarded or treated as fresh.

`SingleOpeningLifetimeMeasurable` proves accepted-call and failure-witness
replay on worlds agreeing with the complete history, even for arbitrary

reconstructs an actual native sampler receipt and pins its completed state and
pending field input. The reconstructed nonce has the same exact field binding,
which preserves the original common-source false-claim predicate. No
world-independence premise is imposed on the native receipt. The finite and
unbounded failure events are measurable through the recorded-history view.
Thus the lifetime inequality bounds a measurable ideal-oracle failure event,
not only an outer-measure envelope.

## Native outer scalar first-exposure challenge and one-round healing bound

`GoldScalarChallengeLaw` maps the actual shared-budget native collector's three

eligibility, even at an offset beyond the initial candidate cursor; it is not

prefixes on the original first-read posterior fiber.

### Source-derived scalar polynomials and deterministic native healing

`ScalarSourcePolynomial` constructs honest scalar round polynomials from a
sum of products of original factor tables. It folds each factor at the common
point prefix before multiplying. Repeated factor indices are allowed: the
honest degree bound is the expression arity, not a multilinearity claim for
the product. The module proves the native zero/one recurrence, challenge
update, degree bound and full-point terminal identity with the product of
original factor multilinear evaluations. No supplied honest-polynomial
certificate or independent evaluation witness is required.

`ScalarPublicSourceModel` flattens the existing executable public packed source
cube into this factor-table representation, including every padding lane.
Its terminal value is the existing original packed source truth, and its
query is the original base-field source query encoded in the cubic extension.
The public-to-analysis equality retains the actual cache-backed code
constructor and decoding-radius premise. Append stability retains the explicit
original source-key checkpoint premise. Packing width remains independent of
code width. The model takes no opening response or claimed source values.

`ScalarChainHealing` proves that a fixed false original equation either remains
false or has a false-to-true transition among the actual native completed
records. This uses the existing native chain and its original getters rather
than a supplied trace, and introduces no union over batch equations.
`ScalarNativeSourceHealing` derives native equation semantics from actual
ordered completed-record getters. A healing transition produces distinct
received and source-derived honest polynomials, derives both degree bounds,
and proves agreement at the literal retained native challenge. The finished
native verifier has an actual healing transition whenever an originally false
claim has become truthful at the returned common point. Missing getters are
explicit; the truthful terminal getter premise excludes missing-slot vacuity.

Regression tests cover repeated-factor quadratic behavior against the incorrect
pointwise-product interpolation shortcut, a nonzero fourth packing lane,
packed terminal evaluation, a consistent two-variable source table and actual
native zero-message rounds. The source sum is one while the original native
claim is zero; the first completed zero draw heals it. Tests derive root
agreement from native round meaning and original getters, and derive the
completed healing witness from actual native verifier completion. Thirty exact
axiom guards cover the new public definitions and theorems and contain only
standard Lean axioms.

The generic honest-polynomial and deterministic scalar no-healing gaps are now
closed at this table-model boundary. The modified PBS caller's exact arithmetic
expressions, factor allocations and original roots must still be associated
with this model. Source ownership must be established at or before scalar
first exposure; append stability alone does not establish this. The actual
producing sampler's prior common point must also be associated with the
chosen chain prefix before composing these healing roots with the causal
all-budget challenge law. Global adaptive exposure summation, lookup/PBS

attacker-work/compiler/cache/RNG refinement remain open. The final modified-PBS
128-bit actual-attacker-work theorem is not proved. Frozen `Native*` files and
kernel resource limits are unchanged.

### Pending-read source stability and original allocated scalar factors

`SourceFrontierStability` identifies the executable public-history selector
with the native causal selector for every history, including the fallback of
an unrecorded key. A resolved pending positive read freezes exactly the log
already selected from the earlier history, at every one of the 64 supported
heights. Every arbitrary positive answer, offset and later continuation keeps
that same selected log. The public cube and its flattened scalar factor are
therefore unchanged from the pre-read history. This strengthens plain append
stability: an existing checkpoint is no longer required when the pending input
resolves the original full context/root key. Zero-byte observations do not
supply this guarantee. Pure table stability needs neither a decoding-radius
premise nor a code-constructor assumption; the separate interpretation and
source-truth theorems retain their original hypotheses.

Chronological native lineage supplies resolution from the old observed byte
cache. The position-indexed theorem connects a completed history to its actual
pre-read prefix. The ancestry theorem covers both source facts and helper
context facts with their committed roots. It derives the pre-read table or
returns the existing `SeedQuoteOrder.Bad` event; chronological ancestry is not
silently assumed, and this exception is not absorbed into the shared hash bad
event or treated as free. The existing seed-order analysis still has to be
included in the final adaptive global composition.

`AllocatedScalarSource` builds each source factor from the original registry
slot of the actually assembled lookup context. The slot's original store
reference, chosen allocation, full parameters, root, constructor request and
constructor configuration are derived from assembly. The scalar query evaluates
that same original factor. Actual native registry initialization supplies its
complete context/root key and the observed hash of the original full parameter
serialization, including unused and aliased slots. The key is tied directly to
the selected allocated object and reference root, without separate parameter,
code or digest-association certificates from a caller.

`AllocatedScalarHelper` selects the same assembled store's actual borrowed
helper object and the original proof-root ordinal. Its original parameters and
constructor provenance are retained, and its source factor has no future
opening response argument. Source and helper factors both inherit first-read
stability, including a first freeze at the current read. Their ancestry
adapters retain the explicit existing seed-order exception. Every packing
lane, including unused padding, is retained; packing width remains independent
of the original code block width. These are logical allocation associations,
not Rust pointer or heap refinements.

Regressions cover a genuinely new source key, arbitrary positive response
bytes/offsets and later hashes, identical pre-read owners across different
answers, all supported heights, and zero-byte non-freezing/fallback changes.
They exercise a four-lane scalar factor, position-indexed mixed-history
prefixes, actual source and helper ancestry through a descendant read, original
allocation/root/constructor retention, actual registry key computation, and
source/helper factor stability. Twenty-five exact axiom guards cover the new
public API and contain only standard Lean axioms.

original source lanes. The frontier proof now factors through the common

test selects degree three; the other branch selects degree four. Their

### Consumed-byte replay and actual lookup producer traces

`FieldConsumedReplay` proves that native field collection retains uniform

accepted coefficients obtained by filtering every candidate, including rejected
ones. Initialization, single-candidate advancement, bounded execution and
receipt completion preserve this invariant. Positive-width chunks are uniquely
determined by their concatenation. Consequently two traced states with equal
consumed bytes, or equal raw `NativeFieldReceipt.input` keys, have equal accepted
coefficient lists, even across different worlds, inputs and execution budgets.
The theorem has no minimum coefficient count or receipt-length bound; it applies
to short three-coefficient lookup draws as well as larger PCS draws.

reciprocal-rejection and equality reader machines, across arbitrary budgets and

lookup requests and completed selections. `LookupProducerConsumed.producer`
uses the original executed job's producer membership to obtain this invariant
without a caller-supplied collector trace certificate.

observations, explicitly charging fresh-digest/collision risks, and composing

### Earlier receipt keys cover original lookup factors

`ReceiptPayloadView` retains the complete raw consumed-byte payload named by
each positive receipt-key read at any offset, or by a hash observation. Starts
and empty reads add no payload. Coordinate knowledge and actual `seen = true`
each imply payload membership, without a supplied synthetic receipt read.
Payloads form a finite set with cardinality at most the raw history length.

`ReceiptCoefficientCandidates` deterministically parses fixed positive-width
chunks from each payload and filters canonical candidates, including rejected
ones. It proves exact recovery for every `FieldConsumedReplay.Traced` state,
with fuel derived from the payload length rather than a retry bound. Observed
receipt keys therefore cover the actual retained coefficient list in a finite
history-determined set. This set has cardinality at most history length and is
fixed on equal-history fibers. Distinct raw payloads may decode to the same
accepted coefficients; these candidates are deduplicated.

`LookupReceiptCandidates` maps that coefficient cover to typed scalar values
and equality points, retaining the same cardinality bound. Its original-job
producer adapter derives the collector trace and value correspondence from
actual batch execution and the original producer membership. Its original
equality adapter recovers the actual equality request from the successful
prelude contract. Every retained draw is either in the earlier-key candidate
set or has an explicitly unseen receipt key. No caller-supplied coefficient
trace, artificial output, successful sampling certificate, or positive-width
premise is needed at these Goldilocks original-job boundaries.

This is a finite candidate cover, not single-value counterfactual fixation.
It does not turn equal receipt digests into equal keys, charge unseen receipt
risks, or identify history length with physical attacker work. In particular,
the cardinality lemma alone does not justify an extra history-size multiplier
in the final work bound. The remaining composition must select or cover the
actual lookup/EQ factors on each causal fiber, preserve original metadata and
table families, discharge receipt/collision and seed-order alternatives, then
apply the conditional degree law and PCS bounds with global adaptive accounting.
The final modified-PBS 128-bit actual-attacker-work theorem remains open.

`ReceiptCandidateCompletion` is an analysis-only replayable extension of the

`LookupDigestFixation` transports coefficient fixation to typed lookup scalar

premises; binding each original draw's receipt message to the selected scalar

membership and the unseen-receipt alternative are supplied separately by the
original-job adapters from the preceding milestone.

The new collision is a SHAKE receipt-block collision, not the existing SHA-512
registry/cache bad event. No probability bound or free absorption into another

then conditional degree/PCS composition and global adaptive work accounting.

### Adaptive SHAKE receipt collisions at first naming

`ReceiptCollisionRisk` supplies the previously separate SHAKE receipt-collision
probability obligation. It selects a receipt payload when its key is first
named by a positive SHAKE read at any offset or by a SHA-512 hash query.
Starts and empty reads do not name keys; later naming of the same raw payload
is ineligible. The selected payload is absent from the earlier payload set,
which implies that all of its SHAKE coordinates are unseen.

The event compares the selected key's full 512-bit SHAKE digest against the
full digests of earlier named keys. Those earlier keys may have only partial
reads or hash observations, so their full digests need not be known in the
original prefix. `retained_bound` completes only those earlier keys using
`ReceiptCandidateCompletion`, retaining the entire original selecting packet.
The new key is distinct from every completion query and remains wholly
unseen. On the refined fiber the earlier digests are fixed, giving a target
bound of `earlierNamedPayloads.card / 2^512`. Averaging the refined posteriors
proves `averaged_bound` on the original world law. No fresh-full-read claim is
made for a key already partially observed.

`ReceiptCollisionOnset` proves monotonicity of named payloads and their
collisions and identifies the first actual observation that introduces a
collision. `ReceiptProgramObservation` ties that observation's candidate to
the next causal request at the exact raw-log position, and identifies each
prefix log with the corresponding take of the full raw log.
`ProgramReceiptCollision.covers` therefore covers every collision among
receipt keys named in the complete enclosing program log; `prefix_covers`
also covers all earlier posterior-prefix collisions returned by receipt
candidate/fixation arguments. `collision_le` bounds the event by the expected
sum of first-naming charges over the program lifetime. It adds no per-round,
per-job, per-factor or collector-retry multiplier.

`combined_le` retains one inherited root/hash event and adds the fresh-receipt
guessing and SHAKE receipt-collision lifetime integrals separately. It uses
no independence assumption between these bad events and does not absorb the
new SHAKE collision risk into the SHA-512 registry hash event.

with the posterior coefficient/factor and degree/PCS reductions. Cross-world
original metadata/source-family coupling and actual attacker-work accounting
remain open. Receipt collision probability now has a native-history coverage
and lifetime-risk bound, but its charge still requires physical-cost coupling.
The final modified-PBS 128-bit actual-attacker-work theorem is not proved.
Frozen `Native*` modules, dependencies and kernel resource limits are unchanged.

### Parent-seed refinement for cross-world ancestry

The native parent ledger deliberately retains every compatible parent under
a partial seed cache. Raw prefix equality alone therefore does not fix full
parent seeds or justify identifying one original parent across worlds.
`ParentSeedCandidates` collects all recognized parent-seed inputs from the
actual prefix, including starts, empty reads, hashes and arbitrary partial
reads, matching native discovery semantics. Candidate membership proves that
the strict parent parser succeeds; it does not authenticate the metadata.

`ParentSeedCompletion` adds analysis-only full seed reads for those keys and
retains the entire old packet. Its replay theorem fixes every candidate's
full 64-byte seed on the refined fiber, and `matching_on_fiber` fixes the
whole set of exact seed matches. Several matches may remain; no parent is
selected by a claimed uniqueness of a partial cache.
`ParentMetadataReplay` transports chronological semantic source and helper
ancestry through that fiber. The transferred facts still refer to the
original raw prefix, not to a replacement history containing auxiliary reads.
These facts identify context digests and source roots, not authenticated full
parameter records.

`ScalarParentSeparation` proves that the original typed scalar request is
rejected by the parent-seed parser: its final field frame has kind 4, whereas
a recognized parent seed request ends in kind 2. It derives this from the
actual recovered scalar reader. Completing all recognized parents therefore
leaves the entire outer scalar SHAKE key unseen, without an independent key
separation or framing certificate.

`ParentFactorFiber` combines parent-seed completion with receipt completion.
It projects the joint packet back to both the parent packet and the original
receipt-only completion packet, using the fixed full receipt blocks rather
than replacing the original observation history. Semantic ancestry replay,
scalar-word and equality-point fixation, posterior mismatch bounds, and the
exact uniform law of any finite scalar SHAKE block all hold on this one
refined fiber. Reference-world bad-event exclusions and actual input/receipt
position matching remain explicit. Auxiliary reads are not native attacker
operations and are not fed into the original root-freezing table definition.

Next, use this stable parent/ancestry data to recover the actual canonical
binding, original slot addresses and full parameter hash preimages across
worlds. Residual multiple-parent matching and late parameter identification
must be accounted for explicitly; this change does not assume them away or
prove complete source-family equality. Good reference-family construction,
degree/PCS posterior composition and actual attacker-work accounting remain
open. The final modified-PBS 128-bit actual-attacker-work theorem is not
proved. Frozen `Native*` modules, dependencies and kernel resource limits are
unchanged.

### Bounded parent-seed collisions and raw-parent coupling

`ParentSeedCollisionRisk` charges a recognized parent input at its first
naming by any actual request, including starts and empty reads. Eligibility
requires that the key is absent from the earlier parent candidate set. This
implies whole-key SHAKE nonexposure; a later partial or full read of the same
key is not charged again. The event compares the new key's complete 64-byte
seed against the complete seeds of earlier recognized parent keys.

The earlier keys may have only partial observations. `retained_bound`
completes only those earlier parent seeds, retains the original selecting
packet, and keeps the distinct newly named key wholly unseen. It bounds the
conditional event by `earlierParentKeys.card / 2^512`. `averaged_bound`
transfers that bound to the original world law. No full-block fresh law is
claimed after a key has already been partially read.

`ParentSeedCollisionOnset` identifies the first naming observation that
introduces a collision, and `ParentSeedObservation` ties it to the actual
next request at that raw-log position. `ProgramParentSeedCollision` covers
both full-program and earlier-prefix parent-seed collisions by one lifetime
sum of first-naming charges. `combined_le` adds this charge once to the
existing inherited and receipt-event bounds. The parent-seed event remains
separate from SHAKE receipt collisions, fresh receipt guesses and the shared
SHA-512 root/hash event; no independence or per-job union factor is used.

`ParentMatchFixation.on_fiber` compares parent candidates in two worlds on
the joint parent/receipt fiber. If both match the same quoted child seed,
the raw parent inputs are equal or the reference world's parent-seed
collision ledger holds. The proof transports the counterfactual parent's
full seed to the reference world and retains the collision branch rather
than assuming a partial cache has one compatible parent.
`known_on_fiber` derives candidate membership from semantic helper ancestry.

`AllocatedParentPrefix.known` recovers that ancestry in the actual scalar
first-read prefix from executed allocated verification and native framing.
It uses the existing seed-order exception to establish chronology, recovers

actual first-read witness. No parent index, prefix membership or independent
chronological certificate is supplied. The seed-order bad event is still an

### Exact original helper-root vectors at scalar readers

`HelperRootsView` strictly recovers the most recent helper-roots frame from
complete framed bytes using the exact digest-vector codec. It retains the
entire original order and repetitions. A malformed latest roots frame is
rejected without fallback, and a same-label frame of a different kind cannot
replace the binder. Parser soundness identifies the actual roots frame and
proves there is no later roots binder. Earlier caller-controlled decoys are
permitted and cannot replace the actual native binder.

`RootSafeExtension` strengthens valid native transcript extension with the
fact that no helper-roots frame is appended. The proof covers typed scalar
and vector requests, candidate retries, suspension/resumption and receipt
finalization. `RootSafeEquality` derives this property after the actual roots
binder through equality-point sampling and successful prelude execution.
`RootSafeScalar` derives it through scalar statement and round binding,
checked guards, interpolation/decode failures, rejected candidates and every
completed reader. All work is in new modules; frozen native sources are
unchanged.

`OriginalHelperRoots.completed_roots` obtains the complete original proof-root
vector from the literal pending input of every completed native scalar round.
Its caller framing comes from the actual native fork header. The theorem
requires only the existing native roots/statement/round allocation domains,
not an independently supplied roots-frame position or root-membership/order
certificate. Equal literal scalar inputs therefore fix the full vector and
every corresponding original ordinal without an oracle exception or equality
search over roots.

`AllocatedScalarFamily.at_scalar_first` constructs the parent-family package,
complete original helper-root vector and quoted scalar input directly from
actual allocated execution at the selected first read. `OriginalScalarFamily`
compares these data on the existing joint fiber and retains exactly the prior
parent-seed, root/hash and late-context exceptions. Its helper-table theorem
now identifies complete packed tables at matching original root ordinals,
replacing the earlier independent common-root premise. Helper row dimension
and all helper packing lanes remain intact.

The original helper-root ordinal gap is closed under the existing native
allocation domains. Assembly of the selected native job's complete source
and helper functions, including request/job ordinal and dependent dimension
alignment, remains open. Good reference-family selection, degree/PCS
posterior composition, adaptive lifetime false-PBS reduction, profile

`AttainableReferenceBound` proves a pointwise choice-or-bad-coverage split.
A reference is chosen only when a good witness class on the region is

and each lifetime charge once at a fixed analysis prefix. No extra
reference-selection or per-job ledger is created.

all-budget scalar agreement bound on the joint parent/receipt completion

the existing eligibility lemma without executing a query, changing the
observation log or claiming physical work. Fixed table tests pay the literal
native `D / Goldilocks^3` bound, over all auxiliary and collector budgets.
`LookupIdentityTableCongruence` and `CandidateIdentityTables` transport the

### Adaptive scalar lifetime and joint scalar/PCS bound

`GlobalReferenceBad` separates the complete-history root/hash event from the
four existing parent-seed, context-target, fresh-receipt and receipt-collision
lifetime events. Root badness persists from every original prefix into the
completed log. Excluding this single global union supplies every prefix's
good-reference conditions; no global bad mass is repeated per position/job.
The non-root probability is bounded by the existing four lifetime charges.

`OracleFiberOuterBound` proves outer-measure upper bounds using the countable
partition of attainable replay histories. Arbitrary existential events need
not be assumed measurable, and reference choices need not be measurable.
All histories retain their original unnormalized mass. Its score version
averages the same selecting-packet score, including infinite scores, without
conditioning on a successful world or imposing a positive class-mass floor.

`SafeIdentityKernel` chooses a reference only from an attained globally safe
class. Safe competitors then have the same original families, factors,
packet/message, metadata, profile and recovered replay on the joint fiber.
The class pays only `4 / Goldilocks^3`, with no posterior bad remainder.
Empty attained classes have zero conditional mass.

`ScalarPositionKernel` removes the union over arbitrary literal inputs:
the actual original first-read command determines the input on every joint
fiber. Recovery of that key supplies the literal statement, and the original
odd identity slot proves that every attained job ordinal is below its
encoded equation count. A finite union over those ordinals gives a
prefix-selected charge of `equationCount * 4 / Goldilocks^3`. Missing first
reads and unrecoverable keys pay zero. Earlier positive reads of the same
key prevent another charge, even at a different byte offset. Completed
prefixes and every later extension pay zero. The score depends only on the
actual original prefix packet; auxiliary completion queries create no work
or score entries.

`ScalarLifetimeComposition` sums these charges over all analysis positions
and bounds the union of all globally safe attained identity-healing events
by the expected sum. No fixed input list, job-count cap, retry cap, uniform
completion depth or attacker lifetime cutoff is supplied. The full global
bad event is retained once outside that union.

`JointIdentityLifetimeBound` combines the adaptive scalar event with the
original helper/source PCS-family lifetime event. The scalar branch's
full-history root/hash bad event enters the PCS family's same source-bad
ledger; it is not charged twice. The joint probability bound is one hash
supremum, helper/source exposure charges, the four global non-root lifetime
charges, and the expected scalar equation-count charge.
`AllocatedJointIdentityBound` instantiates this with the actual borrowed
helper and original registry constructor provenance and packing geometry.
The prior allocated native identity coverage supplies these alternatives
under its existing execution/framing/seed-order and admission premises.

Five regressions cover an empty read, malformed far-offset scalar input,
encoded native statement count, later reads of different bytes on the same
valid key, and arbitrary extensions after completion.

The remaining goal includes whole modified-PBS initial falsity (and any

## Scalar metadata and specified interpreter work (2026-11-11)

`ScalarMetadataSize` proves that each equation in a successfully recovered
native scalar key contributes at least two statement metadata bytes. The
proof follows the actual bincode usize varint codec and transcript frames;
it does not assume eight-byte integers. The equation count is consequently
bounded by the selected literal input's byte length.

`ScalarEquationWork` decomposes the existing observation-clock scalar charge
exactly into the first-read equation count times `4 / Goldilocks^3`, both
pointwise and in expectation. It bounds those equation counts by selected
key bytes without finite lifetime or finite expectation assumptions.

`ClosedByteScalarWork` prices the same generic first-read count at actual
issued closed-byte instructions. Every selected key's length is bounded by
that instruction's specified price. Summing over all instruction indices
bounds the instruction-clock scalar charge by the existing lifetime work
counter times the scalar rate.

`PrivateCoinScalarWork` transports this instruction bound through runtime
private-coin instructions and the original fixed-tape execution sections.
The joint expected charge is bounded by the existing expected work counter
for an arbitrary private-tape measure, without conditioning on success,
preloading a fuel-dependent coin tape, truncating the execution, or assuming
finite expected work.

These are specified interpreter work bounds. In particular, this change does
not yet identify the enclosing pure `Program` observation-clock scalar sum
with the instruction-clock sum: silent byte instructions require an exact
trace/clock refinement, retaining first-read uniqueness. Nor does it price
native Rust primitives, caches, or physical RNG work. Those obligations
remain necessary before substituting actual attacker work into the joint
security bound. Whole modified-PBS initial falsity, native domain/seed-order
closure, numeric/profile admission, and the other charge-accounting
obligations listed above remain open. The final 128-bit theorem is unproved.

## Observation-clock scalar charge paid by specified work (2026-11-11)

`ScalarLogWork` supplies the missing accounting inequality for the original
pure `Program` charge. A positive-read log entry contributes its literal

prefixes and then taking the unbounded sum bounds `totalBytes`, and hence
the original `ScalarLifetimeComposition.totalCharge`, by the full original

proved against the same complete program run. No synthetic completion
queries or local instruction indices enter that observation-clock sum.

`ByteScalarLogWork` bounds this log potential by the existing input-work
potential, whose closed and runtime-private-coin interpreter accounting was

observation-clock scalar charge is bounded by its actual final specified

there is no assumption that instruction and observation positions coincide.
Repeated positive reads may be overcounted in the intermediate potential,
but each is paid by its original issued instruction. The first-read
security charge still selects the key only once.

The supremum of original observation-clock charges over all private-coin
instruction horizons is bounded pointwise by the existing specified
lifetime work. Its joint integral over arbitrary private tapes and worlds
is bounded by expected specified lifetime work times the scalar rate.
The existing safe-scalar probability theorem is also instantiated for
every closed and fixed-private-tape instruction horizon with expected
specified lifetime work on its right-hand side.

indexed original column event, rather than the whole original source failure.
This composition conservatively adds another `1 / 2^159` reference charge;
it does not claim a newly optimized joint reference accounting.

lifetime remain required before eliminating that residual probability.

## Adaptive columns, shared receipts, and the complete analysis work bound

`BatchColumnContextName` recovers the complete column input frames and the
exact linked field frames. The field-prefix batch binding names its literal
context/root in the direct ledger, without assuming receipt correctness.
`BatchColumnParameterCandidate` retains original code origin and calibrated
role, actual first positive column read and observed full context computation.
On an equal pre-read replay packet, safe candidates have equal full parameters
and calibrated radius. The existing shared root/late-context events are the
only exceptions; digest-to-parameter injectivity is not assumed.

`AdaptiveBatchColumnKernel` compares every competing safe source family on
a replay fiber to an attained candidate and pays one native column loss.
The source recovered at the first field read stays fixed by the original past.
Native domain, quota and matrix-count eligibility remain in the column event.
Actual observation positions bound its charge by specified interpreter work.
Continuation preserves attained candidates and the same event. The joint
`AdaptiveBatchColumnLifetime.safe_bound` costs at most `17 / 2^141` times
expected specified lifetime work across all instruction horizons, with no
source-family count or event-measurability premise.

`AcceptedBatchColumnCandidate` derives candidates from accepted native calls.
`AcceptedBatchJointCoverage` and `OriginalSourceJointCoverage` retain this link
through native false-claim analysis and original indexed source witnesses on
their exact instruction logs. Outside shared hash failure, every original
source failure now enters a common-profile early-receipt event or an attained
adaptive field/column candidate. Full parameter/profile equality, retained
constructor provenance and original role admission remain explicit.

`ProgramEarlyReceiptWork` prices the common early-receipt event at raw program
positions. It masks by log length below a proof-only threshold, then uses
Markov's inequality for larger expected-work executions. No runtime cap,
consumed-length decoding or success-floor normalization is introduced.
`ProgramEarlyReceiptContinuation` proves that the event depends only on its
selected view and persists through program continuation. The original private
coin prefix factorization lifts the bound to the joint tape/world lifetime:
`PrivateCoinEarlyReceiptProbability.lifetime_le_255` charges `1 / 2^255` times
expected specified work for all raw positions, instruction horizons and native
collector budgets together.

`IndexedSourceJointProbability` removes the complete indexed source-failure
probability from the ledger. Its index type is arbitrary, including unbounded
or repeated original families; there is no cardinality fee. The source rate
is conservatively `34 / 2^141 + 1 / 2^255` outside shared lifetime reference
failures. The shared-hash-only version adds the existing `1 / 2^159` reference
allowance, as in the preceding reduction.

`CalibratedJointWorkBound.bound` composes original helper/source PCS failures,
scalar analysis failures and one shared hash ledger with no residual probability
term. Its exact aggregate rate is bounded by `1 / 2^128` using finite rational
arithmetic and checked coercions. `work_128` proves
`2^128 * P[scalar/helper/original-source analysis failure] ≤ E[specified interpreter work]`
under the stated original constructor and calibrated-profile premises, even
when expected work is infinite. The reference allowance is conservatively
charged twice; the shared hash event is still charged once.

This is an analysis-event/interpreter-work theorem. It does not establish that
public modified-PBS false acceptance implies that event, close native domain
and seed-order obligations, derive admission for the actual application
profiles, separate honest/verifier work from attacker work, or refine specified
interpreter charges to physical attacker work. Those application and pricing
obligations remain before the requested final actual-attacker-work theorem.
The goal remains active and that final theorem remains unproved.

## Independent retained-parameter radii in native identity coverage

Inspection of the application-to-analysis link found an important interface
mismatch: the existing allocated identity alternatives interpret all source
and helper tables with one common radius, whereas the calibrated joint bound
uses each original role's radius. The actual Goldilocks source and helper
role radii differ. Equating them would impose an unjustified application
premise, so the new coverage uses independently derived radii instead.

`ParameterDecodingRadius.ofParameters` computes the decoding radius solely
from the retained row-code height and message-block dimension. Source and
helper calibration each prove equality with their corresponding admitted
role radius. The original constructor and calibration derive the required
`3 * radius < distance` facts. Context/root hashes, claims, query values,
scheduler state and future responses do not select the radius.

`CanonicalAllocatedTables` decodes each original source slot using that slot's
parameter radius, and the helper using its own parameter radius. Original
allocation records, roots, packing padding and row/column casts are retained.
Aliases of one original slot share the same complete table and radius.
`CanonicalAllocatedFamilyFixation` proves that these actual canonical source
and helper families agree on the existing original replay fiber, outside the
same reference bad alternatives. Radius agreement is derived from full
parameter equality, separately for each original object. This prepares the
canonical tables for the remaining scalar-candidate recovery step.

`CanonicalAllocatedOpeningCoverage` recovers the original accepted source
receipt and pair for a wrong canonical source fold. Only that source's own
radius condition is needed; a wrong source does not require a common radius
valid for unrelated registry entries. It yields the original indexed batch
lifetime failure at the exact calibrated source radius.
`CanonicalAllocatedHelperCoverage` applies the analogous independent radius
to the actual original helper receipt, deriving its original single-opening
lifetime failure at the calibrated helper radius.

`CanonicalAllocatedJob` retains a native completed job, its original allocated
context, source-slot map, geometry, framing and enclosing-program observation
subtrace. Its wrong-fold event is defined using the actual canonical public
families. `wrong_covered` derives the existing original PCS family lifetime
or shared full-history hash alternative. `CanonicalAllocatedJobWork.work_128`
therefore proves the 128-bit specified-work bound for any original native
wrong-fold job across all runtime private-coin instruction horizons, using
the actual allocated helper/source constructors and common parent profile.
The scalar event used in this bound is only an over-approximation from the
existing joint theorem; wrong-fold coverage itself enters the PCS branch.

`CanonicalAllocatedIdentity.false_identity` also derives native scalar healing
or those calibrated PCS failures from an originally false identity claim
interpreted against the canonical public tables. It retains the original
full/partial branch, completed scalar reader and native messages. Canonical
healing has not yet been recovered into the priced attained scalar event;
no whole false-identity probability bound is claimed here.

Whole modified-PBS initial falsity and application-stage enforcement, native
round-domain/seed-order closure, actual profile admission, actor-cost
separation and physical work pricing remain open. The final public modified-PBS
actual-attacker-work theorem is still unproved and the goal remains active.

`CanonicalCandidateFixation` combines the original retained metadata/factor

`CanonicalIdentityWork.work_128` proves

## Seed-order safety is now a priced exception

`SeedOrderRiskBudget` prices the existing `SeedQuoteOrder.Bad` ledger directly
on original raw program positions. The event is the union of a seed quoted by
an earlier observation and a self-quote in the pending complete input. Prior
target count is bounded by original log length; the pending quote contributes
one additional full 512-bit target. Neither the absence of a prior quote nor
a self-dependency removes that pending-input charge.

Below an analysis threshold, the combined score is at most
`threshold / 2^512`, since `log.length < threshold` pays for the extra pending
target. Scores vanish without an actual pending request. Summing across raw
positions is bounded by specified interpreter work. A Markov split covers
larger-work executions; the threshold does not constrain execution, query
count, native retries or dependency-graph size.

`SeedOrderContinuation` retains an original ordering exception through any
program continuation. `PrivateCoinSeedOrderProbability` uses original finite
coin-prefix selection to lift the bound to the joint tape/world measure and
all instruction horizons. `lifetime_le_159` proves that the entire seed-order
bad lifetime costs at most `1 / 2^159` times expected specified interpreter
work. There is no tape-support or graph-cardinality fee, no finite expected
work premise and no caller-supplied measurability assumption on the event.

`SeedOrderIdentityWork.Witness` retains the same actual native job, canonical
public-table initial falsity, framing, domains and original allocation as
`CanonicalIdentityWork.Witness`, but has no seed-order safety field.
`covered` derives either an actual seed-order bad event or the previous safe
witness, preserving its complete native data. `ordered_bound` retains the
exact numerical margin of the previous canonical joint ledger.

`SeedOrderIdentityWork.bound` and `work_128` add that seed-order lifetime charge
and prove the originally false canonical native identity work bound without
a seed-order premise. Checked finite rational arithmetic proves that the
old aggregate rate plus `1 / 2^159` still fits `1 / 2^128`. The ordering bad
event is paid once for the entire execution, rather than once per source,
helper, quoted edge, job or enclosing-program horizon.

This removes the explicit seed-order safety assumption from this native
false-identity endpoint. Native framing, round/parent domains, actual profile
admission and the fixed assembled-reference scope remain explicit. Whole
modified-PBS initial falsity/application enforcement, actor-cost separation
and physical attacker-work refinement remain open. The requested final
public modified-PBS actual-attacker-work theorem remains unproved.

## Scalar round framing from bounded canonical proof bytes

`ScalarProofFraming` defines the nested scalar proof's canonical analysis
codec using the existing native message and vector codecs. It proves varint
encoded-length monotonicity, ordered collection's count and payload bounds,
and that every successfully extracted round packet from a nonempty proof
has encoded length at most that of the complete proof. The first
certificate's round-count header pays for the packet's round-index header;
the outer proof count and packet message count agree. No degree, equation
count cutoff or independent nested-vector-size assumption is substituted
for the full encoded-length condition.

`nonempty_of_finished` derives the necessary nonempty condition from actual
native scalar completion: rejected preflight remains terminal, and accepted
preflight checks a nonempty statement with matching certificate count.
`roundDomain_of_bytes` therefore supplies the original native `RoundDomain`
from an exact canonical proof-byte source whose length fits the 64-bit target.
`bounded_source_iff` makes the remaining obligation precise: such a source
exists exactly when the canonical full proof encoding fits. This analysis
reader is not claimed to implement Rust/serde decoding or allocation errors.

`FramedIdentityWork.Witness` carries those bounded canonical proof bytes
instead of a separately supplied round domain. Its conversion retains the
same native job, allocation, canonical public-table falsity and all other
original witness data. `work_128` inherits the seed-order-inclusive bound
without an additional probability or per-equation charge.

Seven regressions cover all varint width transitions, successful ordered

counterexample to unconditional size dominance, deriving the domain from a
bounded source and rejecting a trailing byte. Existing Native modules are
unchanged. Remaining gates include Rust proof decoding/serialization
refinement, statement/parent and other framing obligations, whole modified-PBS
initial falsity/application enforcement, actual profile admission and the

## Full shared-proof serialization supplies component framing domains

`SharedProofByteCodec` adds a compositional canonical analysis codec for the
complete Goldilocks shared proof. It retains the Rust record's seven-field
order: grouped multiplicities, helper roots, scalar algebra, original source
values, helper values, grouped source openings and independent helper
openings. Reconstructing the typed packet checks its flattened multiplicity
count; no flat vector is independently supplied. Prefix roundtrip, exact
roundtrip, injectivity and the equivalence between a bounded canonical source
and a bound on the complete encoding are proved.

This is an analysis codec assembled from the existing field codecs, not a
Rust/serde deserializer equivalence or allocation-error refinement. In
particular, the exact byte view rejects a wider noncanonical count spelling;
coverage of native inputs accepted with such spellings still needs a
nonexpansion/refinement argument. The full canonical encoding bound is not
inferred merely from individual vector or component bounds.

`SharedProofSerializationDomain` proves that flattening's payload words fit
inside the grouped row payload, while its new count header costs at most
nine bytes. A full proof containing a root has enough additional serialized
bytes to cover that header even across varint width changes. Root
nonemptiness is derived from the retained native job's actual prelude root
count and job index. No equation-count cutoff or hash assumption is used.

One bounded full proof source therefore supplies root, scalar algebra,
grouped multiplicity, flattened multiplicity and terminal-value frame bounds,
as well as every source/helper opening response bound, preserving the
original vectors and their membership. These bounds include the original
raw lazy u64 representations rather than normalizing field words.

`SerializedIdentityWork.Witness` carries the bounded full canonical proof
source. Its conversion derives the previous endpoint's root and multiplicity
bounds and constructs the scalar byte source from that same proof. It
retains the original native job, allocation, initial falsity, public-table
truth and remaining framing/profile domains. `work_128` inherits the prior
seed-order-inclusive rate with no additional probability charge. This is a
conditional byte-source endpoint; it does not assert equivalence with all
arbitrary typed witnesses or establish native deserializer correspondence.

## Structural proof reads cannot enlarge canonical encodings

`PrefixCodecReadSize.Nonexpanding` records that a successful prefix read has
canonical encoded length plus remaining-input length at most the original
input length. This is proved for the actual usize reader, using the decoded
wide integer's value bound and the original consumed width. Wider spellings
may shrink on reencoding; invalid tags and truncation remain failures.
The property is then proved compositionally for products, transported
records, repeated elements, vectors, degree-prefixed fixed sequences and
raw fixed byte arrays. It is not inferred from codec roundtrip alone.

`SharedProofReadSize` instantiates those rules for measured row readers,
Goldilocks extensions, scalar messages/proofs, root/path digests, columns,
single and batch openings and all seven shared-proof fields. Its full proof
bound covers every successful structural read, not only canonical input:
`encodedProof.length + rest.length ≤ originalInput.length`.
A bounded source therefore supplies a bounded canonical source for exactly
the same typed proof, including when the original spelling is wider or the
reader leaves a suffix. The canonical-source nonexpansion gate left by the
previous milestone is closed for this specified reader.

`readAll` optionally requires an empty suffix without requiring canonical
spelling. Its success is equivalent to a successful full structural read.
`DecodedIdentityWork.Witness` instead retains the original bounded prefix
buffer, its actual remainder and successful shared-proof read. Conversion
to the serialized endpoint derives the canonical source internally.
`ofSerialized` and `failure_iff` prove equivalence of the two failure events;
`work_128` inherits the prior rate without adding a probability charge,
normalizing raw field values or losing any native job/allocation data.

Thirteen regressions cover wider outer/row/extension-degree prefixes,
four- and eight-byte integer forms, a decoded proof with an exact suffix,
full-packet wider reads, strict trailing/truncated input rejection,
canonical shrinkage, suffix accounting, construction of a canonical source,
component-domain recovery and invalid integer tags. The fingerprint helper
uses codec injectivity to identify the entire original proof, rather than
checking only its dimensions. Existing Native modules are unchanged.

These are proofs about the specified structural reader. Correspondence with
Rust/serde's accepted language, exact values, consumed lengths, errors and
resource behavior remains open, as does binding the byte view to the actual
native input source. Other remaining gates include original parent/config
allocation domains, deriving opening-response bounds for original receipts,
whole modified-PBS initial falsity/application enforcement, actual profile
admission and the fixed assembled-reference scope, actor-cost separation
and physical attacker-work refinement. The final public modified-PBS
actual-attacker-work theorem remains unproved.

## Helper receipt framing from original parent and checked metadata

`CheckedPcsMetadataSize` bounds raw row, matrix and query encodings using the
existing usize encoder. Successful native single-opening completion recovers
both `numVariables < 64` from actual parameter validation and the literal
query/value/matrix checks from the original binding prefix. For widths at
most four this proves a 20,530-byte upper bound on the opening metadata,
without restricting root contents, raw field words, response size, number of
helpers or enclosing execution length.

`HelperReceiptFramingRecovery.call_domain` obtains those metadata bounds for
the actual completed helper receipts. Original packet membership and decoded
proof bytes supply response bounds. The original receipt order therefore
derives the entire helper-call framing domain, rather than accepting that
domain as an independent certificate. The trace invariant retains both the

## Scalar statement framing from executed construction and retained allocation

`CheckedScalarStatementSize` bounds the original independent scalar statement

metadata has maximum multiplicand count at most four; its allocated helper's
variable count is below 64. Each original info therefore occupies two bytes.
Each original lookup job contributes two infos and two claims, giving the
bound `18 + 60 * jobs.length` with both outer vector headers included.

`allocated_numVariables` follows the helper handle through the actual
assembled reachable parameter store, the retained initializer's successful

profile admission or independently selected parameter object. The native

provides the exact statement build, and identifies both statement vector
lengths and the original job/root count.

The original proof root payload contains 64 bytes per job. Its actual bounded
encoding, already derived from the retained proof decoder, implies that
`18 + 60 * jobs.length` fits the frame length domain. This arithmetic does
not assert that the conservative statement bound is at most the root packet
length; it uses the existing frame capacity and original root count.
`retained_fits` composes these results for the actual retained caller job,
with no scalar statement byte-size certificate supplied by its caller.

security rate and specified-interpreter expected-work bound; this change
adds no probability charge.

## The original even-slot helper-sum equation has native failure coverage

The preceding 128-bit work endpoints concern initially false **identity**
equations at slots `2 * job + 1`. A native shared lookup also checks its
helper-sum equation at slot `2 * job`. This stage adds that missing native
arithmetic alternative; it does not silently enlarge the already priced
identity failure event.

`LookupViewSumReduction.event_or_wrong` uses an original recovered lookup
view, its actual completed scalar batch, the literal even-slot sum claim
and the actual helper-sum equality guard. The completed batch contract
derives that the sum and identity subclaims share the original returned
point and dimension. If the initial sum equation is false, truthful helper
folding forces a literal completed-input scalar healing event at that even
slot. Otherwise the original helper opening is wrong. No point equality,
healing flag or independently chosen helper row is supplied as an assumption.

`AllocatedSumAlternatives.false_sum_or_wrong` recovers the sum metadata,
claim address and guard match from the original successful prelude/body and
retained original job. The helper cube is the same canonical public table

lifetime failure and needs only the helper calibration, without source
profile admission. `false_sum` embeds the result in the existing shared
opening-family alternatives. `false_pair` combines sum and identity cases:
if either original equation is initially false, its actual healing event,
the one shared source/hash bad event, or an original calibrated PCS failure
must occur. This is logical coverage, not yet a probability bound for the
enlarged paired-equation event.

`SumCausalChallengeBound.conditional_bound` specializes the existing actual
first-read conditional scalar theorem to the degree-one sum metadata. For
fixed helper tables its conditional loss is exactly bounded by
`1 / goldilocksModulus^3`, with the same replay, recovered input and native
first-read conditions as the generic theorem. It covers its union over
native collector budgets and auxiliary replay. It cannot be applied to
world-dependent canonical tables without the corresponding fixation and
attainability argument. The current canonical adaptive candidate/event
machinery still targets odd-slot identity messages; extending it to these
even-slot sum messages and composing their lifetime/work charge remains open.

## Native initial arithmetic reduces to paired work with an equality exception

`LookupInitialArithmetic` derives the literal original even-slot public sum
and odd-slot zero from successful native preparation, with counts addressed
by the original request ordinal. It interprets the canonical helper sum and
both full/partial identity truths as the actual EQ-weighted masked reciprocal
residual. Source flattening and independent helper decoding use the original
job geometry and canonical allocated families. `false_pair_iff` characterizes
the exact original scalar falsity condition by helper-total mismatch or a
nonzero weighted residual. `obstruction` covers a concrete sum/pointwise
reciprocal violation by that original scalar event or `EqualityMiss`, which
requires a nonzero Boolean residual and its vanishing at the actual EQ point.
It does not infer pointwise correctness from a zero weighted sum.

`LookupProducerArithmetic.produced` derives nonzero r, excluded public poles,
the original compressed public table and its inverse-vector semantics directly
from successful raw production. `public_total` retains arbitrary list/zip
semantics; `public_total_vectors` identifies the literal native total with
the finite reciprocal sum for rectangular original public rows/counts.
`job_obstruction` therefore covers reciprocal nonpassing using the actual
native producer, without a supplied nonzero-r or public-total certificate.
Original table shape and request-indexed count association remain explicit
at `LookupInitialPairedWork.ofNonpassing`; they are not arbitrary replacement
tables or an assumption that a scalar claim is initially false.

`LookupInitialPairedWork.Witness` retains the original caller job, sequenced
input observations and original caller-parent framing. Its arithmetic claim
is a false helper total or a nonzero pointwise masked residual. `ofNonpassing`
constructs this witness from reciprocal nonpassing over rectangular original
public rows and their actual counts. `covered`/`failure_covered` reduce its
all-prefix event to the existing paired scalar event or an equality miss on
the same witness. `work_with_equality_exception` proves
`2^128 * P[arithmetic failure] <= specified expected work +
2^128 * P[actual equality exception]`. The new probability term is explicit;
no adaptive equality security charge is silently absorbed into the 128-bit rate.

`fixed_residual_bound` proves dimension/cardinality loss for an independent
uniform EQ point after the entire original residual is fixed. It is not a
bound on the actual adaptive exception above. Conditional fixation of the
canonical decoded families, the native equality draw law and all-prefix
work pricing still need composition before the exception can be discharged.
Tuple compression/reciprocal detection also remain to be priced in the native
joint work ledger before reciprocal nonpassing covers arbitrary false lookups.

Five named regression checks demonstrate a truthful helper total with
nonzero reciprocal errors, cancellation at the midpoint EQ draw, detection

## Native equality-vector law and original residual exposure

`GoldEqualityPointLaw` assembles consecutive blocks of three canonical
Goldilocks coefficients through the original cubic basis. Its assembly is an
equivalence, yielding the joint uniform law on the whole equality vector.
The conditional native law retains the shared candidate-budget completion
mass for `n*3` coefficients. Its all-budget version includes every suspension
and rejection, without a retry cap or conditioning on successful completion.
`eventual_residual_bound` gives `n / goldilocksModulus^3` for a fixed nonzero
Boolean residual at a causally fresh native vector input. Cubic coefficients
form extension elements; they do not supply an independent three-lane power.

`EqualityCollectorTrace` proves that active and completed initialized native

It retains the job's original draw index and the native raw-word point order.
`LookupEqualityResidual.miss` transports the canonical decoded residual from

`of_miss` puts the original equality exception into an all-budget collector

## Original caller equality recovery and arithmetic work without an exception remainder

`EqualityCollectorLogs` retains each original equality collector's initialized
raw read trace as a sublist of the actual equality machine log, across
rejected coefficients, suspension, resumption and later draws. A completed
positive-dimensional vector therefore supplies an actual positive field-stream
read. Receipt queries alone are not treated as field-stream exposure.

`CallerEqualityFamily` reconstructs the allocated execution from the caller's
original allocation and successful native run. Its recovered candidate retains
exactly the caller's allocation, origin, index, job, geometry and complete
canonical source/helper tables. `CallerEqualityExposure` embeds the original
collector trace through the prelude and native verification into the enclosing
program and recovers its earliest stream read, including earlier adversarial
prequeries at arbitrary offsets. No independent first-exposure certificate is
required by the final caller recovery.

`CallerEqualityResidual` transports the complete masked residual between the
original scalar cube and native cube. Original draw evidence identifies the
point in the same coordinate order; seed-order safety supplies complete-table
stability at the original first read. The zero-dimensional case cannot have
a nonzero residual and vanishing weighted sum, so an actual missed residual

## Original lookup scalar collectors and causal pair-challenge bounds

`LookupCollectorTrace` proves that every active and retained original lookup

Its complete raw read log remains a sublist of the actual challenge log across

## Refined lookup freshness, adaptive compression classes and all-horizon class probability

`LookupInputSeparation` derives from actual initialized native lookup and
batch execution that compression and reciprocal field inputs end in kind-4
request frames and are rejected by the parent-seed input parser. Suspension,
coefficient rejection, completed offset rejection and resumption preserve
that distinction. This is not an assumption about a later scalar input or
a final helper-root frame.

`RefinedCompressionKernel` proves that neither parent-seed auxiliary
completion nor named consumed-byte receipt completion exposes the original
lookup stream. Its exact fixed-candidate compression bound therefore holds
on the same `ParentFactorFiber` that fixes the complete source tuple test.
The numerator is the original request complexity
`table.length * (columns-1)`. The refinement uses the retained original first
read and exact raw input; no fresh replacement query is added to actual work.

`CompressionClassKernel` builds attained adaptive classes indexed by original
input, job ordinal and actual request complexity. Outside the one shared
global reference bad event, each class has bound `cost/q^3`. References are
chosen only from attained event worlds on the fiber; empty classes contribute
zero without a success floor or measurable chooser. `cost_unique` proves
that safe candidates at the same input/job on the completed fiber have the
same actual complexity. `cost_alternative` handles events spanning all
complexity indices by that one attained cost or zero mass, so no extra union
loss over possible cost values is introduced. The unindexed `Lifetime` event
retains every candidate through its own actual complexity, without assuming
an external cap or discarding large requests.

`CompressionContinuation` preserves the original source candidate, exact
complexity, first-read position, complete tuple test and kernel through
actual program continuation. Both individual classes and the full lifetime
event are monotone across private byte-interpreter instruction horizons.
It does not assert that a safe event remains safe after arbitrary later work.
`CallerCompressionClassRecovery.covered` recovers original caller compression
misses into attained safe classes or the existing seed-order/global reference
bad alternatives, with those alternatives retained once outside the class.

`PrivateCoinCompressionClassProbability` proves the all-instruction-horizon
safe bound for each original input/job/cost/position class under arbitrary
private-tape measures. It uses countable finite tape prefixes and the proved
class continuation, and excludes the global reference bad event once across
all horizons. The bound is `coins(univ) * cost/q^3`, hence `cost/q^3` for a
probability measure. This is a per-class probability theorem, not an
expected-work bound on the union of every class.

The remaining compression work is a justified finite/dynamic aggregation
over original inputs, positions and jobs with actual lifetime work charging.
The original request-size/shape and producer-hash bridges are also still
needed. Reciprocal numerator/source/y/count fixation and adaptive work
composition remain open. The new class rates have not been inserted into
`LookupInitialWork.work_128` or used to claim full lookup nonmembership
soundness. Whole false-PBS output enforcement, original caller-parent
provenance, Rust execution/codec/read correspondence, supported profile
admission, fixed assembled-reference scope, actor-cost separation and physical
attacker-work refinement remain open. The ultimate security theorem is not
proved.

## Rebuilt request execution, literal public arithmetic and parent payload bounds

`LookupRequestRebuild` rebuilds typed original wire requests using the
existing native configuration checks and normalization. Its model theorem
identifies the result with `NativeSharedLookupConfig.rebuild`; successful
rebuilding derives native validity, preserves request length/order, source
slots, logical lengths, repetitions and semantic public tables. No Boolean
validation certificate is supplied to this operation.

`RebuiltLookupExecution.program` performs rebuilding before the existing
allocated native lookup entry point. Invalid configurations return an
explicit invalid outcome without allocation/verifier calls or oracle reads.
Successful execution derives the actual assembled context's rebuilt requests
and their validity, preserving the exact existing native verification log.
This is a logical constructor/entry-point adapter. Rust invocation/constructor
correspondence and physical constructor cost are not asserted by it. Existing
unrebuilt caller records have not silently acquired a validation premise;
results needing validated shapes explicitly use successful rebuilt execution.

`LookupValidatedPublicTable` proves that rectangular original rows are
exact finite raw tuples. The earlier width interpretation has no missing
entries on this domain. The native raw table compression equals the ordered
public tuple hashes. Successful native production supplies the nonzero r,
public pole exclusions and literal multiplicity-weighted public total.

`RebuiltJobPublicGeometry` derives the selected original job's rectangular
public rows, positive reciprocal domain and active-count characteristic
bound from the same rebuilt execution. Independently, `counts` and
`counts_vector` recover the exact multiplicity length and original request
ordinal association from actual native proof checking and prepared-job order.
The caller supplies neither a rectangular finite table nor a matched count
vector as a new certificate.

`RebuiltCallerLookupCoverage.nonmember_covered` reduces nonmembership of an
original complete decoded source tuple to one of three events on that same
job: the existing native arithmetic work witness, the compression miss at
the literal produced y, or a missing hashed source whose nonzero reciprocal
numerator vanishes at the literal produced r. Its nonpassing branch derives
all original row/count associations needed by `ofNonpassing`; its reciprocal
branch derives numerator nonzeroness from the original configuration's
characteristic guard and root evaluation from actual native production.
Compression and reciprocal miss probabilities still need their remaining
adaptive lifetime work composition before full lookup soundness is claimed.

`LookupRequestPayloadSize` bounds the sum of validated per-request
compression complexities by the exact serialized request-vector payload.
Each raw usize word consumes at least one byte; variable bincode headers and
raw representatives are retained, without a fixed eight-byte word assumption.
`LookupParentPayloadBound` places that payload inside the original parsed
parent's actual request frame and bounds selected original complexity by
the parent input length. `rebuilt_candidate` and `rebuilt_kernel_bound`
discharge validation from actual rebuilt execution, yielding the refined
compression bound `parent.input.length / q^3` for that candidate. This is a
size/charging interface, not yet an amortized work theorem over repetitions,
positions, reused parents or every input/job class.

stream key's byte length pays the complete degree bound at rate `2^-132`.

original first-read position by a score selected from the original prefix:
`selectedKeyBytes * 2^-132`. An empty selecting fiber pays zero, as do stopped
or already-exposed streams. There is no union over input, job or degree
classes and no use of a later successful-read normalization.

lifetime probability bound. Its total charge is exactly the existing
first-read byte potential times the rate. `ScalarLogWork.program_bytes` and

specified interpreter's actual instruction work counter; log length is not
defined to be attacker work. Arbitrary earlier partial/far-offset prequeries,
rejected native offsets, source/query order and suspension remain covered.

original private-coin measures and every instruction horizon without a query,

The separate `bound` retains one explicit lifetime reference-bad probability.
This closes reciprocal first-read-position charging in the specified model;
it does not identify interpreter work with physical attacker work.

and original tuple nonmembership to this lifetime event, preserving existing

`PrivateCoinLookupChallengeProbability` combines arithmetic scalar/equality
and reciprocal safe events with summed work rates under one excluded global
reference ledger. PCS, compression and whole application output enforcement
remain separate obligations.
